articleTitle: Development of Switchable Linear-to-Circular Polarizer Using Reflective Electromagnetic Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper deals with the development of a simple structure of Reflective Electromagnetic Surface (RES) which is switchable as a regular reflector or as a linear-to-circular polarizer. In the off-state condition, RES can convert linear incident waves into circular reflected waves by utilizing a rectangular diagonal slot in the center of square patch. While in the on-state condition, it maintains linear polarization for both incident and reflected waves. Investigations on co-polarization and cross-polarization reflection coefficients, both in magnitude and phase, as well as the axial ratio from the simulation results, demonstrate these two functions in both states. The good agreement between measurement and simulation further validates the performance of switchable linear-to-circular polarizer at the frequency of 3.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Channel Impulse Response Correlation in the Application of Dynamic Channel Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper analyzed channel impulse response (CIR) correlation in a dynamic channel characterization. Two measurement scenarios in a corridor have been performed, i.e., line of sight (LOS) and non-line of sight (NLOS). The correlation was calculated based on the CIR of two sequential positions. The result shows that the correlation is significant.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of Patch Antenna Incorporated by Magnetized Yttrium Iron Garnet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Due to its superiority in performance at microwave frequencies, Yttrium Iron Garnet (YIG) has been frequently used to enhance the performance of radio frequency (RF) devices. This study investigates the feasibility of YIG ferrite incorporation within the host dielectric substrate to miniaturize the size of patch antennas. The proposed magneto-dielectric patch antenna is designed and fabricated on multi-layer Rogers RO4003C dielectric substrates, with the total thickness of 1.61 mm. The measurement results, including the resonant frequency response and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> parameter, are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Focal Region Ray Tracing for Spherical Reflector with Shaped Sub-Reflector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: 5G mobile communication system and beyond require antennas with multi-beam radiation patterns feature at the base station. Spherical reflector is regarded as a promising candidate due to its perfect symmetrical configuration. This study expands upon previous research on dual reflector antennas, comprising a main spherical reflector with an attached shaped sub-reflector based on constant path length principle. By employing the established shaping method of sub-reflector, focal region ray tracing is developed adhering to the law of reflection. The ray tracing is conducted in MATLAB and later validated by Electromagnetic (EM) simulation in FEKO.

articleTitle: Surface Wave Suppression at a Seawater Tank
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the case of radio wave propagation measurement using a seawater tank, large surface wave produced at the tank wall will limit the measurement area. In order to reduce the surface wave, to attach some structure on the tank wall may be expected. In this paper, small pyramidal structure, metal plate and wire mesh attachment are investigated through electromagnetic simulations. It is concluded that both metal plate and wire mesh structures can effectively reduce the surface wave more than 20dB.

articleTitle: Integrated Planar Array with Butler Matrix for Beam-Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an integrated configuration between a planar array and a Butler matrix for beam-steering applications. The integrated planar array comprises square patch antennas in 2×2 arrangement. To achieve a compact design, a miniaturized 4×4 Butler matrix based on meander-line techniques is adopted, whereby the Butler matrix and planar array boards are then integrated in a stacked manner. The overall dimensions of board integration are 72.3 mm×122.2 mm×25.8 mm. The measurement and simulation results show that the proposed configuration has the beam-steering of ±20° and ±30° at the frequency of 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Sectoral Antenna Array Fed by Proximity-Coupled Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study proposes improving the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of a wideband circularly polarized sectoral antenna array by utilizing proximity-coupled method for the array excitation. The utilization of proximity-coupled feeding is intended to satisfy the necessary of 3 dB AR bandwidth mostly required in wireless communications. This sectoral antenna array is designed on two layers of FR-4 Epoxy substrates to achieve a broader impedance bandwidth for both Right-Hand Circular Polarization (RHCP) and Left-Hand Circular Polarization (LHCP) modes. The characterization results show an improved AR bandwidth using the proposed configuration, whereby the 3 dB AR bandwidth is achieved by the sectoral antenna array in RHCP mode, yielding the achievement of 220 MHz. While in LHCP mode, the sectoral antenna array achieves the 3 dB AR bandwidth of 130 MHz.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Glass Metasurface Using Commercialized 5G mmWave Small Cell and Phone
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a transparent metasurface using a glass substrate and mesh patterns. The metasurface was designed to steer electromagnetic wave of 5G mmWave band centered at 28GHz. Gen2 size glass (370 mm x 470 mm) was applied to the fabrication process to increase the signal received on the metasurface and to deploy enough unit cells on it to control the direction of the reflection signal. The fabricated metasurface makes 60° beam-tilt, from a 60° incident wave to a 0° reflection wave. The signal improvement by steered reflection from the metasurface was verified in a real office environment in conjunction with commercialized radio devices such as a Corning mmWave 5G small cell and a Samsung smart phone. The test results show signal enhancement of maximum 20 dB in a weak signal area, and they show coverage expansion by the metasurface.

articleTitle: Design of a Multi-Channel Full-Polarimetric SFCW GPR Experimental System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This manuscript describes the design and preliminary tests of an experimental full-polarimetric multistatic GPR system. The requirements of such a system seem more adapted to frequency modulation instead of time domain, that is prevalent for these radar sensors. The operational bandwidth of the sensor lies between 0.4 GHz and 6 GHz, defining this sensor as ultrawideband. From the design a maximum of 144 measurement channels can be achieved using 6 dual-polarimetric antennas with a total of 12-physical ports. The system was thought as a modular concept; therefore, all components are flexible for being used in different configurations.

articleTitle: Independent control of Spatial Wavefront of Beam Scanning Antenna with Transmissive Phase Gradient Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To control and shape the spatial wavefront of reconfigurable leaky-wave antenna (LWA) by integrating a single layered transmissive phase gradient metasurface (TPGMS) is demonstrated. The amplitude and phase of transmission is controlled with single layer sub-wavelength design of TPGMS, where phase modulation is achieved through the geometrical manipulation of the unitcell structure. The proposed unique design of metasurface has advantage of transmission phase tunability and stability for polarization insensitive waves at different angle of incidence. The numerical simulation of the proposed integrated model shows the full control of the scanning beam from 22° to 48° at 5GHz for sub-6GHz applications.

articleTitle: Double-crossed Bowtie Antenna-coupled Carbon Nanotube Microbolometer with Meander Structures at 1THz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A high reception of THz waves is important in the design of an antenna-coupled microbolometer, which is indicated by the ability to detect THz waves effectively from all directions. In this study, we implement the meander line structure in a carbon nanotube (CNT) based bolometer coupled with a double-crossed bowtie antenna. The structure is designed on a SiO2 substrate with an additional metal reflector at the bottom. The simulation results reveal the potential high responsivity of 281.5 kV/W and could effectively minimize the NEP down to 0.0145 pW/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>. These results demonstrate the prospect of a meander line bolometer structure to enhance THz wave absorption with great potential in the application of real-time imaging.

articleTitle: Coherent Bandwidth and Distance in an Ultra-Large-Scale Antenna Array at 15 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study presents a measurement campaign with an ultra-large-scale antenna array in both Line-of-Sight (LoS) and Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) outdoor scenarios. Measurements were conducted at a center frequency of 15 GHz with a bandwidth of 4 GHz. A virtual 40×40 planar antenna array, formed by moving a vertically-polarized bi-conical omni-directional antenna (ODA) along regularly spaced grids, was employed at the receiver (Rx). The transmitter (Tx) utilized a single ODA. The variations of coherent bandwidth and coherent distance along the array are investigated. The results are important for generating realistic channel realizations for the design and performance evaluation of communications with large-scale arrays.

articleTitle: FMCW Monopulse Radar with an Orthogonally Polarized Dual-Beam Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar system using dielectric resonator antenna (DRA), which has two beams with orthogonal linear polarization to each other, is introduced to function as a monopulse radar. The DRA operates at 24.3 GHz with a 16.8% bandwidth and provides over 40 dB isolation between V-pol and H-pol ports. Simulations demonstrate effective target detection and advanced directional information extraction, similar to monopulse radar, using a signal processing technique to address overlapping beam regions.

articleTitle: Development and Mission Objectives of KOMPSAT-6 and Next Advanced SAR Satellite System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper outlines the development and mission objectives of Korea's SAR satellite systems, KOMPSAT-6 and the next advanced SAR satellite system. KOMPSAT-6 will provide high-resolution SAR images for national applications in GIS, land and ocean management, and disaster monitoring. The next advanced SAR satellite system will incorporate advanced technologies such as High-Resolution Wide Swath (HRWS), Digital Beam Forming (DBF), multi-static configurations, and multi-polarization. The system will include one primary satellite and multiple companion satellites for enhanced capabilities. Early development and localization of key technologies are emphasized to ensure timely and independent advancement, aiming to adhere to development schedules and minimize technological risks.

articleTitle: A Voltage-Controlled Oscillator with Dual-Band Structure in 0.18-µm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) with dual-band structure in 0.18-µm CMOS technology is proposed in this paper. By adopting a fourth-order LC-type resonant mechanism, the proposed CMOS VCO could generate frequency band 1 and band 2 for wireless dual-band direct-conversion receiver (DCR) applications. The proposed VCO uses only one control voltage to achieve dual-band function and to reduce frequency control procedure. The measured output frequencies are 1.14 GHz for the frequency band 1 at control voltage of 0 V and 3 GHz for the frequency band 2 at control voltage of 1.7 V, respectively. For the frequency band 1 at 1.14 GHz and frequency band 2 at 3 GHz, the measured phase noise of -100.3 dBc/Hz and -107.42 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz frequency offsets, respectively. The proposed dual-band CMOS VCO core consumes 10.5 mW at 1.7 V supply.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Phased Array Antenna for Electronic Warfare in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a linear phased array antenna which is built in fixed-wing of unmanned aerial vehicle. The proposed antenna covers over 3 octaves bandwidth for electronic warfare system with azimuth beam steering. It is possible to receive the signal from threat for direction finding and to transmit the high power jamming signal toward a found threat within beam steering.

articleTitle: Phase-Retrieval Method Using Wire-Grid Model in Spherical Near-Field OTA Test
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a method to estimate the far-field using two spherical wire-grid models in a phase-less spherical near-field. From the simulation results for monopole, 1-patch, and 4-patch antenna, it was confirmed that the EIRP can be estimated within 1 dB at more than 100 sampling points.

articleTitle: Development of CPW Fed Patch Antenna for Ground Penetrating Radar Application using APAST Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: GPR is a non-destructive geophysical method used to detect subsurface structures, and its effectiveness depends on the antenna design whereby this research introduces a Rectangular CPW Fed Patch Antenna for GPR, with sensing capabilities up to 0.5m depth at 800MHz. The antenna, made with Rogers RO4003C substrate (228x304x0.81 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>), achieves -32.56dB of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, 4.78dBi of realized gain, 90% of radiation efficiency, 1.048:1 of VSWR and optimized by APAST.

articleTitle: Medical Bandages Characterization as Potential Substrate for a Wearable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper presented the effect of different medical bandage materials that are commercially available in medical industry as the antennas’ substrate. Simulated S11 have shown noticeable deviation on the return loss due to different types of flexible substrate materials. Different types of medical bandage materials are characterized in terms of permittivity and loss tangent using open-ended coaxial probe method. Results have shown significant variation as low as 17% on the dielectric properties due to different types of medical bandage materials. The presented work may give an insight for the development of wearable telemedicine devices and application.

articleTitle: Integration of GAT and GCN for WiFi Positioning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel algorithm that combines graph attention network (GAT) with graph convolutional network (GCN), both of which are types of graph neural networks (GNNs). GNNs have gained attention for their ability to overcome the non-line-of-sight (NLoS) bias in WiFi positioning by efficiently extracting local features from graphs. Existing GNN-based algorithms often rely on GCNs due to their low computational complexity. Our empirical experiments demonstrate that the proposed technique reduces RMSE by 8.6% and 21.0% for self-supervised and semi-supervised learning, respectively, compared to using GCN alone.

articleTitle: Topological Insulators Supporting Surface Plasmons
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We investigate the plasmonic phenomena in a topological insulator, Bismuth Selenide (Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) in the terahertz frequency region. By mapping the dielectric function using a Lorentzian oscillator, we show that the Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> displays a resonance of 1.9 THz. Additionally, the chosen material exhibits plasmonic phenomena in the frequency range of 2-6 THz, as evidenced by the negative real part of the permittivity. These characteristics highlight the material’s potential for manipulating electromagnetic waves at terahertz frequencies. Notably, several biological materials, particularly protein structures, have resonances within this frequency range, which indicates suitability in developing highly sensitive terahertz fingerprinting systems.

articleTitle: SAR Assessment of a Dual-Band Wearable Antenna for WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work investigates the SAR analysis of a compact dual-band wearable antenna designed for WBAN applications. The antenna utilizes Rogers Duroid RO3003<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> substrate material, which has compact dimensions measuring 32 × 30 × 0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. It achieves a bandwidth percentage of 4.4% at 2.4 GHz and 5.1% at 5.8 GHz. The antenna exhibits bidirectional and directional radiation patterns in the E-plane, while omnidirectional patterns are observed in the H-plane. SAR levels at both 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz conform to FCC and ICNIRP regulations, making this antenna a compelling choice for WBAN applications.

articleTitle: A multibeam circularly polarized antenna array based on miniaturized Butler matrix network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized microstrip antenna array based on a beamforming network is designed. The beamforming network is a miniaturized 4×4 microstrip Butler matrix. The antenna array operates at 2.41~2.47GHz with S11<-10dB. Gain of the antenna array is greater than 8.7dB which axial ratio is less than 3 dB in the width of the main lobe. The antenna array can form four beams with about 40° spacing in a plane.

articleTitle: Aircraft Radio Altimeter Interference Path Loss Evaluations of Small-Sized Fixed-Wing Aircraft During Flight
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Radio altimeter interference path loss (IPL) characteristics of the Beechcraft B300 aircraft during flight have been measured and evaluated. Although RTCA DO-307B/EUROCAE ED-239A specifies IPL evaluation when the aircraft is on the ground, this study obtains IPL characteristics during flight and compares the differences. Measurements are taken at 31 locations inside the cabin, assuming the presence of 5G mobile communication devices and Wireless Avionics Intra-Communication devices. The minimum IPL values during flight and on the ground were 51.9 dB and 60.0 dB, respectively. In addition, it is confirmed that the minimum IPL values are always higher during flight than on the ground.

articleTitle: Robust Transmitting Coil Design for Wireless Power Transfer System to Mitigate Input Voltage Variations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a robust transmitting coil design for maintaining consistent output power across various airgap conditions. The system operates in three modes based on different configurations of transmitting coil connections, adjusting the inductance accordingly. Simulation results indicate that by changing modes as coupling coefficient varies, the system can consistently deliver 200 W to the load with a constant input voltage of around 27 V and current of 15 A. This method can provide stable power over a wide range of airgaps without the need for a DC/DC converter, reducing cost, loss, and size.

articleTitle: Numerical Modelling for the Evaluation of Dispersion Properties for Hexagonal Lattice Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, we present a multimodal transfer matrix method for obtaining the eigensolutions in the complete irreducible Brillouin zone for hexagonal lattices. The method is compared in terms of accuracy and speed to a commercial software and to a method-of-moments implementation, and is found to be as accurate but faster.

articleTitle: Plasma Diagnostics Based on Miniaturized FSS with Angular Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) for plasma diagnostics is presented in this paper. The detection system consists of metallic patches and supporting slabs. The metallic patches with circle slots provide a passband at a specific frequency, which is the signal of operation states. Two slabs are arranged symmetrically, which are separated by air space. The FSS is transparent at nearly 4.8 GHz. Considering the threshold of 1dB of the transmission coefficient, the sharing passband of TE and TM polarizations is from 4.59 to 5.27 GHz when the incident angle gradually increases to 60°. The plasma diagnostic system operates when the space is infused with plasma. The plasma inside the FSS absorbs the incident wave. By installing this FSS on the detection window, the existence of the plasma is quickly detected.

articleTitle: Highly Selective and Miniaturized Filtering Antenna Based on a Modified Substrate Integrated Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a highly selective and miniaturized filtering antenna based on a modified substrate integrated cavity (SIC). To achieve the desired performance, a center via and multiple slots are introduced into the conventional rectangular SIC. The proposed filtering antenna demonstrates three resonance points within the desired frequency range. Two of these resonance points are provided by gap-coupled patch resonators, while the third one is achieved through a center via-loaded circular patch resonator. Additionally, this design generates two radiation nulls (RNs). The RN in the upper stopband is achieved by the radiation of left side grounded patch resonator, while the RN in the lower stopband is achieved through cross-coupling between the two grounded patches on the both sides of the SIC. A prototype is designed and simulated. The results show good filtering function and radiation performance.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Frequency- and Mode-Reconfigurable Flexible Textile Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-band flexible textile antenna with reconfigurability in both frequency and operation mode is presented. The antenna is designed to switch between broadside and omnidirectional modes centered at 2.45 GHz and 3.50 GHz, respectively. Importantly, frequency reconfigurability is introduced in both radiation modes, namely tuning from 1.92 to 2.58 GHz for the lower band and from 3.26 to 4.10 GHz for the higher band. An antenna prototype is manufactured and measured to validate the reconfigurable multi-mode operating concept.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band Low-Noise Amplifier MMIC Using 0.15-µm GaN HEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper shows the results of designing and fabricating a Ku-band low-noise amplifier (LNA) MMIC using ETRI’s 0.15-μm AlGaN/GaN HEMT (High Electron Mobility Transistor) on a SiC substrate. In order to enhance the noise figure and gain of the LNA, the sources of GaN HEMT devices were connected to ground using microstrip lines acting as inductors. The measured results of the designed and manufactured Ku-band LNA were presented a 3-dB bandwidth of 3.5 GHz, a gain (S21) of 30~33 dB, an input matching (S11) of -7~-3 dB, an output matching (S22) of -19~-4 dB, and an isolation (S12) of -67~-59 dB at frequencies of 16.5~20.0 GHz. The characteristics of the noise figure of the LNA were measured at 1.7~2.3 dB in the same frequency range. And the measured results of the Ku-band LNA shows a small-signal gain (S21) of 25~33 dB, an input matching (S11) of -5~-2 dB, an output matching (S22) of -5~-3 dB, and an isolation (S12) of -67~-60 dB at frequencies of 15.7~17.2 GHz. The noise figures of the LNA were measured at 1.7~2.3 dB in the same frequency range. The chip size is 2.3 mm x 1.2 mm including the input/output pads and the DC input pads.

articleTitle: Dielectric Fan Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a dielectric fan antenna that has a high gain beam-steering capability. A four-patch array is used for the exciter for this antenna. The radiation beam achieves a high gain of more than 19 dBi across an angle range of 64°. The proposed antenna achieves a higher gain of more than 10 dB, compared to the gain of the exciter.

articleTitle: Design of Quasi-optical Path and Analysis Focusing Characteristics for 220GHz Millimeter-wave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper mainly studies the quasi-optical path design of 220GHz millimeter wave imaging system and the radiation characteristics of offset feed elliptical reflector antenna. For the elliptical reflector antenna, the radiation characteristics of the feed at the focus are better and the resolution is higher. When the bias angle becomes larger, the focal spot gradually deteriorates and the resolution decreases.

articleTitle: A Balanced-to-Single-Ended Filtering Unequal Power Divider Using Isosceles Right-Angled Triangular Patch Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a balanced-to-single-ended unequal power divider with a bandpass response and a power division ratio of 2:1. Isosceles right-angled triangular patches are used as resonators. To convert balance to single-ended operation, a balanced input port and two single-ended output ports are employed. The unequal power divider was designed based on the theory of coupled resonators to achieve a second-order bandpass response. A prototype has been developed. It operates at 3.5 GHz with a bandwidth of 6%. At the central frequency, the differential-mode input return loss is better than 20 dB, and the differential-to-single-ended insertion losses are 3.84 dB and 6.96 dB. Isolation between output ports is larger than 20 dB. 20-dB common-mode suppression in the passband is also achieved.

articleTitle: Horn Antenna With a Paraboloid Reflector for 24 GHz Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a pyramidal high-gain horn antenna with a paraboloid reflector operating at 24 GHz specifically for Foreign Object Debris (FOD) radar applications. The proposed design incorporates a paraboloid reflector to enhance the gain and radiation characteristics. Simulations demonstrate that the modified horn antenna achieves a gain of 27.21 dBi, a bandwidth of 2000 MHz, and a sidelobe level (SLL) of −19 dB. These results show the potential of this design for FOD radar applications.

articleTitle: Design of 2×2 Interpolating-Fed 5×5-Element Phased Array Antenna-in-Package in 300-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 5×5 two-dimensional phased array was designed in 300-GHz band. Only 2×2 elements are fed from the feeding lines. Interpolating elements are located between the fed elements and surrounding the fed elements. The interpolating elements are excited through coupling circuits from adjacent elements. Although the fed elements are only 2×2 in a 5×5-arrangement, grating lobes are suppressed and the effective aperture is extended by surrounding elements. Thus, the directivity increases. The effect of the proposed technique on the phased array was confirmed by simulation in this work.

articleTitle: Moving target detection from the roadside by millimeter-wave radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, we investigate a traffic monitoring method to detect passing cars, bikes, and humans from roadsides using millimeter-wave radar during road work. Because a road worker is one of the most dangerous occupations, the number of people trying to get this type of job is decreasing. To give a safety work condition and reduce road accidents with respect to the road works, a millimeter-wave radar is one of the candidates for infrastructure sensors that can be expected to offer robust detection performance regardless of the surrounding environment. Then, we applied millimeter-wave radar to traffic monitoring during road work. We examine that the radar detects passing cars, bikes, and humans, and estimates their direction with two corner reflectors from the roadside. These experiments were carried out, and the results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: CNN-Based Radar Image Enhancement for Estimating Human-Body’s Silhouette
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN) based radar image enhancement technique for human-body detection. A millimeter-wave radar with multiple antennas observes the reflected waves from the human-body, and generates a spectral image, which is input to the trained CNN to generate a sharpened image. The numerical analysis resulted in a 0.93 2D correlation coefficient and 0.02 error rate in comparison with the original images, and this result showed that the proposed method could well reconstruct the image of human-body’s silhouette.

articleTitle: A Multi-Stage Matching Rectifier with Wide Input Power Range for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Due to the unpredictable wireless power transfer (WPT) path losses and the unknown location of RF sources, the received RF power is distributed with unknown power levels in WPT scenarios. Therefore, RF rectifiers should obtain high efficiencies within a wide input power range. This paper proposes an efficient rectifier topology with a wide input power range. The proposed rectifier topology uses the multi-stage matching method and consists of two parallel rectifier arrays to provide two different DC paths for low and high input power levels, respectively. For validation, a wide input power range rectifier has been designed, fabricated, and measured. It maintains an efficiency of over 50% at 2.52 GHz over an input range from 4 to 30.5 dBm.

articleTitle: Impact of Electric Field Coupling on High- frequency Magnetic Probe Calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the impact of electric field coupling on the calibration of magnetic probes at high frequencies is presented. Electric field coupling to magnetic probes increases at high-frequency regions, leading to distorted calibration results due to errors in the probe factor. The impact of electric field coupling has been demonstrated through 3-dimensional electromagnetic field simulation results on a reference microstrip structure.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Unit Cell Arrangement of Reflectarray Antenna with Independent Control of Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new unit cell arrangement structure for reflectarray antenna is proposed to independently control the beams of horizontal and vertical polarizations. By leveraging polarization orthogonality, unit cells reflecting horizontal and vertical polarization are arranged alternately. Simulated results show a gain of 16 dB in the 40-degree direction at 29.3 GHz with an array size of 9 λ×9 λ. This result suggested that horizontal and vertical polarizations can be independently controlled using a simple structure. This structure can optimize the communication channels by accounting for difference in reflections from surrounding structures through the polarization MIMO function.

articleTitle: Reflective Metasurface on Different Position of Fractal Koch Shape
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the comparison of inward and outward of a fractal shape performance at X-band frequency for Reflecting Intelligent Surface (RIS). The proposed initial reflector is using a square shape and modified with the fractal of inward and outward on the substrate of Rogers RT5880 with a thickness of 0.51mm. The simulated result is shown in the S-parameter graph and the reflection phase. The bandwidth of the proposed reflector is calculated based on the reflection phase results. From the simulation results, the reflector with an inward fractal shape position has a wider bandwidth compare with the outward fractal substrate.

articleTitle: All-Metal Share-Aperture High-Isolation Millimeter-Wave End-Fire and Broadside Phased Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a shared aperture antenna capable of achieving end-fire and broadside phased array beam coverage. The antenna uses an all-metal slot structure and is designed for the millimeter-wave band. Designed within a metal cavity, it achieves independent beam control. The top broadside antenna and the end-fire antennas share a common metal aperture. To reduce mutual coupling between the end-fire and side-fire antennas, orthogonal electromagnetic fields within the cavity ensure high isolation between different antenna ports. Without adding extra structures, the simulated isolation reaches below -50 dB. A 1×4 phased antenna array is designed, achieving 11.8 dBi gain in the broadside direction and 13.4 dBi gain in the end-fire direction while ensuring high isolation. This provides a solution for high-power capacity millimeter-wave base stations.

articleTitle: A Front-end Readout Sensor with a DC offset Cancellation for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a front-end readout sensor for biomedical applications. An analog receiving circuit processes the baseband signals, which are fabricated by the UMC 180nm CMOS process, operating at a voltage of 1.8V. A 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order complementary source follower low-pass filter is proposed and designed to reject the unwanted out-of-band interferences. Moreover, a DC offset cancelling mechanism is incorporated into the receiving sensor to avoid signal saturation in the following stages.

articleTitle: The Optimal Sample Region Required to Predict Monostatic RCS from Finite Near-Field Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: During near-field measurements, truncating the sampled angular domain can cause "spectral leakage" in the spatial domain, leading to measurement errors in Radar Cross Section (RCS). In this paper, we apply triangular window weighting to the sampled scattering field. By modifying the sampling region and observing the variations in errors, the optimal sampling region can be determined. Simulation results show that the weighting method significantly reduces error oscillation and facilitates the fast and effective identification of the optimal sampling region. Importantly, the measurement accuracy of RCS is not dependent on expanding the sampling region. The accuracy of the sampling region is influenced by the scattering characteristics of the target. Thus, calculating and analyzing the optimal sampling region for a specific target can provide a solid theoretical basis for practical measurements.

articleTitle: Programmable Space-Time Metamaterial Antenna-Receiver: Applications and Advancements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents two primary applications of a space-time-modulated metamaterial (ST-MTM) receiving antenna. The first application utilizes the antenna to extract information from multiple users transmitting distinct data on a shared carrier frequency. The second application involves estimating the direction of arrival (DOA) of an incoming signal.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Metal and Surface Roughness Losses in 1-D Periodic Structures Using the Multimodal Transfer Matrix Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We discuss the application of the multimodal transfer matrix approach (MMTMA) to evaluate metal and surface roughness losses in one-dimensional periodic structures. To this aim, we analyze the dispersion characteristics of a parallel plate waveguide periodically loaded with chamfered glide-symmetric corrugations. The metal and surface roughness losses are included and accurately evaluated. Furthermore, the attenuation in the stopband region, which cannot be calculated with the eigensolver of commercial software, is also retrieved with the MMTMA. The advantages of MMTMA with respect to a first-order perturbation method are discussed.

articleTitle: Proposal on Radio Propagation Prediction System Using Quantum Annealers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: At present, ray tracing method is commonly used for radio propagation analysis, but calculation time (/amount of calculation) increases to improve analysis precision. Therefore, we have proposed propagation path model (P-QUBO model) for path search which is applicable to quantum annealer. In this paper, the concept of our developed radio propagation prediction system based on P-QUBO model is explained and performance of our system in urban environment are clarified.

articleTitle: Near-Field WPT for Sustainable Wireless Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In our rapidly digitizing society, the increasing number of wireless nodes per square kilometer presents significant sustainability challenges. Wireless power technologies (WPT) provide hope by enabling wireless power delivery to these nodes, reducing the need for wires and batteries. This paper overviews near-field WPT for wireless devices and addresses existing research challenges.

articleTitle: Utilization of ABS Material for In-Band Full-Duplex Antenna Implementation Using 3D Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the use of additive manufacturing technique is highlighted for developing radio frequency (RF) and microwave devices. The potential of utilizing lightweight materials such as Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) material using a three-dimensional (3D) printing technology is focused to In-Band Full Duplex (IBFD) antenna implementation. A three-port microstrip antenna with a 180° hybrid ring coupler is employed to mitigate self-interference arising from concurrent transmission and reception on the same frequency. Copper paint is used as a coating material to cover the conductive elements of antenna. Both simulation and measurement confirm that the proposed IBFD antenna meets the design specifications and performs efficiently at the frequency of 2.4 GHz. The results shows that the realized IBFD antenna can maintain stable performance and achieve high isolation up to 47 dB, demonstrating the effectiveness of approaching technique in modern communication systems.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Angular Scattering Characteristics of the Human Body Using Millimeter-wave 2D-MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper provides experimental results of angular scattering characteristics of human body and imaging results of the walking human observed by millimeter-wave MIMO radar. The angular scattering characteristics of the human body confirmed that the response of the legs was greater when irradiated to a sideways human body than when irradiated from the front. Therefore, imaging of the human body crossing the front of the radar confirmed not only the response of the torso, but also the arms and legs, successfully projecting the contours of the human body. Thus, it is important to observe the human body from multiple angels to obtain a clear image of each part of the human body in millimeter-wave radar.

articleTitle: Efficient Computation of Large Sea Surfaces For Simulating Synthetic Aperture Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a rapid and memory-efficient technique for generating sizable, dynamic sea surfaces in synthetic aperture radar system simulations. Our method significantly reduces runtime and memory consumption by leveraging the sea spectrum decomposition and eliminating data redundancy inherent in simulated systems.

articleTitle: Design Results of a Wideband Active Electrically Scanned Array(AESA) Antenna for X-band Satellite Synthetic Aperture Radar(SAR) Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a wideband Active Electronically Scanned Array(AESA) antenna for X-band satellite Synthetic Aperture Radar(SAR) applications. The proposed antenna incorporates a wideband beam steering capability achieved through the addition of one True Time Delay Line(TDL) to each of the 0-channel Transmit/Receive(TR) modules, in addition to phase shifters. Furthermore, to form dual linear polarization, a V-polarized radiator(a slotted waveguide type) and an H-polarized radiator(a stepped notch type) are alternately arranged. To validate our design, the antenna was fabricated and verified through near-field measurements. To conclude, our proposed antenna demonstrates the capability to form dual polarization and steer beam in the same direction within the bandwidth of about 00%.

articleTitle: A High-Density Array Antenna Using Narrow Elements for High-Power Rectenna DC Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-density array antenna utilizing narrow antenna elements to achieve high-power rectenna DC arrays. A microstrip antenna employing a narrow antenna element has a lower gain than conventional microstrip antennas with a square patch. However, the narrow element allows us to arrange more elements in a unit area. As a result, the overall performance of the array antenna can be improved even though the performance of each element degrades. In this study, aperture ratios of the proposed array antenna and conventional array antenna using square elements are compared by simulation. Furthermore, a 9-element array antenna prototype is fabricated and experimentally evaluated. The aperture ratio of the proposed array antenna is improved by 20% compared to that of the conventional ones.

articleTitle: Analysis of Polarimetric Scattering Properties for Multiclass Change Discrimination
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Change detection is one of the important topics in the application of remote sensing. It is essential to identify various changes to enhance the practicality of remote sensing. Recently, polarimetric SAR data that provide additional observations can be an effective tool for multiclass change detection, classifying various land cover changes. Therefore, this study analyzed the polarimetric scattering properties to propose method for discriminating multiclass changes.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of QRM-MLD on OAM-MIMO
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study investigates the system throughput of orbital angular momentum (OAM) multiplexing by employing multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) using QR decomposition and M-algorithm maximum likelihood detection (QRM-MLD). The lower computational complexity of QRM-MLD makes it more effective than traditional MLD by reducing the number of searched paths. Unlike previous research, which has been limited to analyzing the Shannon capacity at a given signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), this work incorporates actual signal processing to effectively address the performance gap of the Shannon limit. Moreover, the effectiveness of QRM-MLD in OAM-MIMO is verified through computer simulations by comparing its performance with that of the traditional MLD-based approach.

Author Keywords: QR decomposition and M-algorithm maximum likelihood detection (QRM-MLD)

articleTitle: End-to-End System Evaluation of an Orbital Angular Momentum Modes Multiplexing Communication System for B5G/6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a new workflow that offers complete end-to-end system simulation of an Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) modes multiplexing communication system. By combining Ansys high fidelity electromagnetic solvers and MATLAB script, we can accurately predict the communication system performance while considering all the realistic factors that could deteriorate the system performance. This workflow enables early design & optimization of system at component level, hence allows "shift-left" in the product development cycle for next generation communication system.

articleTitle: A Comparative Simulation Study of the Optimal Electrode for Through-The-Earth Communication Using Earth-Grounded Antennas at 350 kHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study investigates Through-The-Earth (TTE) communication using electrodes operating at a frequency of 350 kHz in the Medium Frequency (MF) band. These electrodes, situated at the end of the wire of an earth-grounded antenna, facilitate signal transmission between the Earth's surface and subterranean regions by inducing electric currents. The simulation study evaluates the impact of electrode types—specifically Y-shape, X-shape, and V-shape, commonly encountered—on parameters such as transmission coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>), surface current, and impedance. CST software is employed to analyze these effects and identify the most suitable electrode shape for use with the earth-grounded antenna. Analysis of simulation results shows that the X-shape electrode exhibits superior performance, displaying the highest S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> and surface current while exhibiting the lowest real impedance compared to other shapes. Because the X-shape electrode has a higher contact area than all other electrodes, it results in a low contact impedance value. As a result, the X-shape electrode appears as the optimal choice for integration with the earth-grounded antenna, particularly in Through-The-Earth communication applications.

articleTitle: An Effect of Time Reversal Based Multiple Beacon Selection on Wireless Power Transfer Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of multiple beacon (multi-beacon) systems in Wireless Power Transfer (WPT), focusing on improving overall RF-DC efficiency. Through simulations within a 5.64 GHz scenario, limiting a dynamic range of TXA element radiation power to a maximum of 20 dBm, and using a RXA rectifier within a specific range, multi-beacon configurations significantly enhanced RF-DC efficiency compared to single-beacon setups. The results showed that multi-beacon systems achieved 43.07% RF-DC efficiency and a RXA DC power of 1.20 W at a distance of 0.5 m, compared to 13.49% and 2.40 W with a single-beacon configuration, demonstrating the appropriateness of multi-beacon selection in our system design. On the other hand, trade-offs are evident: while multi-beacon systems bring high RF-DC efficiency, they also degrade absolute power and require high hardware complexity. This underscores the importance of adaptive beacon selection, taking into consideration the dynamic range specifications of both TXA and RXA.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna with Wideband Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study developed a small, low-profile magneto-electric dipole antenna with wideband characteristics by adding a capacitively loaded loop (CLL) structure and stubs. The proposed antenna consists of an electric dipole, a magnetic dipole, and a reflector. The folded reflector and bent electric dipole that constitute the antenna operate as a CLL at low frequencies, thereby substantially reducing the electrical size of the antenna. The rectangular stubs attached to the electric dipole compress the higher-order modes of the dipole, expanding the bandwidth of the antenna. The electrical size of the proposed antenna is 0.316 × 0.292 × 0.0389 $\lambda _{\text{L}}^3$, its –10 dB impedance bandwidth is 0.73 to 1.97 GHz (91.9%), and the gain achieved within the operating bandwidth is 4.3 to 6.7 dBi.

articleTitle: Slots Effect on CPW Pentagonal Patch Antenna for 3.5 GHz 5G and 5.9 GHz DSRC Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This research investigates the effects of two different slots on the CPW pentagonal patch antenna for 5G and Dedicated short-range communications (DSRC). Initially, first antenna design, Antenna A is pentagonal patch antenna with pentagonal slots while the second antenna design B is constructed by a pentagonal patch antenna with mini multiple slots structure. This Antenna A performs best at 3.32 GHz and 5.77 GHz with - 20.83 dB and - 49.56 dB, respectively. Besised that, the Antenna B perfoms at 3.50 GHz and 5.92 GHz with - 46.13 dB and - 20.09 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Vital Sign Detection in Sleep Using WiFi and High Directivity Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach for monitoring vital signs during sleep by utilizing a high directional antenna to capture the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) and Channel State Information (CSI) from 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi signals. The study conducted an evaluation experiment, analyzing data collected over a 2.5-hour period from three individuals in bed, and shows promising applications for smart home technology in the context of the IoT era.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Microstrip-Based Phase Inverter as a Phase Delay Component at 24 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized microstrip-based phase inverter (PI) operating from 23.05 to 25 GHz. The proposed miniaturized PI integrates interdigital capacitors and meander slots on the ground plane while utilizing only two metallic vias to achieve a compact size. The circuit area of the layout is only 24.4% when compared to the original microstrip-based PI and 32.4% when compared to the ordinary 180°-delay meander line. Simulated and measured results demonstrate an 8.13% usable bandwidth, 0.53-dB average insertion loss, and phase deviation within ± 10° from 23.05 to 25 GHz. This design offers promising size reduction and competitive performance for microwave circuit integration.

articleTitle: Multiband, Dual-Strip Biplanar Monopole for Internet of Things Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-strip monopole antenna printed on the two layers of the low-cost substrate for internet of things (IoT) applications is presented. The antenna design comprises one longer direct-fed strip on the front layer and one shorter coupled-fed strip on the back layer for compact layout. The longer strip can resonate a well-matched mode in the 2.4 GHz (2400-2500 MHz) band and at the same time, produce a higher-order resonance in the 6 GHz (5925-7125 MHz) band. In addition, the coupled shorter strip is able to produce another resonant mode in the 5 GHz (5150-5850 MHz) band. Together, these two monopole strips make it possible for the biplanar monopole to achieve multiband operation in the 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz bands. The antenna design is discussed, and the numerical results are presented.

articleTitle: Study of Radio Wave Propagation Characteristics in a Suburban Environment at 169 MHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study evaluates radio propagation in a suburban area in the 169 MHz band to enhance the frequency-efficient utilization of UAV communication. The research compares the received power from experiments with radio propagation simulations considering terrain. The results indicate strong agreement. Additionally, a comparison was made between the calculated results and measured data using the free-space propagation, two-ray model, and Okumura-Hata model by selecting a location with a good Line of Sight (LoS) environment. Future research will involve studies in various propagation environments.

articleTitle: Fixed-Frequency Beam-Scanning microstrip Leaky-wave Antenna for Ku-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Varactor tuned interdigital capacitor (IDC) slot loaded microstrip antenna for fixed-frequency beam scanning is proposed for Ku-band applications. Microstrip patch loaded with an IDC-slot and two shorting vias for forward-backward frequency scanning is designed. A pair of oppositely oriented varactor diode at the gap of IDC slot is studied at fixed-frequency. The main beam scan from +2° to +60° (58°) in the forward quadrant at 13.9GHz, by changing the diode states from 0.9-0.1pF with maximum gain of 9.2dB.

articleTitle: Path loss Measurements and Analysis in an Urban low-rise/Suburban Environment at 159 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reports on channel measurements conducted in an urban low-rise/suburban environment in the 159 GHz frequency band. Based on the measurement results and analysis, we investigate path loss characteristics according to distance by comparing them with widely used global standards such as ITU-R and 3GPP path loss models.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band Amplitude and Phase Controllable Transmitarray based on 3D-Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, 3D-printing technology is used to design a dielectric-only transmitarray (TA) at 38 GHz. The electric properties of the 3D printing material are first extracted by the Nicolson-Ross-Weir (NRW) method. The amplitude and phase control units are then developed separately. The amplitude unit is fulfilled by a laminated structure composed of alternatively air and dielectric layers to control the transmission coefficient upon incidence. Meanwhile, the phase unit is controlled by the connecting length between two linearly tapered cones. The proposed TA unit cell has a full 360° phase coverage while the transmission | | is smaller than -0.25 dB. A transmitarray with a diameter of 120.6 mm (13 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) is realized (1268 elements), the maximum gain at the center frequency of 38 GHz is 26.3 dBi, and the aperture efficiency is 23 %.

articleTitle: A Metasurface-based Dual Passband Filter with Sharp Rejection Band for Navigational Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a metasurface-based closely spaced dual passband filter in L-band. A sharp rejection feature has been introduced within the two passbands in the design. The proposed structure operates at 1221.2 MHz and 1572.2 MHz together with a rejection at 1396.7 MHz. The proposed structure is angularly stable in nature as well as polarization independent owing to the four-fold symmetry in the unit cell making it a potential candidate for radar navigational applications.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Time-Division Parallel FDTD Using Time-Reversal Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The FDTD method combined with a time-reversal technique is applied to time-division parallel computation. The time-domain response of electromagnetic field from dielectric cylinders is investigated and computational accuracy is verified. The proposed method enables faster computation.

articleTitle: Isolation Enhancement of Compact MIMO Transparent Antenna Using Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discussed the Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna with enhanced isolation. The conventional patched antenna is designed at 28 GHz and modified with metamaterial load. The use of circular split ring resonator (CSRR) based unit cell and complement on the ground give an advantage on further enhance the isolation between the elements. The antenna has been designed using transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) coated over a glass substrate and simulated using CST software. The performance of the antenna has been observed on the reflection and transmission coefficient. The transmission coefficient improved by 10 dB showing the enhancement of isolation between the elements. The S-parameters data has been used to calculate the MIMO parameters such as the directive gain (DG) and envelope correlation coefficient (ECC). The design achieved the MIMO standard with ECC ≤ 0.5 and DG ≥ 9.

articleTitle: Design of a circularly dual-polarized wideband microstrip antenna fed by two orthogonally-arranged L-probes and a hybrid coupler
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents design of a circularly dual-polarized wideband microstrip antenna (MSA) fed by two orthogonally-arranged L-probes and a hybrid coupler. In order to obtain wideband performance as well as circularly dual-polarized characteristics, the proposed antenna is composed of a single-layer dual-polarized wideband MSA with two orthogonally-arranged L-probes and a branch-line hybrid coupler placed on the backside of the ground plane. Firstly, the single-layer linearly dual-polarized wideband MSA fed by two L-probes and the hybrid coupler are designed at around 5 GHz separately. Then, reflection characteristics, port-to-port isolation characteristics, and radiation properties of the assembled circularly dual-polarized wideband MSA are obtained by the simulation with Mentor IE3D. Based on the simulated results, the dimensions of the assembled MSA are tuned again so as to realize wideband and circularly-polarized performance. Consequently, 18.8% fractional bandwidth of the proposed MSA with less than -10 dB reflection, more than 10 dB port-to-port isolation, and less than 3 dB axial ratio characteristics is obtained. Good wideband and circularly-polarized performance of the proposed antenna is confirmed by the simulation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Bending and Human Body Effects of Compact Full Flexible Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna for 3.5 GHz in 5G sub-6 GHz Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes human body effect and bending analysis of a fully flexible wearable antipodal Vivaldi antenna for 5G n77 and n78 bands with compact size of 33 × 33 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (length × width), resonating at 3.5 GHz. The flexible polyester substrate with a dielectric constant (ɛ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) of 1.34 and loss tangent (tan δ) of 0.005 has been used for the design. The antenna is bent in both x- and y- directions, with different angles. On-body analysis was performed on different body parts using homogeneous human model. The analysis was performed extensively using reflection coefficients of the studied antenna structure.

articleTitle: Power Scalability Modeling of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces for THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an attempt is made to model the total power requirements of a full scale Reflective Intelligent Surface (RIS) with switches(microfluidics based and CMOS based) operating at 140 GHz frequencies. First, we modeled the static powers associated with FPGA boards and its control boards of RIS and then estimated the dynamic power requirements associated with RIS based on different unit cell elements configurations and then the combined total power values for various configurations with 1-bit, 2-bit, and 3-bit (binary switching states) are presented.

articleTitle: Waveguide Slot Array Antenna for Near-field Heating of Underground Coal Seams
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a waveguide slot array antenna operating at 2.45 GHz for near-field heating of underground coal seams. The main body of the antenna adopts a three-segment stepped circular waveguide. The radiator adopts a slot pair array, and the unit is an orthogonal slot pair, which increases the radiation aperture and benefits the radial uniform radiation of electromagnetic waves. The inner conductor of the coaxial line extends a certain distance into the waveguide, ensuring that the TM01 mode is excited. The inner conductor adopts two-section stepped copper wires to achieve better impedance matching. To cope with high temperature and high pressure, a silicon nitride ceramic sheath is used to wrap the antenna. The simulation results show good radiation performance, and this type of antenna has bright prospects in scenarios such as coalbed methane mining.

articleTitle: Resonant frequency control of a varactor-loaded double-layer dual-band miniaturized microstrip antenna fed by an L-probe with straight shorted elements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents resonant frequency control of a varactor-loaded double-layer dual-band miniaturized microstrip antenna (MSA) fed by an L-probe with straight shorted elements. The proposed antenna consists of two miniaturized straight shorted patches with varactor diodes on the top layer and a feeding L-probe arranged on the bottom layer. Two resonant frequencies of the patches can be controlled by DC bias voltages applied for the varactors independently. In order to reduce the area occupied by the patches as well as to improve cross polarization radiated from the L-probe, the L-probe is arranged on the bottom layer of the double-layered dielectric substrate under the patches. The frequency-tunable performance as well as radiation properties of the proposed MSA are confirmed by the measurement.

articleTitle: Fundamental Study on Polarimetric Scattering For Change Detection in Flooded Built-up Area
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this research, a simple change detection method in flood-affected built-up area is proposed based on the eigenvalue/eigenvector analysis using quad polarimetric SAR data. Change of the angles between the eigenvectors before and after a flood event is considered as a detection indicator in the method. To verify the usefulness of the proposed method, polarimetric scattering analysis for a simplified built-up area model is carried out by using the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method. Feature of the angle between scatterings with and without the contribution of the flood-affected ground is examined for the quad polarimetric data obtained by the FDTD analysis.

articleTitle: Broadband Dielectric Characterization of Multilayer and Thin Film Using Tunable FSS in Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a new method for broadband dielectric measurement of thin-films and multilayer materials using a varactor-based tunable Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) through a waveguide. This approach utilizes varactors allowing resonant frequency to shift with an applied DC voltage from 0 to 12V. The proposed FSS consists of eight unit-cells with aperture and an edge-cut rectangular patch. Using the tunable FSS, the sweeping measurable frequency range spans from 17.2 - 25.2GHz. The proposed method is validated through simulations and measurements of samples with known dielectric constants- TLY and RF-35.

articleTitle: Design of Endfire Antenna in SIW with Step Structure in Multilayer Substrate at 300GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An endfire antenna is developed in this work. A step structure fed from the middle layer to the aperture is formed in the multilayer substrate. The lengths of the steps are approximately a quarter wavelength in the substrate to operate as an impedance transformer. The lengths of the steps are optimized to match over wide frequency bandwidth. The matching characteristics and the radiation performances are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Active Performance Verification of 28 GHz 5G Beam-forimg Antenna Module using CATR Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: As mobile communication technologies such as 5G and 5G-Advanced continue to evolve, the development of millimeter-wave band beamforming antennas is progressing rapidly, accelerating their application in commercial use. For millimeter-wave band beamforming antennas, it is essential to have modules that integrate the antenna and beamformer directly. New parameters such as TRP, EIRP, EVM, and Beam Scan Range are required to verify the beamforming capabilities. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for verifying the performance of beamforming antenna modules using existing CATR chambers and validates it using a 28 GHz band 5G antenna module.

articleTitle: Batteryless NFC Sensor Tag for Temperature Threshold Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, we designed a batteryless near-field communication (NFC) sensor tag to be used in metal environments. The batteryless sensor is powered wirelessly by an interrogating device (e.g., a wireless phone). A use-case of this sensor tag is to determine the health of batteries in the automotive industry by monitoring violations of temperature safety thresholds. The NFC sensor tag is backed with ferrite material, capable of such temperature threshold measurements in harsh metal environments. Read range measurements indicate that the design is ideal to tag batteries with a metal housing and read out the sensor state. We were able to achieve read ranges of 60 mm, which were almost independent of metal beneath the coil.

articleTitle: A Vertically Polarized Gap Waveguide Array Antenna for Joint Communication and Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An array antenna utilizing gap waveguide technology has been designed for joint communication and sensing applications. The array comprises a 5 × 5 configuration of single elements, each generating vertical polarization. Each group of five vertical slots is combined into a single port, resulting in a 5–element linear array that allows horizontal scanning. The design features a multi-layered structure, with five layers enabling vertical polarization. The initial distribution layer guides electromagnetic waves, while the subsequent four slotted layers progressively rotate the electric field orientation. The S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> < −10 dB impedance bandwidth is from 75.9 – 84.3 GHz at broadside and from 77 – 83 GHz at 30° scanning.

articleTitle: Impact of Safety Angle on Channel Capacity in THz X-Haul Links
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: THz X-Haul links have great potential to replace conventional cable connections. One of the limiting factors to operating THz X-Haul links is the high interference level. The high interference level can be managed by considering the safety angle between adjacent links at the planning stage. This paper discusses the impact of the safety angle on the channel capacity in THz X-Haul links considering the radiation pattern of different antenna gains recommended by ITU.

articleTitle: Precision Enhancement in EMC Measurements: Optimizing Multi-Layer Lens for Horn Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study focuses on advancing precision in Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) measurements through the innovative optimization of Horn antenna performance. Utilizing a multi-layer lens with strategically varied radii, the proposed design significantly enhances antenna directivity and sensitivity across a wide frequency spectrum. Beyond addressing challenges in radiated emission and immunity tests, the novel lens configuration demonstrates notable gain improvement. The wideband horn antenna working in the range of 1–18 GHz offers a gain improvement from 7.5–14.65 dBi to 11–23.1 dBi. This work promises to elevate the reliability of EMC measurements, facilitating more accurate assessments and compliance evaluations in diverse electronic systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of 3-D Prited Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna using Property Variation of Material Infill Process
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, analysis of 3-d printed pattern-reconfigurable antenna using property variation of material infill process is proposed. The proposed antenna structure consist of 5 beam microstrip patch and 4 type material infill density. With this variation of lens infill density, deteriorated return loss and increased directivity of radiation pattern are shown in simulation. By optimization of infill density with 80%, experimental results shows that proposed element can obtain over 12 dBi peak gain for each 5-beam mode and 3dB beamwidth(BW) about ±35° in both Elevation and horizontal plane.

articleTitle: Investigation of Parameters Influenced by Antenna Boresight for 5G Receive Signal Level
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study explores the impact of boresight adjustment effects on receive signal level in the context of 5G mobile network technology. This research aims to analyze and identify parameter features that affect changes in the received signal level by 5G receiving devices. Utilizing simulations and experiments in a controlled environment, we vary the boresight angle and measure its impact on the detected signal strength. This paper analyzes and investigates two parameters that are strongly affected by the presence of boresight at the transmit antenna. These two parameters are then analyzed with the receive signal level obtained based on the drive test results. There are several things that can be found to be related and interrelated between these parameters and the received signal level. Hopefully, these parameters can be used further in other research, especially in analyzing the receive signal level or to predict the signal level that will be received in a network, especially in 5G network.

articleTitle: Multi-physics Modelling of Stretchable Antennas on Soft Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The ongoing progress in stretchable materials has led to significant advancements in stretchable and wearable electronics. Consequently, there is a growing demand for multi-physics modelling methods for stretchable antennas on soft materials, which is crucial for optimizing antenna design and functionality. This paper presents a comprehensive approach to multi-physics modelling of stretchable microstrip patch antennas based on serpentine mesh layouts, integrating mechanical deformation and electromagnetic performance analyses. The designed stretchable antenna is based on a solid microstrip patch antenna with dimensions of 60*60*2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and a resonant frequency of 2.45 GHz. The results reveal a significant trade-off between the antenna's stretchability and electromagnetic performance, providing valuable insights for the design and optimization of stretchable antennas.

articleTitle: Wing-shaped Wearable Textile Antenna for a Military Tracking System on Ripstop Nylon Fabric
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a wing-shaped antenna structure fabricated on military camouflage ripstop nylon material for military applications. The design employs the defected ground structure (DGS) technique to enhance bandwidth and mitigate frequency detuning commonly encountered during military operations under harsh conditions. The conductive part of the antenna is made from a self-developed copper-covered yarn created by twisting polyester and copper yarns together. Validation was performed through simulations using the CST tool and lab measurement. The results showed good agreement between the simulations and measurements, demonstrating the practicality of the design for military operations. DGS implementation has improved the return loss value from -14.35 dB to -24.85 dB as well as the bandwidth which increased from 60 MHz to 100 MHz. The size of the slot has been a good variable for controlling the operating frequency. As a result, the antenna can be tuned to operate at desired frequency.

articleTitle: A Study of 3D-printing High Equivalent Isotropic Radiated Power Circularly Polarized Self-Oscillating Integrated Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a high equivalent isotropic radiated power (EIRP) circularly polarized self-oscillating integrated antenna (CPAIA) based on a quad-helical antenna design is developed. This research employs metamaterial zeroth-order resonators to effectively excite the ground plane and utilizes the 3D-printing technology to fabricate a three-dimensional antenna structure with quad spiral arms. An artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) is placed on the back of the antenna to further increase the overall antenna gain. The proposed quad-helical CPAIA achieves an EIRP of 17.8 dBm and a DC-RF conversion efficiency of 20%, with a circular polarization region spanning -50° to 55° in the xz plane and -50° to 70° in the yz plane.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable High Power Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Single-Chip Transmitter Circuit for mm-wave Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel single-chip high-power transmitter solution for dual-band millimeter-wave (mmwave) satellite applications. Integrating a power amplifier (PA), an absorptive single-pole-double-throw (SPDT) switch, and a dual-band branch-line coupler (DB-BLC), the chip enables a dual-band, dual-polarized transmitter circuit working at 18 GHz and 28 GHz. Its unique design generates opposite phases at split ports, facilitating direct use with orthogonally placed linearly polarized antennas to produce dual circular polarization at dual bands. The reconfigurability is achieved using the switch to get the desired polarization. This innovative single-chip solution addresses the complex demands of satellite communication, offering compactness, reconfigurability, and polarization diversity essential for modern satellite systems.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Rg and Rgs Effects on MOSFET for EMI Reduction in a Full Bridge Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In wireless power transfer (WPT) system, the reduction of electromagnetic interference (EMI) is significant. Not only noise caused by leakage magnetic field, but also noise from inverter affect EMI problem to peripherals. Switches of the inverter generate a switching waveform composed of harmonic components, which are harmful to other devices. In this paper, investigations of the rise time of the switching waveform, which is affected by the gate resistance and gate-source resistance, are conducted in order to decrease the harmonic components.

articleTitle: Analysis of Frequency Characteristics of Leaf Attenuation by a Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper clarifies the frequency characteristics of attenuation due to tree leaves (leaf attenuation) by the finite-different time-domain method. The attenuation at 15 GHz was measured, and the calculation results were confirmed by comparison with the measurement results.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Recognition with the Fusion of ToF and UWB radar sensors
