publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposed a fusion model of both radar and Time-of-Flight sensor data for the recognition of 12 daily used hand gestures. During the recognition process, a fusion model with the time-frequency analysis result of raw UWB radar data and the optical data after Mediapipe were constructed. A fusion of these two features to obtain further classification results. Finally, the fusion process yielded a classification accuracy of 95.42%.

articleTitle: On the Reconstruction Accuracy of MIMO Radar Channel by Reconfigurable Electronic Phantom
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the concept of a reconfigurable electronic phantom (RePH), using a reconfigurable intelligent surface, as a simple and low-cost test system for human-sensing multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radars. RePH consists of an array antenna and variable loads connected to each array element. By controlling the variable loads, the propagation characteristics of the signal incident on the RePH can be passively manipulated. That is, it can reconstruct any MIMO radar channel in the presence of a human subject, acting as a dynamic phantom that reproduces the Doppler shift caused by human biological activity. This paper investigates the relationship between the reconstruction accuracy of the MIMO radar channel and the RePH configuration through ray-tracing simulation.

articleTitle: Material Parameter Optimization for Raytracing Simulations in a 300 GHz Indoor Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper analyzes THz communications, by comparing 300 GHz channel measurements from a conference room with corresponding raytracing simulations. The room geometry, as well as the material parameters are carefully measured, to ensure accurate simulation results. Additionally, all relevant interaction mechanisms, i.e. reflections, diffractions and scattering, are used during the raytracing simulations. Afterwards, simulated annealing is used, to improve the accuracy of the previously measured material parameters, to obtain better results for the raytracing simulations. It is shown, that the match between the channel measurements and raytracing simulations significantly improve through the usage of the proposed simulated annealing algorithm.

articleTitle: Calculation Methods for Phase Retrieval in Near-Field Planar Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, to reduce the calculation time of the phase retrieval method, we use singular value decomposition and conjugate gradient method to solve the problem and compare the calculation accuracy and time. The simulation results confirm that singular value decomposition simplifies the calculation process and reduces calculation time in high accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Metamaterial Technology for Microwave Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, two technologies of metamaterial for microwave wireless power transfer are shown. One is a zeroth-order resonance for a microwave snow melting system, and another one is a focusing reflector for realizing of a highly efficient wireless power transfer space. A zeroth-order resonance leads a uniformed microwave heating and a flexibility of feeding in a snow melting system. Focusing reflector can make some electromagnetic hot and null points in a space. These are expected to be required technologies for highly efficient wireless power transfer.

articleTitle: Effect of Backscattering Caused by Two Localizers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of backscattering caused by two localizers (LOCs) positioned in a straight along the landing course. The LOC is a navigation system that horizontally guides landing aircraft. When the LOC needs to be updated or replaced, a new LOC is placed and operated while the current LOC remains. Scattered waves from the forward LOC have the potential to affect the operation of the backward LOC. In this paper, we analyze the backscattering caused by the forward LOC and investigate the acceptable distance between them to ensure safe operation.

articleTitle: Characteristics of A Transparent Metasurface with A Cross-Mesh Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An electromagnetic (EM) wave of a high frequency band exhibits a higher propagation loss and smaller ability to wrap around shielding objects than a low frequency band. In the case of the receiving antennas placed in a non-line-of-sight (NLOS) coverage area degrades the received signal strength indicator (RSSI). To solve this problem, a metasurface reflector that can enhance a reflecting EM wave in the desired NLOS direction had been actively researched. However, in a typical metasurface reflector, the area behind the reflector becomes a new NLOS location. Therefore, we have developed a transparent metasurface with a cross-mesh structure that allows to control the direction of reflected EM waves. We clarified the influence of the structural parameters of a transparent metasurface with a cross-mesh structure on the EM properties and its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Compact MIMO Closed-Slot Antennas for 2.4/5/6 GHz Laptops
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact WiFi-7 multi-input multi-output (MIMO) system with six antennas, tailored for laptop integration. Each antenna incorporates a 44 × 2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> closed-slot structure with a straightforward T-shaped feeder that achieves half-wavelength and full-wavelength resonances through feed-in coupling. The antennas are arranged in parallel, each spaced 4 mm apart, forming a tight array that eliminates the need for additional isolation elements. This configuration enables dual-band functionality, covering the 2400–2500 MHz and 5150–7125 MHz WiFi-7 bands. Additionally, the radiation efficiency of the array is measured to exceed 64%.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Multi-Beam Flat Lens Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of a multi-beam flat GRadient INdex (GRIN) lens antenna. The lens profile is found analytically in conjunction with an arc feed trajectory to produce an approximate uniform phase on the lens aperture for maximum radiation angle. Compared to previously reported designs, this approach significantly improves the scanning performance of the flat lens in two-dimensional (2D) planes. The variation in the refractive index profile of the lens is implemented using a partially filled dielectric periodic cubic unit cell. An array of microstrip patch sub-arrays is used as feed sources. The sub-arrays are arranged in two orthogonal planes to demonstrate the 2D multi-beam performance of the lens antenna system. A prototype lens antenna is fabricated using 3D printing technology operating from 12 to 15 GHz. This design is a high-gain multi-beam antenna suitable for satellite communications.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured Dual-Band Reflective Metasurfaces for Quadruplexed Channel and Energy Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Additively manufactured dual-band reflective metasurfaces (MSs) are proposed for generating four orbital angular momentum (OAM) carrying beams and two focus beams with the arbitrary energy distribution ratio (EDR). The Pancharatnam–Berry (P–B) phase controls the phase difference between the left-hand and right-hand circularly polarised (LHCP, RHCP) waves. The dynamic phase determines the reflection phase of co-polarisation. These two phase-control methods enable independent manipulation of the LHCP and RHCP for the unit cell. The MS’s unit cell has a multilayered structure, the upper cross-bar for the high-band phase control and the lower circular patch (CP) antenna with time delay lines (TDLs) for the low-band, which helps achieve independent phase control in the dual-band. The proposed MS samples are fabricated using multi-material additive manufacturing.

articleTitle: Transient Far-Field Radiation of Reconfigurable Liquid Crystal Reflectarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The unit cell dynamics of Liquid-Crystal (LC) based reflectarray antennas and Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces have been recently analyzed. However, the temporal evolution of the radiation pattern, which can differ from the individual cell response, has not been thoroughly studied. In this paper, a methodology to analyze the dynamic far-field radiation is proposed and tested for two LC antennas. This can open the door to the relaxation of temporal requirements and to achieve further antenna-level response time optimization.

articleTitle: A Hexagonally Shaped Unit Cell for Holographic-Based Leaky Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a hexagonally shaped unit cell that allows for the realization of the modulated surface impedance of a holographic-based leaky wave antenna is presented. For a valid eigenmode solution a rectangular cut-out of the hexagonally unit cell arrangement and an analytical calculation of the hexagonally unit cell positioning is performed. The eigenvector-supported tensor synthesis is used to compute the impedance hologram by utilizing hexagonally shaped unit cells. The hexagonally shape leads to an increased number of unit cells and thus to an increased radiated power. A holographic-based leaky wave antenna is fabricated on a fused silica wafer for an operation frequency of 160 GHz. The far field measurements show a maximum gain of 34.1dBi corresponding in an aperture efficiency of 40% and a side-lobe level below −27dB is achieved.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Human Activity Recognition Using Millimeter-Wave Radar with WSCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) using radar is valued for its robustness in all-weather conditions and its adherence to privacy. However, the limited diversity in radar datasets often results in models that are overly fitted to specific environments, impairing their ability to generalize. Addressing this challenge, we introduce a Wavelet Scattering Convolutional Neural Network (WSCNN). This model leverages a small, targeted dataset to generate time-frequency spectrograms. Experimental findings demonstrate that WSCNN not only sustains superior performance with few-shot training but also dramatically reduces the number of parameters required for training.

articleTitle: Wearable Wideband High-Gain Low-SAR Antenna with Bending and Wet Conditions Analysis at Sub-6 GHz 5G band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A rhombus shaped wearable textile patch antenna with inset-fed concept for sub-6 GHz 5G is proposed in this paper. By introducing rhombus-shape structure for the first time in the wearable antenna domain, the gain of the antenna has been enhanced significantly. The Felt substrate used has relative permittivity of 1.45 and thickness of 3 mm. The proposed antenna with a total size of 60 mm × 57 mm operated at n78 and n77 band of the sub-6 GHz with overall bandwidth of 300 MHz when placed on-body and gain value of 5.099 dBi when bent at 30° in free space. Besides, the antenna was robust in operating at the desired frequency at bending and fully wet condition. The proposed antenna achieved good directional radiation patterns, low SAR value and high antenna gain at the desired frequency band. The proposed design can be a valuable candidate for body-centric wearable communications.

articleTitle: Improving Heart-Rate Estimation Accuracy Using Two-Beam Technique in Millimeter-Wave Vital-Sign Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper experientially examines heart rate estimation using a millimeter-wave vital sign radar, which can eliminate the body-motion components using two-beam technique. Measurement was conducted in an anechoic chamber using a 79 GHz 2 × 4 Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave (FMCW) radar. When the subject rocked his upper body at 1 Hz, the experimental result showed that this technique reduces the body-motion components by 40 dB and improves the heart rate estimation accuracy by 14.6 bpm compared to the case without this technique.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Low-Profile Wideband Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact low-profile wideband metasurface antenna is presented in this paper. At first, the metasurface structure composed of 2 × 2 patch periodic arrangement is utilized to effectively reduce the transverse dimension of the antenna. After that, the bandwidth is effectively expanded by loading a metal via on the feeding strip to introduce resonant modes of the feeding structure at a low frequency. Simulation results show that the -10-dB impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 15.7% at a profile of only 0.034λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.

articleTitle: Mosaic Frequency Selective Surface Absorber for Low Profile Directive Antenna Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study investigated the incorporation of the Mosaic Frequency Selective Surface (MFSS) absorber at a separation distance (d) lower than quarter-wavelength from a basic monopole antenna (MA), to augment the MA’s directivity, thereby increasing the front-to-back ratio (FBR). The resistive MFSS is backed with a metal conductor, with 5 mm air gap spacing in between, to act as MFSS absorber. For the MA, a subminiature version A (SMA) connector is attached at the middle bottom of the silver conductor ground plane. The simulation process is conducted using the Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio software. By comparing simulated result performances between MA, perfect electric conductor incorporated monopole antenna (PECMA), and MFSS absorber incorporated with monopole antenna (MFSSAMA), the MFSSAMA demonstrated promising performance, in which FBR of 15.16 dB is obtained when d is only 4 mm (0.08 ${\lambda _{{f_r}}}$). Even though the PECMA demonstrated the highest FBR of 17.79 dB, however, PECMA experienced impedance mismatched when d = 4 mm. Meanwhile, the MA exhibited zero FBR. This had proven the significant suitability of the MFSS absorber incorporated with MA for low-profile directive antenna applications.

articleTitle: 3D-printed Flat Dielectric Lenses Using Split-pin Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article presents two different 3D-printed dielectric lenses, a Luneburg and a Gutman lens, which use a split-pin unit cell in a parallel plate waveguide implementation. The split-pin allows to generate higher refractive indices by allocating a high permittivity slab on top of a lower permittivity pin, which facilitates the manufacturing.

articleTitle: Array Filtering Antenna with Polarization Diversity for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study presents a ±45° polarized array filtering antenna using two interdigital resonators with via hole and a rectangular radiator. The filtering antenna is integrated adapting antenna and filter integration using single layer substrate. The single element antenna with 45° polarization is obtained by applying two orthogonal resonators represented by the interdigital and rectangular radiator. By mirroring the via hole position in +45° polarization antenna, −45° polarization antenna can be achieved. Array filtering antenna with polarization diversity is obtained by arranging the two antennas with −45°and +45° polarization side by side. The antenna operates at 4.6 GHz, bandwidth of 4.5% and gain of 7.6 dBi.

articleTitle: Design of a Flexible End-Fire Antenna with Low RCS Property
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a flexible end-fire antenna with a low backscattering structure. The antenna operates in the L-band and consists of the driven element, directors, and frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) to achieve low radar cross section (RCS) levels in the C-band. The design concept is from the Yagi-Uda antenna, which conducts the antenna to conform to the leading edge and radiate with the end-fire pattern. In addition, by using the resonance property of FSSs, the antenna maintains the radiation properties at an antenna operation frequency similar to comprising the metallic reflector. Hence, the numerical results verify both the scattering and radiation performance of the antenna.

articleTitle: Estimation of Interference Path Loss Characteristics for Radio Altimeter in Small Aircraft Using Parallel FDTD Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we perform large-scale numerical simulations using the parallel FDTD technique to evaluate the interference path loss (IPL) characteristics for the aircraft radio altimeter. We consider two types of transmitting (TX) antennas, a patch antenna and a dipole antenna, operating in the 5G-Sub6 frequency band neighboring the radio altimeter's band. We also discuss radiation patterns of the TX antennas mounted on the aircraft.

articleTitle: All-dielectric Terahertz 1D Leaky-Wave Antenna Based on Vertically Asymmetric Grating
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Beam-steering antennas with high gain are important in sensing applications. Yet, such antennas are scarce in the terahertz domain due to the lack of efficient tuning mechanisms. In this article, a 1D leaky-wave antenna based on vertically asymmetric grating is proposed. Leakage is obtained by introducing a periodic array of gratings, enabling the antenna to scan from −46° to 17° as the frequency sweeps from 220 GHz to 330 GHz. In the absence of a ground plane, the asymmetric grating largely suppresses backlobe radiation. The average mainlobe level is 21 dB with the backlobe level being suppressed to an average of around −10 dB. This antenna with its efficient and broandband operation has a strong potential for terahertz sensing applications at large.

articleTitle: Beam Steering with 1-Bit Coding Reconfigurable Metasurface Reflector Using Mechanical Slides
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper explores the beam steering capabilities of a low-cost, efficient, and 1-bit coding reconfigurable metasurface (MS) reflector using a mechanical slide. A one-dimensional 1x16 MS reflector was designed, with the unit cell configured to demonstrate three reflection angles: 0°, 15°, and 30°. Desired phase distributions corresponding to the reflection angles are achieved by adjusting mechanical slides. The results confirm the theoretical predictions, showcasing the potential for advanced wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Utilizing Floating Wind Turbine Foundations for Underwater-to-Air Radio Wave Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Utilizing the existing foundation of a floating wind power turbine in the ocean as the channel for radio wave communication from underwater to air is studied. It is demonstrated that the foundation can be a low-loss transmission line for radio propagation in the sea. Additionally, on the opposite side of the excitation source, fields decrease more slowly in the radial direction.

articleTitle: Modelling of an Inverted Discone Antenna on an Infinite Soil Plane for Radio Astronomy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The Cosmic Dawn epoch marks a pivotal phase in the evolution of the early universe. A frequency-independent antenna is required to avoid confusion of the weak radio signal of neutral hydrogen in the early universe from foregrounds that are at least 50 dB stronger. This paper models two inverted discone antennas placed on the ground as candidates for this purpose. To avoid edge effects of a metallic ground plane, the antenna needs to be modelled on dielectric. The antennas are modelled on soil from 40 MHz to 120 MHz and the effects of integrating a receiver directly into the disk section are investigated. We explore these as potential candidates to detect the global imprint of redshifted hydrogen on the cosmic microwave background.

articleTitle: Wideband Single-Element MIMO DRA for 5G Millimeterwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, we present a single-element multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) with improved bandwidth. By removing a portion from the center of the DRA, the achieved impedance bandwidth ranges between 26.3-29.5 GHz covering the entire 28 GHz band. By utilizing orthogonal excitation, metallic via inserted inside the DRA, and defected ground, an isolation exceeding 16 dB across the entire operational bandwidth is obtained. The peak gain attained 6 dbi and the radiation efficiency is up to 96%. The MIMO performance parameters are well within the acceptable limits which makes the design a suitable choice for operation in the mm-wave 5G band. Owing to its single-element configuration, the proposed MIMO antenna offers a very compact design.

articleTitle: Angle of Arrival Antenna Array Design for BLE 5.1 Direction Finding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Indoor localization is the procedure of determining the precise position of an object or person within a confined space, such as building or room. Unlike outdoor global positioning systems (GPS) that rely on satellite signals, indoor localization faces extra challenges because of the absence of reliable GPS signals in indoor environments. Directional finding systems in Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) frequently utilize antenna arrays based on the Angle of Arrival (AoA) method to determine the source of a BLE signal. This technology is widely utilized in situations like indoor positioning, asset tracking and location-based services. Thus, in this regard, 12patch antenna array is proposed in this paper for direction finding applications. A 12-patch antenna array is designed and fabricated using an FR4 substrate measuring 200 mm X 200 mm with 1.6 mm thickness. Additionally, simulation and design of the 12-patch AoA antenna array are conducted using Ansys Electronics Desktop 2021R1. The A3 patch antenna operates in 2.37-2.49 GHz frequency band with 2.40 GHz resonant frequency. Moreover, it has -20.30 dB return loss and 3.2 dBi gain. Also, the simulated results closely align with the measured findings.

articleTitle: Design of a single-layer ring microstrip antenna with a varactor-loaded open stub for pattern-reconfigurable reflectarrays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents design of a single-layer ring microstrip antenna (MSA) with a varactor-loaded open stub for pattern-reconfigurable reflectarrays. The proposed MSA consists a ring-shaped patch and a varactor-loaded open stub with a coupling probe arranged on a single-layer dielectric substrate with a ground plane on the back. The reflection phase of the proposed ring MSA can be controlled by a DC bias voltage applied for the varactor diode on the stub, where a capacitance of the varactor diode is changed by the DC voltage. Therefore, electronical beam shaping or beam steering can be realized by reflectarrays with the proposed MSAs. Firstly, the proposed ring MSA with a varactor-loaded open stub is designed at 5.1 GHz by using Ansys HFSS. The simulated results with the periodical boundary condition reveal that phase of the reflected wave of the proposed MSA can be changed in the range of 325 degrees when the capacitance of the varactor diode is varied from 0.2 pF to 0.75 pF. Then, beam steering performance of the 3×5 element reflectarray with the proposed MSAs is analyzed. It is confirmed by the simulation that 77 degrees beam steering to a normal incident plane wave can be obtained.

articleTitle: K−factor Emulation in Different OTA Chambers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses over-the-air testing chambers and the principles behind emulating Rician-distributed channel fading envelopes of the propagation channel. The discussed chambers are the classical reverberation chamber, the vibrating intrinsic reverberation chamber, the multi-probe anechoic chamber, the resonating cavity hybrid anechoic-reverberation chamber, and the aveguide hybrid anechoic-reverberation chamber.

articleTitle: Frequency Reconfigurable Miniature Monopole Antenna Using Magneto-Dielectric Material
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable miniature monopole antenna partially loaded with a Tunable Magneto-Dielectric Material (T-MDM) in the VHF band. A parametric study optimised the amount of the T-MDM and its effect on miniaturization. The antenna achieves a 40% miniaturization rate with just 17% of its height loaded by a 2 mm thick MDM, and demonstrates 15% frequency agility in the VHF band.

articleTitle: Damaged Building Detection Using Time Series Interferometric SAR Coherence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigated the factors of temporal decorrelation using time series Sentinel-1 data in damaged urban areas affected by the 2016 Kumamoto earthquake. Co-seismic coherence was primarily influenced by sub-pixel level coregistration errors related to surface deformation, while post-seismic coherence was mainly affected by damage. Through these findings, we proposed a damage indicator using the stacked pre-seismic coherence and the post-seismic coherence.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Dual-Band Leaky-Wave Antenna-in-Package Concept Based on Dual-Mode Grid-Shaped Microstrip Line for Upper-mid Band and Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper is the first to propose a dual-polarized dual band leaky-wave antenna (LWA) with a grid-shaped feed structure. The V-/H-polarization feature is realized in excited even/odd mode. The coupled circular patch structure is a shared aperture topology exemplified for the upper-mid band and Ka-band. Furthermore, the open stopbands are suppressed by adding a circular patch structure with a slit and matched hole structure. As a result, continuous beam scanning from backward to forward is achieved. An ultra-wideband balun and power divider based on SICL feed are designed to support the radiating structure. The validated prototype exhibits scanning range results show that the V-/H-polarized scanning ranges of the 1-D LWA are -30/-34 to +15/+10 (upper-mid band) and -30/-55 to +40/+15 (Ka-band), respectively. The peak gain exceeds 8 and 10 dBi at the two operating bands, demonstrating the fact that high gain can be achieved despite more than 64% size reduction compared to recent reference designs unit cells number reduction of more than 72%.

articleTitle: Towards Handheld Millimetre-Wave Scanners: Challenges and Opportunities of Freehand Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Freehand imaging systems enable the retrieval of high-resolution electromagnetic images with a compact handheld device. In particular, they rely on radar modules of reduced size that are moved by hand by the operator of the system over the area under inspection while its position is tracked. Thus, they bypass the use of bulky positioners and their overall cost is drastically reduced. This work summarizes the main features of these systems and their architecture, and provides an overview of the latest advances in this technology. In addition, some of the challenges that must be addressed to enable the use of freehand systems in practical applications, illustrated with measurements obtained with a freehand imaging prototype, are discussed.

articleTitle: Meandered Line and Inverted L-shaped loaded Tri-Band Flexible Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A triple band monopole microstrip patch antenna for wireless local area network (WLAN) Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band, and lower 5G Sub-6 GHz band, Band is presented in this article. The overall geometry of the antenna consists of a substrate, multiple stubs to radiate at three bands, and a ground plane. The antenna is made flexible by using the Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrate. The antenna has -10dB impedance bandwidth three bands are 2.2-2.6 GHz, 3.3-3.6 GHz, and 5.2 – 7 GHz respectively. The antenna dimensions are 15 × 20 × 1 mm3. The antenna is a potential candidate for multiple wireless applications.

articleTitle: Wide-angle Multi-beam Spherical Homogeneous Dielectric Lens Antenna in 270 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A spherical homogeneous dielectric lens antenna with wide-angle multi-beam characteristics in 270 GHz band is developed. The placement position and arrangement pitch of the primary radiators of the developed antenna are designed taking into consideration not only the peak gain but also the obtaining high cross-over gain. As a result of designing the arrangement radius and the arrangement pitch of the horns considering the multi-beam cross-over gain, a 16 multi-beam spherical lens antenna with a cross-over gain of more than 27 dBi within ±30° range is realized.

articleTitle: Initial Assessment of THz Indoor Channel with Passive Reflective Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) communications is expected to be an essential part of the future mobile communication system to meet the demand for ubiquitous high-speed data transmission everywhere. To overcome the limitations of THz communications, reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) shows their great potential. THz indoor channel measurements were performed using 1-bit and 3-bit passive-RIS fabricated as a passive reflector engraved on the PCV panel designed for a fixed angle of incidence and reflection to understand the propagation channel including RIS. A part of the initial assessments for the THz channel measurement including RIS are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-Polarized 1-Bit Reconfigurable Reflect-Array Unit Cell at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-polarized 1-bit reconfigurable reflect-array antenna (RRA) unit cell is reported at Ka-band. By jointly exploiting the electric and magnetic resonant modes, a novel wideband unit cell with 1-bit phase resolution and simple laminates is proposed. Moreover, the reflection loss is smaller than 0.9 dB and the 1-bit phase shift is achieved within 180° ± 20° from 23.2 to 30.5 GHz. The experimental results measured in a square waveguide are well matched with the simulations, further demonstrating the validity of the proposed element.

articleTitle: RIS Subset Selection/Assignment Based on Multi-Armed Bandit in Multi-RIS-Aided Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper, proposes a preliminary approach to optimal user-Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) subset selection/assignment based on Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) to improve the overall communication quality of wireless systems. Users select optimal RIS subsets based on the observations of previous selections to maximize the Spectral Efficiency (SE) based on instantaneous Channel State Information (CSI). The SE is drawn from Nakagami-m distribution and mean. The simulation results show that with the adopted approach faster RIS subset selection/assignment to the users can be achieved.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Convex-Type Multi-Beam Metasurface Reflector for mmWave Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Reconfigurable metasurface reflectors have recently been considered as the countermeasures for the coverage hole problem in millimeter wave (mmWave) communication systems. In this paper, a novel reconfigurable convex-type multi-beam metasurface reflector is proposed for obtaining a wide reflection direction range without an external direct-current (DC) supply. To obtain a wide reflection phase range, the proposed reflector includes large-via mushroom-type structure. As a result, a wide reflection direction range could be achieved by mechanically changing the aperture angle of convex-type reflector.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Planar Ultra-wideband Modular Antenna Design Based on Folded Active Dipole
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel miniaturized planar ultra-wideband modular antenna (PUMA) unit design operating from 2.51 to 11.31GHz with active voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR)<3 at broadside is proposed in this paper. When scanning up to ±45° in both E-, H- and D-planes, the PUMA provide 4.5:1, 4.2:1 and 4.4:1 relative bandwidth with active VSWRs<3, respectively. At the same time, the total efficiency of the PUMA is simulated to be above 95% for both broadside and scanning cases. Folded active dipole arm instead of traditional bowtie design is adopted to achieve antenna miniaturization. Above it, this article loads overlapping pads and passive dipole to move the working band towards lower frequencies, achieving further miniaturization while obtaining broadband. Notably, the PUMA unit has sizes of only 0.19λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</inf>×0.19 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</inf> ×0.45λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</inf>.

articleTitle: RCS Prediction Using Image-Based NFFFT Algorithm with Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Measuring far-field RCS requires creating an environment that matches the target, which involves spatial and economic constraints. For this reason, research on far-field to near-field conversion algorithms has been actively conducted. Accurate RCS calculations require a large amount of measurement data, but obtaining many samples increases measurement time and the computation time for Reflectivity images. In this paper, to calculate high-accuracy RCS with fewer samples, we applied an interpolation function to the Reflectivity image data of the existing image-based NFFFT algorithm to create new Reflectivity images. Based on this, we compared and analyzed the accuracy of the RCS calculation results and the computation time of far-field to near-field conversion with those of the existing algorithm.

articleTitle: The Potential of Channel Impulse Response Correlation in Integrated Sensing and Communication: A Wideband Measurement Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Integrating a sensor in communication systems becomes a warm topic. While communicating between channel elements, namely transmitters, and receivers, an additional device detects objects in the channel vicinity. Those objects change the behavior of received signals. This work proposes an analysis based on channel impulse response (CIR) values, and the characterization is performed using a correlation of the CIR. A measurement was performed, and the result analysis shows that the correlation value drops when an object moves around the elements. The object significantly changes the correlation if it is close to the elements.

articleTitle: A Study on CNN-Based Rain Attenuation Prediction Considering Spatial Characteristics for Millimeter Wave Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Rain attenuation poses a significant challenge for High Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS) communication systems operating at millimeter wave frequencies. This paper analyzes the performance of the attenuation prediction using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based machine learning model considering the spatial rainfall characteristics in the 38GHz at points along the propagation path from the transmitter to the receiving sites. Results show improved performance when rainfall variations along the propagation path are considered.

articleTitle: Fast Numerical Simulation of Electric Field Distribution in Dielectric-Loaded Multimode Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a fast numerical simulation for analyzing dielectric-loaded multimode cavities using the electric field of active elements. The proposed method was applied to a cavity (700×600×500mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) containing water, where the magnitude and phase of the power source for each port were also adjusted. The accuracy and reliability of the proposed method are verified through a 3D electromagnetic full simulation. The proposed method not only reduces the time required to analyze field distributions within complex cavity geometries but also demonstrates its practical applicability in advanced microwave heating technologies.

articleTitle: Antenna Misalignment Effect for Kiosk Data Downloading Enviroment at 285GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Antennas used in the terahertz band are mainly directional antennas. When using a directional antenna, if the transmitting and receiving antennas are not aligned, the reception rate will inevitably be affected. From a received power perspective, if the directional antennas are not aligned, the received power is reduced. However, in terms of delay time, no specific research results have been presented on the impact of misalignment between directional antennas. In this paper, we will explain the correlation between antenna alignment and delay time when using directional antennas in the terahertz band.

articleTitle: Simple Estimation Method of Bistatic RCS for Transmitarray with Tilted Beam
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a simple estimation method of bistatic RCS of the transmitarray (TA) with tilted beam. In 5G, TA with tilted beam has gained attention. Such a TA with tilted beam is evaluated by the bistatic RCS measurement. However, the measurement setup of Bistatic RCS measurement is normally complicated. This paper proposes simple estimation measurement method of the bistatic RCS of TA by using planar scanning with two waveguide probes. The proposed method can predict bistatic RCS of TA with small space as compared to ordinal bistatic RCS measurement system. The validation of the proposed method is confirmed by the simulation with TA operating at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: A Reflection-Type Phase Shifter Using a Simplified Magic-T with a Delay Line and Parasitic Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we design a simplified model of a reflection-type phase shifter (RTPS) using the magic-T proposed in previous study. The proposed magic-T aims to achieve a compact, wideband RTPS with low insertion loss. The magic-T satisfying these criteria is designed, combined with a ring-type T- divider transitioning from microstrip to coplanar strips (CPS). A RTPS is designed using this magic-T. The RTPS makes a 90° phase difference in the two arms. In this paper, to simplify the design, this section is implemented using a λ/4 delay line. The bandwidth of the RTPS is 45%, with S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> less than -10 dB, and the phase shift is 122.3°. The RTPS is used a dipole array antenna. The bandwidth of the proposed array antenna is over 12%, with S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> less than -10 dB, and the phase shift is 38°.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Wideband Dual-polarized Antenna for 5G Base station
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel broadband dual-polarized antenna for 5G base station, which consists of a reflector, a radiator and two feed structures and two coaxial cables. etching slots on the antenna patch introduces new resonant frequencies, broadening the antenna's bandwidth while simultaneously reducing its size. To achieve good impedance matching and further broaden the bandwidth, the antenna proposed in this article adopts a new type of feed structure. According to CST simulation results, this dual-polarized antenna operates in the frequency band of 0.71-1.06GHz (N5/N8/N20/N28/N71) with |S11| < -10dB, an average isolation degree of 24 dB, and a half-power beamwidth (HPBW) of approximately 73.7 ± 3.5°. The gain of the antenna is between 6.8 and 7.8dBi in the operating frequency range.

articleTitle: EM Emission Test of a VCO with Twisted Inductor Using Chip-level Near-field Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) with the twisted inductor is tested by using the chip-level near-field coupling measurement for evaluating the radiated electromagnetic (EM) emission. The testing setup resembles the modern stacked packaging scheme by utilizing the flip-chip bonding and integrated passive device (IPD) technology. An embedded coplanar waveguide (CPW) line on IPD carrier is utilized to capture the EM emission via near-field coupling. Two 0.18- μm CMOS 6-GHz VCOs, one with a conventional spiral inductor and the other with a twisted inductor, are tested. The VCO utilizing the twisted inductor exhibited a notable improvement of over 6 dB in EM emission compared to the one employing a conventional inductor.

articleTitle: A Novel Analysis of Complementary Circular Spiral Resonator (CCSR) Based Sensors Using the BCITL Model for Dielectric Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel analysis of a dielectric sensor using the bi-characteristic-impedance transmission line (BCITL) model. The dielectric sensor is based on a microstrip line and a complementary circular spiral resonator (CCSR) on a ground plane, where it is designed to operate at the resonant frequency of 2.45 GHz in the ISM band. The analysis is performed by varying the dielectric constant of materials under test (MUT) placed underneath the ground plane of the dielectric sensor. Numerical results show that the BCITL model of the CCSR-based sensor can provide an additional physical insight into the sensing mechanisms.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Dual-Polarized Transmitarray Using a High-Isolation Feeding Antenna for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband dual-polarized transmitarray antenna illustrated for 24-GHz radar applications, featuring the broadband and high-isolation design. Utilizing two separate feed ports, the dual-polarization design excites two orthogonal modes within the same resonant cavity, resulting in a high port isolation of 40 dB over the entire band. Leveraging a three-layered phase gradient metasurface lens, the design achieves a 9-dB gain enhancement. We integrated the feeding antenna and the three-layered metasurface lens using a 3D printing fixture to realize the high-gain and high-isolation transmitarray module. In addition to the peak gain of 16 dBi, the extremely high port isolation and the radiated polarization isolation are achieved over a broad bandwidth covering from 23 to 27 GHz.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Ground Scattering Environments for Synthetic Aperture Radar Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper provides a method to reconstruct the scattering environment of the target land surface area, suitable for Synthetic Aperture Radar applications. By applying proper scattering models to a set of remote sensing data acquired from different sources, a realistic microwave reflectivity map of the scene can be acquired. Since the method focuses on the water content, the temporal variance of the scattering scene can be taken into account effectively.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Implantable Human Body Communication for Abdominal Neurostimulator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study investigated implantable human body communication (IHBC) for abdominal medical devices, such as neurostimulators, using electromagnetic field analysis. By employing a detailed anatomical human body model, we clarified complex signal propagation in IHBC. The findings reveal that the transmission between the implanted transmitter and the external receiver provides adequate performance for stable communication, and is not affected by variations in device implantation positions within approximately 10 mm.

articleTitle: A Compact Dipole-Type MIMO Antenna Design Using Decoupling Inductor for 5G Terminal Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a compact 2 × 2 MIMO dipole-type antenna that uses a decoupling inductor to mitigate mutual coupling between MIMO antennas. Through the simulated results, the proposed antenna demonstrated a – 6dB bandwidth of 340 MHz, ranging from 3.36 GHz to 3.70 GHz. By integrating decoupling inductors, the mutual coupling in the proposed antenna structure is suppressed to below –13.7 dB, indicating its feasibility for compact MIMO antenna systems.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Quadrifilar Helical Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work proposes a novel low-profile quadrifilar helical antenna for the BeiDou satellite navigation application. The designed antenna adopts four spring-shaped radiating arms, which can extend the current path of the radiating arm in a limited space, realizing the low-profile characteristics. The proposed antenna with a height of only 0.08λ shows good impedance matching in 1.55-1.60 GHz, fully covering the BeiDou B1 band. At 1.57 GHz, the half-power beamwidth (HPBW) of the right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) radiation patterns in the xoz and yoz planes are 119.6° and 118.5° respectively, and the corresponding 3-dB axial ratio beamwidths of which are 118.7° and 127°, respectively. The proposed quadrifilar helical antenna can be an excellent candidate for BeiDou satellite navigation due to its low profile and good circular polarization radiation performance.

articleTitle: A Dual-polarized Tapered Slot Antenna for Measuring probe
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a wideband dual-polarized Tapered Slot Antenna (TSA) for antenna measurement. In IoT and mobile communications whose demand is increasing, wideband, compact, and easy-to-use measurement probes are required. The dual-polarized TSA structure is achieved by inserting two orthogonal planar TSAs in a cross shaped form with slits in the TSAs. The simulation is performed in the frequency range of 2.4~7.0 GHz with a VSWR of 3 or less. The isolation (S21, S12) between the antenna ports is less than -25dB, and the gain is approximately 3~9dBi in the above frequency. The radiation patterns of each plane are almost same. Compared with other related studies, the antenna is suitable for a measurement probe in terms of its size and isolation.

articleTitle: Robust Keypoint Learning Framework for Visual Odometry in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Estimating 6-DoF camera motion in dynamic environments remains challenging because of the influence of moving objects. Traditional feature-based methods and self-supervised approaches struggle with distinguishing dynamic elements from static scenes. To tackle this problem, we propose a robust keypoint detection network designed for pose estimation in dynamic scenes, leveraging cycle consistency and pixel correspondences to guide extracting static keypoints. Our method is validated on highly dynamic sequences from the KITTI multi-object tracking dataset, demonstrating improved performance in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: A Reflectarray Antenna with Slotted Circular Patch Elements and Corrugated Horn Feeding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel design for a single-layer reflectarray antenna (RAA). The elements of the proposed RAA employ a variable rotation technique (VRT) to achieve circular polarization with wide bandwidth and high-gain performance. Each unit cell in the array is assigned a specific rotation angle to achieve the required phase delay. To further enhance performance, the RAA is center-fed by a wideband, dual-circularly polarized corrugated horn antenna. The main beam direction is set at θ = −20°, and an f/D focal ratio of 1.2375 is chosen to maximize the aperture efficiency. A proposed RAA, sized at 14.34 cm × 14.34 cm with 37 × 37 elements, is simulated using CST MWS. This RAA exhibits a simulated maximum antenna gain of 29.06 dBi at 25 GHz.

articleTitle: Received RF Amplifier with Bluetooth Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article presents received low noise amplifier with 2.4 GHz antenna development that uses cascode two stage distributed architecture. Experimental results of the RF integrated LNA exhibit radiation pattern with the proposed Bluetooth antenna. After simulation optimization the L-shaped microstrip patch antenna has been realized by using the printed circuit board (PCB) substrate with SMA connector and experimental were achieved.

articleTitle: Seasonal Changes of Rice Paddy Field Observed by ALOS2/PALSAR2 Polarimetric Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents time-series polarimetric decomposition images over rice paddy field observed by Advanced Land Observing Satellite 2 (ALOS2) /Phased Array type L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (PALSAR2). When planting row in paddy field is parallel to the orbit, the scattering phenomena throughout year exhibit significant changes according to the rice growing stage on the bare surface situation. The polarimetric observation data have been processed by G4U decomposition method which extracts the surface scattering and the double bounce scattering very distinctively. The decomposition images show significant seasonal changes of rice paddy field by the capability of polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) data.

articleTitle: Wide-Incident-Angle Radio-Wave Absorber with Loop-Shape Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work describes wide-incident-angle radio-wave absorbers for millimeter-wave (mmW) and sub-terahertz (sub-THz) applications. A loop-shape frequency-selective surface (FSS) is employed to improve low-frequency transmittance performance (e.g., Wi-Fi), which leads to a lower than 7dB transmittance loss (at the incident angle of 0 deg, simulated) at 2.4GHz. They show wideband 90-%-absorbing characteristics across 26.5GHz– 40GHz (Type 1) and 95.4GHz–181GHz/328GHz–431GHz (Type 2) up to the incident angle of 60deg, respectively.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Full Image Theory Method EM Ray Tracing for Massive Propagation Analysis with Enhanced Computational Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Traditional image theory (IT) ray tracers, while accurate, have been limited by computational inefficiencies. This study introduces a novel full-3D IT electromagnetic (EM) ray tracing (RT) method for extensive propagation analysis. Our framework handles multiple EM interactions—reflection, transmission, diffraction, and diffuse scattering—by leveraging a novel preprocessing algorithm, eliminating unilluminated zones, and utilizing CPU/GPU parallel computing. This results in performance over 34 times faster than commercial EM ray tracing software WinProp, making it suitable for large-scale scenarios.

articleTitle: Active Calibration Model of Wide-band Array Position Errors Using FMCW Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Unknown array position errors significantly impact the accuracy and resolution of angle estimations. This paper proposes an active calibration model using FMCW wide-band signals as the calibration source. However, the precise angle of the calibration source cannot be obtained. To address this, we construct an optimization problem that simultaneously calibrates the source angle and sensor positions. The problem is divided into two sub-problems to mitigate non-convexity, which are then solved using the ADMM algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Dual-layer 4x4 Butler Matrix for 5G application through Via Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In a 5G base station, a Butler Matrix (BM) feed circuit is requested to achieve multibeam patterns while maintaining a compact structure. However, the conventional design and size raise issues in installation and efficiency, especially at the lower 5G band, the 3.5GHz. To cater to many antenna elements, the BM size is increased, and the losses are severe, affecting the phase sensitivity. To address these issues, a stacked 4x4 BM with a dual-layer thin substrate is connected through non-uniform vias that act as a fine-tuning mechanism, where the desired phase difference is obtained by adjusting the circular slot diameter of the via. The BM features a low-profile structure with a 1.03 λ x 1.1 λ dimension, a significant reduction from the conventional 4x4 BM. The designed BM measured results show transmission amplitude of -7dB, and an acceptable range of output phase difference at the operating band.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Circular Polarization Selective Surface at Q/V-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present a dual-band circular polarization selective surface (CPSS) at Q/V-band. A dual-band shared-aperture CPSS element based on the modified Pierrot structure is employed to realize circularly polarization discrimination, i.e., reflecting CP wave of one handedness while transmitting the other orthogonally polarized one. The simulated 1-dB reflection bandwidths for this element are 3.8% at Q-band and 3.7% at V-band with an axial ratio smaller than 3 dB.

articleTitle: Fluid-Controlled Frequency and Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna for the S-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a fluid-controlled frequency and radiation pattern reconfigurable antenna is presented for the S-band applications. The antenna is designed on a 0.508 mm thick Rogers RT5880 lossy substrate. Initially, a partial ground-based monopole antenna is designed and optimized for the 2.4 GHz frequency band with an omnidirectional radiation pattern. Subsequently, two water-based fluid channels are designed on the ground plane. By controlling fluid in these channels, the frequency and pattern reconfigurability is achieved. Using the proposed method the operating frequency can be reconfigurable between 2 GHz and 2.52 GHz, while the direction of the radiation can also be controlled. The designed antenna offers a peak gain of more than 2.68 dBi for all the reconfigurable cases with a radiation efficiency of more than 70%. The overall performance of the presented antenna makes it a viable candidate for S-band applications with both frequency and pattern reconfigurability.

articleTitle: Effect of radio wave absorber in vehicle communication for co-channel full-duplex
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to realize co-channel full-duplex, it is important to reduce the coupling between the transmitter and receiver antennas. The authors have studied the location of antennas and the effects of surrounding objects on the coupling between transmitter and receiver antennas to realize co-channel full-duplex in vehicle communications. In this paper, we evaluate the effect of a radio wave absorber on the electric field strength around the vehicle and the coupling between the antennas.

articleTitle: Reflectivity Dataset Calculation Using Hybrid Method of Geometrical and Physical Optics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The reflectivity dataset of the virtual scene facilitates various applications, such as synthetic aperture radar simulations. However, existing methods are unable to calculate such datasets for electrically large objects. This paper introduces a ray tracing method based on geometrical and physical optics utilizing ray tubes. This method enables the computation of reflectivity dataset by applying physical optics for all ray reflections. The computed reflectivity dataset was validated.

articleTitle: Investigation on Multilevel Characteristic Basis Function Method using PMCHWT Formulation for Multi-dielectric and PEC Composite Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a multilevel characteristic basis function method (MLCBFM) using Poggio-Miller-Chang-Harrington-Wu-Tsai (PMCHWT) formulation. The MLCBFM is an effective numerical method based on the method of moments. It reduces problem dimension using characteristic basis functions to facilitate the inversion process of the impedance matrix. In this paper, we present the entire algorithm of multilevel CBFM using PMCHWT formulation and verify the accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed method with various numerical results. Additionally, we evaluate the performance with respect to certain parameters in the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Modified Compensation Method of Distorted Large Antennas Based on Best Operating Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For the problem of structural deformation caused by different loads acting on the reflector antenna during operation, a method of compensating for panel deformation of the reflector antenna based on best operating surface was proposed. The antenna surface fitting model was constructed, and the best operating adjustment paraboloid and the specific design variables for panel adjustment required for the reflector antenna after deformation were also determined. The proposed method effectively compensates for the deformation of the antenna panel and improves the electrical performance of the antenna. A simulation case of the Qitai 110 m radio telescope antenna is given to verify the accuracy and superiority of the method.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Real Time Anti-Drone RF Scanner using Switched Array Beamformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a cost-effective, real-time anti-drone RF scanner system employing a switched array beamformer and AI-driven drone signal analysis. Addressing the surge in unauthorized drone activities, our system combines Radio Frequency (RF) monitoring, AI-based drone detection and identification, and precise direction finding via a switched array beamformer. Utilizing multi-receiver Software-Defined Radio (SDR) platforms, the system offers comprehensive bandwidth coverage for drone signal detection. AI algorithms analyze time-frequency signal patterns to identify drones, while the beamforming array accurately determines their angles of arrival. Experimental results demonstrate the system's ability to detect and identify four drone types with 90% accuracy and pinpoint their direction with an average accuracy within 5 degrees. This research contributes significantly to the field of drone surveillance and security by providing a cost-effective, efficient solution.

articleTitle: Planar, Metal-Plate Shorted Monopole for Wi-Fi 7 and 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A simple, shorted monopole antenna, constructed from stamping a flat metal plate, operating in the 2.4/5/6 GHz Wi-Fi 7 bands and also the 6G upper mid-band in the 5925-8400 MHz range is introduced. The antenna design comprises a bent rectangular monopole short-circuited to a small antenna ground and a narrow side plate extended in the lateral direction with overall dimensions of 8 mm × 10 mm × 44 mm. The bent rectangular monopole can produce a wide operating bandwidth of 5150-8400 MHz, while the side plate contributes to the 2.4 GHz band. With a height of 0.08

articleTitle: Planar Sparse Arrays Using Triangular Lattice Transformations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the step by step design of a planar sparse arrays that uses triangular lattice transformation method. The triangular transformation allows us to go from a linear sparse array to a sparse triangular lattice sparse array. Moreover, the array is also windowed to generate a circular aperture, which effect is also considered. Finally, the proposed final array has around 4 dB Side Lobe Level (SLL) improvement compared with the linear sparse array.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Phased Array with Switchable Dual Circular Polarization Based on Subarray
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a low-cost K-band phased array antenna for satellite communication is designed. he phased array adopts a subarray sparse architecture to reduce the number of T/R components. However, for ease of subsequent processing and testing, modular requirements were proposed for the subarray topology. Furthermore, for compatibility with various satellite communication systems, phased array antennas also need to possess switchable dual circular polarization states. Furthermore, to validate the feasibility of the proposed scheme, the measurements were conducted using a 256-element K-band low-cost phased array across the entire frequency band. The results that within the scanning range of ±45°, the phased array exhibits good radiation performance and circular polarization capabilities.

articleTitle: Evaluation of SAR in Wireless Power Transfer Systems for Building Management Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recent research and development efforts have been advancing towards the realization of next-generation 5G/6G technologies. Specifically, the Internet of Everything (IoE) is poised to maximize the benefits of 5G/6G by interconnecting industrial machines, devices, equipment, systems, and human activities through networks. However, to date, no concrete IoE service has been fully realized, primarily due to the challenges of battery replacement and the limitations of wired connections for the numerous sensors and devices integral to the IoE, therefore long-range Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) is necessary. In this paper, we report the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) [1], an indicator of the impact of electromagnetic waves emitted from the transmitter on the human body, of Aeterlink’s WPT system AirPlug™.

articleTitle: Two-Port Hexagonal Bar Slotted Dual-Band MIMO Textile Antenna for WBAN and 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band textile Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna for Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) and Fifth Generation (5G) applications. The MIMO antenna consists of two hexagonal patch elements, each integrated with a bar slot to operate in dual-band mode at 2.45 GHz and 3.5 GHz. The dimension of each patch is 48.5 x 30 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This antenna is made fully by an all-textile with radiating elements by the conductive textile. The proposed MIMO textile antenna achieves the satisfactory results such as Reflection Coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) <-10 dB, very low MC < -30 dB, Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) < 0.001, and Diversity Gain (DG) of about 10 dB. The simulated results show that the proposed design covers the operating impedance bandwidth of about 6.3% and 6.2% in the 2.45 GHz and 3.5 GHz. The peak realized gain of 5.5 dBi is attained.

articleTitle: A Transmit Array Antenna for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a meta-surface based transmit array (TA) antenna design that operates at n257 band of 5G NR. A transmit array composed of four substrates with single side printed layers is proposed that provides full 360 deg phase sweep for transmission loss less than 2 dB. These substrate layers have air between them that helps to get wider range of the phase sweep. Two types of transmit array antennas have been fabricated and checked with wide beam horn antenna. The fabricated and simulated models produce similar results of more than 6 dBi broadside gain enhancement beyond 26 GHz. Total bandwidth obtained is more than 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction in MIMO Antenna Using Via-less EBG
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work proposes a MIMO antenna design achieving enhanced mutual coupling characteristics. Via-less meander-line EBG structures incorporated within the design suppress surface waves effectively, leading to a substantial 24 dB reduction in mutual coupling at a close antenna spacing of 0.13 wavelengths. The via-less design offers simplified fabrication while preserving the desired bandgap properties.

articleTitle: Design and Consideration of Broadband 60-GHz Antenna in Package
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Two different types of antenna-in-package are introduced, and the design and consideration are discussed for 60GHz frequency band. The E-shaped L-probe antenna in package reveals wide bandwidth thanks to its E-shaped and L-probe structure because it forms a multi-resonance structure. Horn antenna in package reveals a compact volume thanks to its own geometry. These two types of antennas are expected to be candidates for antenna in a package to be used in 60-GHz communications in the future.

articleTitle: Simulation of low RCS microstrip antenna loaded with artificial magnetic conductor surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In modern military, new breakthroughs have been made in detection technology, which puts forward higher requirements for the stealth performance of stealth aircraft. The RCS of the antenna accounts for the main part of the overall RCS, so reducing the RCS of the antenna is an important research content in the design of stealth aircraft. This paper designs a microstrip antenna and reduces the antenna RCS by loading a checkerboard-shaped artificial magnetic conductor surface composed of circular AMC units and rectangular AMC units.

articleTitle: Reducing Target-Ground Coupling in Near-Field Scattering Measurements by Elevation Adjustments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The measurement of the scattering of big targets is difficult, particularly in indoor near-field conditions where there are many interactions between the target and the backdrop. Scattering clutter caused by the ground has a major impact on Radar Cross Section (RCS) measurements. Existing techniques, such as raising the targets and employing materials that absorb, partially alleviate these problems, particularly when dealing with larger targets. However, they do not completely fix them. This study presents a technique in which the object is measured many times at different heights of elevation. This strategy improves measurement accuracy by utilizing vector superposition to mitigate coupling, surpassing the performance of conventional methods.

articleTitle: A Simple Analysis and Discussion of Poland Longwave Broadcasting Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: With the profound and complex changes of the international situation, the longwave communication has more and more important application value and strategic significance. And longwave can realize a large range of communication and even global communication at the low end of longwave frequency because of its advantages of low propagation loss, strong diffraction ability, etc. Therefore, longwave is widely used in a lot of fields, such as sea navigation, underground communication, underwater submarine communication, and so on. As one of the most important components of the longwave communication system, the performance of longwave antennas (LWAs) play a decisive role. In recent years, the research of LWAs mainly focuses on mechanical antenna and the traditional antenna form is less studied. In this paper, the world's most famous Poland longwave broadcasting station antenna is briefly discussed and analyzed and the development direction of the traditional longwave antenna is proposed.

articleTitle: Efficient IPO-MoM Hybrid Method for RCS Prediction Using for Large Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the application of the iterative physical optics approach combined with the method of moments, termed the IPO-MoM hybrid method, for efficient and accurate Radar Cross Section prediction of electrically large objects. The MoM current on a part of the scatterer is interpolated into the first-order physical optic current. Then, the conventional iterative physical optic iteration is computed. Comparative analyses with the MoM in FEKO, for dielectric object scattering, are provided to show the improvement in RCS estimation.

articleTitle: Real-Time Control Verification of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) Integrated with Direction of Arrival (DoA) Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper verifies the feasibility of real-time control through autonomous operation of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) based on direction of arrival (DoA) data, in scenarios involving a moving electromagnetic (EM) source. Previous studies have faced limitations in phase control due to reliance on data irrelevant to RIS functionalities, with most assuming perpendicular incidence of the source. The autonomously controlled RIS enabled a receiver located at 10 degrees to receive up to 15.1 dB higher power from a transmitter at 30 degrees compared to scenarios without bias, demonstrating the potential of RIS usage despite slow phase change response and unstable DoA data. This study proposes the effectiveness of RIS as a tool to address future communication challenges, offering a strategy for its practical application through simple hardware and automated operations.

articleTitle: Design BandPass Filter with Antenna for Ground-Penetrating Radar (GPR) Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article presents Butterworth bandpass filter with FR4 low-cost antenna for ground-penetrating radar (GPR) applications. The sixth-order bandpass filter consists of converter and leap-frog Gm-C from tsmc 0.35 um CMOS process. After simulation optimization the 100-MHz antenna has been realized by using the printed circuit board (PCB) substrate with SMA connector and experimental were achieved.

articleTitle: Highly Flexible and Foldable Antenna Array using Corrugated CCPM-based Patches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact, lightweight, and flexible array antenna for L-band applications is presented. The antenna consists of a primary patch and two parasitic patches using corrugated copper-cladded polyimide (CCPM) films, which provide excellent bending performance. A single antenna with high bending capability is developed first. This element is used to demonstrate a 1×4 linear array. The antenna has a bandwidth from 1.18 GHz to 1.26 GHz with a maximum gain of 14.6 dBi at 1.22 GHz. The antenna array is analyzed and measured for the flat case as well cylindrical cases with radius of 400, 300, 200, and 160 mm.

articleTitle: Development of a high total efficiency beam-forming antenna with a flat-top beam in radiative-near-field wireless power transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study describes a novel beam flat-top forming method using a low-cost phased array developed for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer at 28GHz to maintain high total efficiency, including beam and rectifying efficiencies, at a rectenna array. We achieve a reduction in the number of antenna elements in the phased array and a flat-top beam suitable for wireless power transfer in a radiative-near field.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: Active Probe Array for Spherical Near-field Measurement of 5G User Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An active probe array system is presented. The system can perform rapid spherical near-field measurements to characterize 5G user equipment (UE) transmitters from 3-60 GHz. The system comprises receiver module arcs arranged in elevation to acquire signals over the entire spherical surface around the UE. The synchronization and calibration procedures are described, which utilizes the GPS-disciplined rubidium oscillator. The measurement procedure is described, which uses a call simulator. The system enables rapid near-field acquisition of full transmitter signal characteristics for 5G UEs without requiring a phase recovery unit.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam Metasurface Reflector for Energy Harvesting to Multi-Devices in Different Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Metasurface reflectors have been applied to microwave wireless power transfer (WPT) for transmitting power to IoT devices that are placed at arbitrary locations. In this paper, a multi-beam metasurface reflector is introduced for realizing simultaneous power transfer to multiple IoT devices. To design a multi-beam metasurface reflector, a superposition method which is superimposing the reflection phase of each beam is used. The proposed scheme employs the Pozar’s design method when the metasurface is close to the wave source. Computer simulation results show that the power can be transmitted simultaneously to the two desired directions effectively.

articleTitle: Traveling Wave Array Design of Comb-Line Antenna Using Thick Elements in 270-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a traveling wave comb-line antenna to obtain a large coupling power of 60% with a reduced side lobe level. A 10-element linear comb-line antenna composed of bottleneck-shaped radiating elements and rectangular elements is designed and analysed at 274 GHz. This combination of elements in the traveling wave array resulted in achieving a sidelobe level of –16 dB and a gain of 11.4 dBi.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Antenna Placement for LoS-MIMO in HAPS Feeder Link
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The feeder link in a high-altitude platform station (HAPS) system must have a high capacity to accommodate the communication traffic of all user equipment in the service link. Given the line-of-sight (LoS) environment between the ground station and the HAPS, LoS-MIMO is an effective method to increase channel capacity in the feeder link. However, the constant changes in the position and attitude of the HAPS cause substantial performance degradation due to mobility. This study examines antenna placement for LoS-MIMO in the feeder link and evaluates its performance against HAPS mobility through simulation.

articleTitle: Wideband DoA Estimation Based on Antenna Current Green’s Function using RBF Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the concept of the antenna current Green’s function is utilized to estimate the Direction of Arrival (DoA) in environments characterized by strong mutual coupling effects and wideband signals. An RBF interpolation technique is proposed to obtain a calibration matrix effective across the frequencies of interest, and it is validated using computational methods. The antenna current Green’s function, which is used for calculating the mutual coupling components between elements of the receiving array, is employed to model the received voltage signals. An optimization process is developed to obtain the calibration matrix, which minimizes the difference between the modeled voltage signals and the ideal signals that incorporate only progressive phase delays.
