For validation, a uniform linear array consisting of 10 half-wavelength dipole antennas operating at 2.4GHz is used as the receiving antenna, and two single dipole antennas serve as the transmitting antennas. Employing the proposed method, RBF interpolation with four calibration matrices spanning frequencies from 1.8GHz to 3GHz demonstrates high resolution for DoA estimation, while linear interpolation, in contrast, yields inferior results.

articleTitle: Polarization Dependence on Delay Profile in a Conference Room at 150 and 300 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Polarization dependence on the delay profile in a conference room at 150 and 300 GHz was evaluated. The measurement of the delay profile shows that the intensities of the H-polarized waves reflected in the conference room are stronger than those of the V-polarized wave at 300 GHz. The delay spread of the V- and H-polarized waves calculated from the measurement results is 6.8 and 6.1 ns, respectively. The intensity of the reflected wave in the conference room is stronger at 150 GHz compared to that at 300 GHz.

articleTitle: Combined L-shaped Broadband Metasurface Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper focuses on the absorber that has the greatest impact on the response performance in terahertz detector structures. By combining L-shaped resonant structures, a dual-frequency metasurface absorber is proposed, achieving up to 100% perfect absorption at two resonant points, 103 GHz and 51 GHz. At a center frequency of 103 GHz, it achieves an absorption of over 80% within a 9.69 GHz bandwidth. The metasurface uses Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> as the dielectric layer, compatible with standard printed circuit board (PCB) technology, significantly reducing production cycles and manufacturing costs. The absorber achieves a certain degree of polarization insensitivity through the rotation and combination of the L-shaped basic structure.

articleTitle: Pseudo-Scale Model for Air-Freshwater Two-Layer Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper examines the possibility of applying scale models for electromagnetic fields to the air-freshwater two-layer problem. Since the conductivity of freshwater is small, a conventional scale model can be used. However, in this paper, the possibility of applying the pseudo-scale model, which has been effective for seawater and brackish water problems, is examined through FDTD calculations and tank experiments. It is found that the pseudo-scale model is applicable to the air-freshwater two-layer problem as long as the conducting medium condition is satisfied.

articleTitle: A Semi-Transmissive Cylindrical Metasurface Enabled Dual-Band Shared-Aperture DRA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Minimizing antenna size continues to pose significant challenges in various applications. This paper presents the integration of two cylindrical dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) into a compact shared-aperture configuration. We introduce two structures designed to reduce scattering and coupling, ensuring the independent operation of the DRAs despite their shared aperture. To validate our approach and optimized design, its prototype was subjected to both extensive simulations and experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Multi-beam Feed Network for Individually Steering of Multiple Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a new type of reconfigurable beam-forming network that can realize individual steering of multiple beams. The design is based on multiple tunable phase shifters and passive components like hybrid couplers, and beam steering is realized by a series of tunable reflection-type phase shifters. A 2 × 8 beam-forming network is modeled and simulated using planar microstrip lines. For verification, a prototype is fabricated and tested. Excellent matching and constant and continuous tuning phases are obtained from simulation as well as measurement. Finally, the designed matrix is employed to feed a linear array for steering multiple beams, demonstrating its capability of independently controlling multiple beams simultaneously.

articleTitle: Design of a Magneto-Electric Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact magneto-electric (ME) monopole antenna. Based on the image theory, the lateral size of the conventional ME dipole antenna is reduced by half, by placing a vertical ground plane. The ME monopole antenna was designed at 2.5 GHz. High front-to-back ratio of 20 dB and low cross polarization are observed.

articleTitle: A Study on Application Effect of RIS on Channel Capacity in Urban Macrocell Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Currently, in mobile communication systems, the use of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) has been investigated for coverage hole counterplan and communication quality improvement in the high-frequency bands (e.g. mm-waves). However, the effectiveness of RIS installation has not yet been sufficiently evaluated. This paper theoretically evaluates the general effects of RIS from the perspective of channel capacity.

articleTitle: A Novel Broadband Wide Angle-insensitive Phase Gradient Metasurface for Both Monostatic and Bistatic RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel planar phase gradient meta-surface (PGM) with wideband radar cross-section (RCS) lowering capabilities is presented. An electromagnetic (EM) simulator is used to develop and model a 8x8 sub-array in order to verify its efficacy. The simulation’s findings show that, at both normal and oblique incidence angles, the reflective metasurface greatly reduces the RCS (below 10 dB) over a broad frequency range of 7GHz to 22GHz. For both monostatic and bistatic designs, a wide range of incidence angles (-30 degrees to +30 degrees) is used to demonstrate angle-independent RCS reduction. Broadband performance, frequency insensitivity, wide incident angle tolerance, and streamlined design are qualities to point out potential uses in real-world scenarios requiring low-scattering stealth capabilities.

articleTitle: High Linearity and Low Noise mm-Wave GaN HEMT RX Frontend
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Because the output power of the power amplifier is very high in the 5G system, switches with good isolation characteristics that can withstand high power and Low Noise Amplifiers that can withstand high power are essential for the stability of the communication system. In this paper, a switch with high isolation characteristics, low insertion loss characteristics, and a Low Noise Amplifier with high linearity and low noise figure were designed and verified. The verified switch has an isolation characteristic of -32 dBm and an insertion loss of 1.28 dB. The verified LNA has a noise figure of 1.8 dB and an OP1dB of 16.7 dBm. By combining these, the RX Frontend is designed with reinforced stability. The size of the proposed single chip is 3,470x1,570 um<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the gain is 23.5 dB, the noise figure is 2.7 dB, and the OP1dB is 19.8 dBm.

articleTitle: CPW-fed Monopole Antenna with 3.5/5.5 GHz Band-Notched Characteristics for Ultrawideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This research presents a printed ultrawideband monopole antenna designed with notches at the 3.5 GHz and 5.5 GHz frequency bands. The antenna incorporates a 50-Ω Coplanar Waveguide (CPW) feed, featuring a gradual central line and ground plane. To notch unwanted frequencies at 3.5 GHz and 5.5 GHz, an inverted triangle slot and an inverted U-shaped slot are integrated into the monopole patch. Operating across a frequency range of 2.62-12 GHz, the proposed antenna supports the UWB system while excluding the 3.22-3.62 GHz and 5.14-5.62 GHz bands. The lengths of the inverted triangle and U-shaped slots correspond to quarter and half wavelengths at 3.5 GHz and 5.5 GHz, respectively. The prototype has been fully developed and tested, showing its effectiveness in reducing Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) in WLAN/WiMAX bands.

articleTitle: Effect of array antenna weight coefficient quantization in wireless power transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the effect of quantization of array antenna weight coefficients on power transmission efficiency and irradiation avoidance in wireless power transmission. The results show that about 5 bits is required for irradiation to the feeding device, whereas 7bit or 8bit is required for irradiation avoidance. Namely, a larger number of quantization bits is required for irradiation avoidance.

articleTitle: A Local Reflectivity Modulation Method for Analyses of the Clutter Sources in the Quiet Zone of CATR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The quality of the Quiet Zone (QZ) is important to the Compact Antenna Test Range (CATR) technology. It is affected by many factors including reflector edge diffraction, source direct radiation and so on, among which the reflection clutter to the QZ is difficult to distinguish and analyze. This work proposes a local reflectivity modulation method to distinguish the clutter contributions caused by the absorbing materials laid on different positions in the CATR. A numerical example is implemented for demonstration, based on a two-dimensional Time Domain Finite Difference (FDTD) algorithm. Corresponding results of fields distribution in time-domain can semi-quantitatively illustrate the contribution of the modulated area on the QZ fields.

articleTitle: A 4x4 MIMO Antenna Array for the Wi-Fi7Access Point on a Metal Wall Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: 4×4 CPW MIMO Antenna array with an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) reflector is presented for Wi-Fi7 access point on a metal wall application in the study. The 10-dB impedance of the integrated MIMO antenna array covers the Wi-Fi 7 operating bands, and the transmission coefficients are under -15 dB in the whole Wi-Fi7 bands. This proposed integrated MIMO antenna is low profile and has good total radiation efficiency (over 60%). The height of the integrated MIMO antenna array is 6.325 mm.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Circular-Polarization Switchable Stacked Microstrip Antenna Loading Cross Slot and Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dual-band circular-polarization (CP) switchable stacked microstrip antenna. The proposed antenna consists of a square patch and a cross-slot patch integrating four diodes. The CP sense in two frequency bands can be changed by the ON/OFF conditions of the diodes. The proposed antenna is designed and evaluated by simulation. The axial ratio better than 3 dB is obtained in 2.4- and 5.8-GHz band, and the proposed concept of the CP switching is confirmed.

articleTitle: Measurement-based Indoor Channel Capacity Analysis at 300 GHz for Coverage Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a high-resolution double-directional channel measurement in a conference room using an ultra-wideband in-house developed channel sounder at 300 GHz is presented. Analysis of the measurement data demonstrates that several non-trivial multipaths that could be utilized in data transmission are present. This motivates us to investigate further multi-stream propagation in the given scenario, and thus, the average channel capacity in an emulated multi-antenna system is evaluated. This paper also demonstrates a capacity enhancement with passive reflecting surfaces (PRS), which will inspire a site-specific coverage design.

articleTitle: Characterization of m x n metasurface for bandwidth extension of patch antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Patch antennas have been drawn rich attention in wireless system because of their low-profile structure, low cost and ease of manufacture. This paper discusses characterization of m × n metasurface for patch antenna in terms of bandwidth enhancement. To clarify the principle of operation of the periodic part we focused on magnetic currents. As a result, it is found that the periodic part can be divided into two parts: a coupling element and a radiating element. At the design frequency of the periodic structure, both the patch and the periodic structure radiate, but the main radiation is from the periodic structure.

articleTitle: Unlocking Operation Principle of Corner Truncated Antenna Enabling to Squeeze-out Axial Ratio Bandwidth with Thick Substrate Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Conventionally, the design of circularly polarized (CP) antennas based on single-feed patch elements has largely relied on intuitive approaches, leading to interpretations for the simulation data only. This lack of fundamental understanding of the CP antenna operation has hindered the development of systematic design methodologies. This research addresses this limitation by elucidating the operating principle of corner-truncated antennas based on the well-established TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode of linearly polarized (LP) patch antennas. A novel CP antenna design method is proposed, offering a new perspective for bandwidth optimization. Specifically, the relative amplitude and phase between the two polarizations that constitute the axial ratio (AR) formula are extracted during the design process. By controlling the AR bandwidth trajectory, bandwidth optimization is achieved. The proposed antenna exhibits an 8.5 % bandwidth centered at 5.8 GHz with a 0.1λ profile.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Vehicle Classification Using Electromagnetic Leakage Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recent studies have reported classification tasks using electromagnetic (EM) leakage signals emitted from various electronic devices. However, there have been no attempts to utilize EM leakage signals from vehicles for classification. In this study, we simulated EM leakage signals emitted from the engines of three types of vehicles and conducted vehicle classification experiments using two machine learning algorithms: random forest (RF) and LightGBM. The experiments utilized fast Fourier transform (FFT) and short-time Fourier transform (STFT) as input features. The experimental results showed that STFT features outperformed FFT features in both models and achieved the highest accuracy of 84.7% when using STFT features with the RF model. This demonstrates the feasibility of vehicle classification based on EM leakage signals.

articleTitle: Compact Frequency-Tunable Harmonic Tag with Asymmetric Spiral Loop Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Conventional passive harmonic tags lack built-in capabilities for unique tag identification. Using frequency-selective tags can solve this problem. This paper presents a compact narrowband harmonic tag design based on a spiral loop topology that is easily frequency tunable. The presented measurement results confirm the frequency selectivity of the proposed tags, supporting their potential use as true harmonic RFID.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Stackable Phased Array Antenna Integration to Enhance Beam Coverage of Millimeter-wave Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel low-cost, stackable patch antenna-in-module that incorporates two 4-element phased arrays into a single die package with a height profile of less than 1.25 mm (0.12 λ₀). By individually adjusting the weight matrix of the excitation ports, the AiP achieves three independent switchable main beam directions (±z-axes / +y-axis). The experimental and simulated results validate the AiP’s performance, showing an improvement of the spherical coverage CDF by more than 4.5 dB at the 50-percentile point compared to a reference model.

articleTitle: Wideband Bidirectional Circularly Polarized S-Slot Antenna with Dielectric Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a circularly polarized (CP) wideband S-slot antenna with a bidirectional radiation pattern, using a dielectric superstrate (DS) to increase the gain. The antenna achieves an enhance axial ratio (AR) bandwidth and reduced back lobe of radiation pattern. The S-slot antenna is positioned midway between a rectangular dielectric superstrate and an S-slot radiating element, which has a dielectric constant of ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 4.3. The DS acts as a lens, refracting the electric field to combine the antenna beam and increase the antenna gain. For performance evaluation, the S-slot radiating element without the DS was compared to the proposed antenna. The antenna size is optimized for a center frequency of 5.5 GHz. The square DS contributes significantly to the bandwidth ratio, achieving an axial ratio AR ≤ 3 dB across the design frequency range (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| ≤ -10 dB) of 4.0–6.25 GHz. This antenna design is suitable for wireless communications and 5G sub-6 GHz applications, such as in long bridge/tunnel areas, coal mines communications, radio frequency identification (RFID) systems, and various wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of a Tri-band Monopole Antenna for Multiband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)

abstract: This study introduces a tri-band monopole antenna tailored for multiband applications. It is engineered to operate at 1.67 GHz, 2.15 GHz, and 2.64 GHz, achieving respective return loss values of -22.07 dB, -24.34 dB, and -20.50 dB. This performance is achieved through the incorporation of specialized inverted L-shaped stubs. The antenna showcases commendable gain and radiation patterns, affirming its efficacy for various wireless communication requirements demanding tri-band capability.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation via SVD Denoising with Coprime Array Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel coprime array interpolation method for direction of arrival (DOA) estimation. By incorporating the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) denoising algorithm, the proposed algorithm has the capability of suppressing the impact of noise. Through array interpolation, the sparse non-uniform coprime array is reconstructed to an uniform linear array (ULA) with the same aperture. Leveraging the ideal covariance matrix properties of the ULA, which includes Toeplitz matrix and Hermitian semi-definite priors, low-rank recovery is achieved using convex optimization techniques. Simulation results indicate that the proposed denoising DOA algorithm based on array interpolation outperforms in terms of degrees of freedom (DOF) and root-mean-square error (RMSE) of azimuth estimation.

articleTitle: Square Loop Antenna Loaded with Mantle Cloak Composed of Strip Conductors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The mutual coupling reduction is required in the wireless devices. Various mantle-cloak antennas have been proposed as a method to suppress the mutual coupling. This paper presents a square loop antenna loaded with mantle cloak composed of strip conductors for horizontal polarization. The proposed antenna consists of a one-wavelength closed-loop structure. The cloaking effect can be confirmed in the electromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: Design of Subarrayed Phased Array With Uniform Beam Scanning Range
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To design the subarrayed phased array (SPA) with uniform beam scanning range, a subarray pattern difference maximization model is proposed. It can find the optimal feeding phase inside regular subarrays by maximizing the subarray pattern differences in different azimuth sectors collaboratively. Thanks to the uniform beam scanning range characteristics, the designed SPA can either expand the minimum beam scanning range by 13° or increase the boresight directivity by 2.3 dB.

articleTitle: Preliminary study of generalized UTD solution of PEC half-plane diffraction by spherical wave excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Analyzing EM waves using the UTD solution requires all relevant UTD coefficients to model diffraction effects from geometric discontinuities. The original UTD for PEC wedge geometries does not fully account for all polarization components. Previous research proposed adding transition region terms to the UTD solution for this purpose, but it was limited to plane wave excitation and did not present results. Therefore, this research study aims to ad hoc modify the UTD solution of the previous research by comparing it with the original UTD formulation to address spherical wave excitation. Accurate results from this ad hoc modified UTD solution are discussed in this research study.

articleTitle: Investigation of Conductive Fabric for Unfurlable Mesh Reflector Antenna Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this letter, the conductive fabric which can be employed for the reflecting surface of an unfurlable reflector antenna structure is investigated. The reflection and transmission coefficients are measured under the laboratory conditions using pairs of waveguides with WR187 and WR90 dimensions. The absorption and reflectivity were calculated based on the measured S-parameters, and considering the absorption from the conductive fabric, the commercially available mesh was found to possess approximately 90% reflectivity at frequencies of 5.4 GHz and 8.2 GHz.

articleTitle: A Quasi-Isotropic and Uniformly Polarized Ultracompact Wireless Power Source for Energizing Battery-Free Internet of Things Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: With the rapid development of wireless power transfer (WPT) technologies, battery-free Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices have become feasible and attractive. WPT enables single wireless power source to energize multiple IoT devices that are dispersed around it. This paper introduces a novel quasi-isotropic and uniformly polarized ultracompact wireless power source that is facilitated by a pattern reconfigurable electrically small Huygens dipole antenna (HDA). It consists of a reconfigurable capacitively loaded loop (CLL) with a PIN diode as the magnetic dipole, an Egyptian axe dipole (EAD) as the electric dipole, a reconfigurable short driven dipole with a PIN diode, and several switching components and circuits. By controlling the status of the two diodes, broadside and backfire Huygens patterns can be switched. This is realized as the phase of the electric dipole is altered by 180° by changing the coupling between the CLL and the EAD. The prototype was fabricated and measured. Throughout the entire space, the co-polarization gain variation is less than 6.9 dB. As an electrically small antenna with uniform polarization, it is an ideal candidate as a transmitting power source for WPT-enabled IoT applications.

articleTitle: Characteristics of window penetration loss (WinPL) and its impact on building entry loss (BEL) from 3 to 40 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, measured results of window penetration loss (WinPL) and their impact on BEL were analyzed in the 3~40 GHz band for 13 types of glass windows. Traditional double-glazed windows exhibit odd harmonic periodic oscillation characteristics due to properties of the multilayer dielectric. The WinPL of thermally -efficient windows is on average 20 dB higher than that of the traditional windows due to the metal coating layer and does not exhibit regular oscillation characteristics. In thermally-efficient buildings, WinPL contributes significantly to the BEL, while it does not significantly affect the BEL in the traditional buildings. In order to improve the BEL models in the future, it is necessary to develop appropriate and relevant parameters for traditional and thermally-efficient buildings based on these analysis results.

articleTitle: Position and Polarization Effect Analysis on Received Power of Vehicular Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study investigates the effects of polarization and antenna position on the received power of a vehicular antenna using simulations with a simplified minivan model. The cumulative probabilities of the received power are evaluated by changing the position and orientation of a dipole antenna at 1 GHz. When the antenna is installed inside a car, horizontal installation exhibits better power than vertical installation. However, vertical installation is superior when the antenna is installed above the window height.

articleTitle: Center-fed Microstrip Antenna Array Fed by Slotted Broadband Transition from SIW to Two MSLs in 300-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A center-fed microstrip antenna array (MSAA) fed from a broadband transition between a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and two microstrip lines (MSLs) is proposed in 300-GHz band. A radiation slot was formed on the proposed transition. Radiation from the slot is controlled to obtain uniform aperture distribution. Two 20-element MSAAs fed by the transition achieved the simulated realized gain of 12.9 dBi at 256.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Pattern Synthesis of Spherical Phased Array Antenna Based on NSGA-II Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An X-band spherical phased array antenna (SPAA) along with a multi-objective optimization pattern synthesis algorithm suitable for SPAA is proposed in this paper. The SPAA consists of 47 dual-circularly polarized microstrip antenna elements with a central frequency of 9.5 GHz, capable of transmitting and receiving left-hand circularly polarized and right-hand circularly polarized electromagnetic waves, respectively. Additionally, a multi-objective optimization pattern synthesis algorithm based on the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is designed for this structure. This algorithm achieves a gain fluctuation below 1 dB, side lobe level below -12 dB, and axial ratio below 1.3 dB for the SPAA at elevation angles from 0 to 90 degrees when the number of elements is 47.

articleTitle: Design of three-element periodic metasurface and its application in wideband low RCS antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a low RCS antenna loaded with a hexagonal periodic AMC surface is proposed, which is composed of multiple circular AMC elements, rectangular AMC elements and circular AMC elements. A low RCS antenna consisting of a hexagonal periodic AMC surface and a bottom-fed microstrip antenna is designed for verification. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna achieves RCS reduction in the frequency band range of 8-40GHz, the frequency range of RCS reduction covers the whole band range from X-band to Ka-band, and the RCS reduction in the frequency range of 12.5-35.5GHz is more than 5dB, and the relative bandwidth of 5dBRCS reduction is about 95.8%. The RCS reduction of 10dB was achieved in the 18.5-31GHz band range, and the relative bandwidth reduction of 10dBRCS was 50.5%.

articleTitle: Doppler Spectrum Generation Method Considering Unsteady Moving Scatterers in V2V Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communications have been studied as technology to realize automated driving. To realize a reliable wireless communication system, a propagation model suitable for V2V communications is necessary. V2V communications have a characteristic that both the transmitting and receiving points move, which is different from cases that one of the transmitting and receiving points moves. This paper proposes a method to generate Doppler spectrum on a computer, considering unsteady moving objects around the transmitting and receiving points. By using the proposed method, it is possible to evaluate the influence of large frequency shifts caused by moving objects other than the transmitting and receiving points, and this method is highly useful for the design of V2V communication systems.

articleTitle: Ultimate Performance of Microwave Ablation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Microwave ablation is a therapeutic procedure to eliminate abnormal tissue within a body selectively. One type of ablation, hyperthermia, is achieved by selectively raising the temperature at the target. This work identifies the fundamental bounds of the efficiency for hyperthermia and the sources to achieve them. The performance of such an optimal source exceeds that of existing solutions by 9.1 dB. The optimal source for hyperthermia is physically realized with an 11 × 11 dipole array, the performance of which closely approaches the bound.

articleTitle: A Novel Analysis of Asymmetric Partially Reflective Surfaces Based on the BCITL Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel analysis of asymmetric partially reflective surfaces (PRSs) using the bi-characteristic-impedance transmission line (BCITL) model. The PRS is made of a double-sided single layer of compact-microstrip-resonant-cell (CMRC) unit cells to achieve the positive reflection phase gradient in the desired frequency band for wideband gain enhancement. Numerical results are illustrated to show the effectiveness of the PRS analysis using the BCITL model with an additional physical insight.

articleTitle: Streamlined Characterization Methodology for Chip-Level Antenna Performance : Electrical and Mechanical Analysis and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new class of characterization methodology for assessing chip-level antenna package performance. The comprehensive analysis and study cover the electrical characterization through the power equivalent loss model, and the influence of mechanical errors, particularly die-shift. In addition, simulated and experimental results of the electrical (insertion loss) and mechanical (die-shift) analysis exhibit conclusive validation of the proposed evaluation methodology. Moreover, it establishes a framework for optimizing antenna design for enhanced efficiency and reliability across a broad frequency range of communication, radar, and sensing chip-level applications.

articleTitle: Current Control for Receiver Power Allocation of Omnidirectional Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a current control method for receiver (RX) power allocation in an omnidirectional wireless power transfer (WPT) system. In systems with multiple RXs, overall efficiency improves by delivering more power to the RX with higher coupling, often resulting in insufficient power for lower coupled RXs. We propose a TX current control method to allocate the required power among multiple RXs and investigate the power allocation boundaries in a specific WPT environment. The validity of the method and the analysis of power allocation boundaries at 6.78 MHz were confirmed through circuit-level simulations.

articleTitle: Frequency-Diverse Computational Imaging System Enhanced by Synthetic Aperture Radar Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Computational imaging (CI) has been recently proposed as an alternative to conventional synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems. CI systems rely on antennas radiating a set of spatially-incoherent patterns, enabling a physical layer compression of the information from the scene. This, in turn, simplifies the hardware layer of the imaging system while, at the same time, provides a fast data acquisition speed. This work studies the impact of considering the information from several acquisition positions on the quality of the images retrieved with a CI system. The measurement results obtained with a frequency-diverse CI system show that combining the information from a reduced number of acquisition positions yields a significant improvement on the quality of the retrieved images. In particular, considering approximately two orders of magnitude less samples than those required by a SAR system, high-resolution images with a reduced clutter level can be obtained.

articleTitle: Identification of Human Emotion Based on Speaking Using Convolutional Neural Network Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The use of voice in data science has been widely employed in numerous studies, including investigation into human, animal, and object generated sounds. One illustrative example of human voice in data science is the identification of emotion through speech, which produces a range of expressions, including anger, sadness, boredom, disgust, anxiety, and happiness. In this research, sound detection is conducted on human speech using the Emo DB dataset, which is then processed using a system designed on Google Colab and analyzed by the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method. The system built is capable of recognizing six emotions: anger, sadness, boredom, disgust, anxiety, and happiness. To extract features from sound, zero-crossing rate (ZCR), root mean squared error (RMSE), and Mel frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) are employed. CNN classification method exhibit flexible performance. CNN method is a development of Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), which is used to process two-dimensional data. It is anticipated that CNN method will be able to detect and recognize the six emotions that have been labeled on the Emo DB dataset with 93% system accuracy.

articleTitle: High Gain and Low Gain Roll-Off Mechanically Beam-Steerable Transmitarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of offset unifocal phase symmetry the achieve mechanically beamsteerable transmitarray (TA) antennas with high gain and low gain roll-off. The proposed offset unifocal phase symmetry operations can compromise phase error, electric-field spillover and illumination efficiencies to maintain the gains of scanning beams and minimize the gain roll-off. It has been demonstrated that the mechanically beam-steerable TA antenna enabled by the offset unifocal phase symmetry can maintain the realized gains of scanning beams, suppress sidelobe levels, and reduce gain roll-off within the beam-steerable coverage compared with the counterparts of unifocal and bifocal mechanically beamsteerable TA antennas. The proposed offset unifocal phase symmetry operations, in principle, is a generalized approach and applicable to reflectarray antennas to improve beamsteerable performance as well.

articleTitle: A Study of MIMO Antenna Array Control for Estimating Multi-Person Locations and Vital Signs based on 3D mm-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In most conventional radar-based remote heart rate measurements, the subject is stationary and there is a single target. When remote heart rate estimation is performed for multiple targets, they are located in different range bins. Therefore, this paper proposes a new remote heart rate estimation method when multiple targets are in same range with 3D MIMO radar. The proposed method estimates the same-range targets’ locations and chest positions, and using point cloud detects the heart rates of with 3D beam steering. Experimental results show that the targets’ signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) were improved, and average errors of the heart beats are about 0.065 Hz (3.9 BPM).

articleTitle: Wideband Reconfigurable Proximity-coupled Patch Antenna with Highly Flexible Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Reconfigurable antennas that combine wide bandwidth with extensive polarization switching capabilities are challenging to develop, yet they are highly beneficial for future smart wireless systems. This paper presents the development of a novel proximity-coupled patch antenna designed to achieve high polarization switching flexibility over a wide operating bandwidth. Specifically, the antenna can switch among twelve linear polarizations (LPs) and dual circular polarizations (CPs) across an over 20% overlapping bandwidth. Full-wave simulations and thorough measurements of the fabricated prototype verify the antenna performance. Notably, it is the first time to facilitate more than 20% impedance bandwidth with such extensive LP and CP switching flexibility within a single antenna element.

articleTitle: Low-Loss and Compact Design of Microstrip-Line-Fed Rotman-Lens Beamforming Network in 300-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact and low-loss microstrip-line-fed Rotman lens beamforming network (BFN) was designed in 300-GHz band. The distance between the input and output ports was 1.13 mm, downsizing the lens section to minimize losses in the lens. Simulation confirmed that more than 60% of input power is transmitted from the central port to all output ports. Uniform amplitude and phase distributions were obtained in the design at 300-GHz band.

articleTitle: Dual-Band, Dual-Polarized Metasurface utilizing a Thin Liquid Crystal Layer at 28/39 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Nematic liquid crystal (LC) is a competitive material poised to replace semiconductor diodes and RF MEMS to enable reconfigurable devices in the mmWave band. However, existing tunable devices using LC have been limited to single band and single polarized operation up to present, and sluggish response due to the electrically thick LC layer. In this paper, a dual-polarized reconfigurable metasurface is designed by implementing a symmetrical structure with biasing using vias. Moreover, by employing the strong coupling of the patch and cross-slot array, an electrically thin LC layer of 10 μm is achieved. The proposed structure is designed to exhibit a phase difference of 180 degrees around 28 and 38 GHz.

articleTitle: Multifunction 7-axis Robotic Antenna Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A multi-functional 7-axis antenna measurement system was implemented by using robots for antenna measurement. A high level of positional precision was secured, and repeatable and precise measurement results were obtained even in the sub-THz band of up to 500 GHz. Measurement application programs that can support various purposes such as dielectric constant measurement and array antenna evaluation were also developed. The antenna gain of a W-band standard gain horn was evaluated, and it was confirmed that the system's measurement precision had achieved the world's highest level. KR-MANMS will continue to be improved to respond to various measurement technologies currently required in the communications and defense industries.

articleTitle: A Unidirectional Radiation Antenna With Water Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a unidirectional radiation antenna with four water layers is designed. The dipole is used as the radiation element, the water layers of different thickness is used as the reflector and dielectric resonators respectively. To adjust the filling states and bending angle of the water layers, the antenna can realize the change of gain and the deflection of the pattern. The antenna is designed, machined and measured, the relative bandwidth of antenna is 20%, the maximum gain is 8.9dBi and the radiation efficiency is 70% at 2.5 GHz.

articleTitle: L Band Array Antenna Design for Data Collection Satellite Payload
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An L band antenna for the communication satellite at geo-stationary orbit 128.2°E, to be launched in 2027, is being developed to provide data collection service. This paper presents the design results of the qualification model array antenna for the satellite payload. It has helix radiating elements and a beamforming network. Before design phase for the antenna level, a single element and a diplexer were fabricated and measured to verify the design method. Good agreement between simulation and measurement was confirmed. To meet the gain requirement, the 13 helical elements for the array antenna was chosen. The designed antenna has greater than 20.4dBi at receiving frequency and 19.7dBi at transmitting frequency over the coverage area.

articleTitle: Beamforming at 26/28GHz for 5G Networks: Array Antennas and Rotman Lens Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper focuses on developing a new arrangement for beamforming networks, which are connected to an array antenna, to control the direction of the beams. The goal is achieved by connecting the 3 x 8 array antenna arrangement with the 3 x 3 Rotman lens beamformers. The central temporal delay line is roughly 18 millimeters in length. This design enables coverage of +20 degrees to -20 degrees. The antennas are spacing with half wavelength (λ/2), the gains are at 8.65 at 26 GHz and 12.4 dBi at 28 gigahertz (GHz), and the reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) stays below -10 decibels (dB). The final design of the beamforming networks produce a gain of 16.4 dBi. In this paper the Roger 5880 substrate is used, which has a dielectric constant of 2.2, a loss tangent of 0.0009, and a thickness of 0.508 mm.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized and Fully Conformal Antenna using Stacked Semi-Elliptical Shaped Polyimide Films
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A multilayer conformal dual-polarized antenna (ML-CDPA) with bending performance in all directions is presented. The antenna consists of a supporting ground plane and four identical radiating elements. Each element comprises two semi-elliptical-shaped polyimide films with patches stacked together to achieve 20% bandwidth. The ML-CDPA is designed for L-band and tested for the flat case as well as conformed to a cylinder with 200 mm, 160 mm, 150 mm, 100 mm, and 80 mm radius.

articleTitle: Experimental Polarizability Extraction of a Waveguide-fed Tunable Metamaterial Element using SIW Characterization Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present a method for the experimental extraction of effective polarizabilities of a metamaterial radiator using characterization circuits and a thru-reflect-line (TRL) algorithm. The metamaterial element considered in this work is an electrically small aperture formed with a varactor-tuned, complementary-LC element inserted into the top wall of a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW). We confirm experimentally the dipolar description of the element by extracting the Lorentzian-constrained effective polarizability using the proposed characterization circuits.

articleTitle: Radiated Immunity Test for Platform Screen Door(PSD) Sensors Using Broadband Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: With the advancement of mobile communication technologies, the use of smart devices, including mobile phones, has increased. To accommodate the growing data capacity, digital modulation techniques such as OFDMA are being used across wide frequency bands. Despite the rise in malfunction cases caused by these broadband signals, current radiated immunity tests are conducted using AM signals based on IEC 61000-4-3 standards. This paper proposes a testing method utilizing mobile communication broadband signals to address the recent malfunction issues of Platform Screen Door (PSD) sensors and verifies the impact of these broadband signals

articleTitle: Analysis on Degree of Symmetry in Both Legs with Walking Motion using a Compact Radar Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For this article, we analyze degree of symmetry in both legs with walking motion of an individual by using a compact continuous waveform Doppler radar. Generally, time-varying Doppler frequencies of both legs in a spectrogram includes two main parameters such as step length and radial upper leg length. Thus, the degree of symmetry in both legs can be presented as a function consisting of main parameters, so it can lead to efficient non-contact walking motion examination of patients undergoing rehabilitation training. In experiments, the degree of symmetry in both legs of an individual was efficiently analyzed from several walking motions.

Author Keywords: degree of symmetry in both legs

articleTitle: Agile Reconfigurable Pin-diode Integrated Flexible Antenna for Vehicle-to-Everything Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A pin-diode integrated flexible multiband antenna for vehicle-to-everything (V2X) applications is presented in the following manuscript. By dynamically switching the pin diode states (and subsequently the surface current density), the radiation pattern and frequency can be reconfigured based on the user’s need. The pin diodes are directly etched over the radiating patch and can be controlled by a cost-effective microprocessor. The proposed flexible antenna shows |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>|< - 10 dB bandwidth operation at 3.4 GHz – 3.8 GHz and 5.3 GHz – 8 GHz, encompassing commercially valuable 3.65 GHz (802.11y), 5.5 GHz WLAN, 5.8 GHz ISM, and 5.9 GHz V2X band. The proposed antenna is compared with previously suggested antenna designs by comparing frequency reconfigurability, compactness, conformance, and pattern diversity, and a comparison demonstrates the prospects of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave/Sub-Terahertz Absorber/Reflector/Radome Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work introduces wideband passive-device designs, including an absorber, a reflector, and a radome, for millimeter-wave/sub-terahertz applications: A radio-wave film-type absorber is essential to reduce cavity resonance at the packaging or module fabrication level and can be adopted for a 77-GHz automotive radar or a 150-GHz/300-GHz wireless system. A 300-GHz band-pass-filtered reflector can expand wireless communication coverage with antenna beam forming/steering abilities. Finally, a radome protects antennas and ICs, realizing low-insertion loss (minimum loss lower than 1 dB) at the desired frequency (300 GHz).

articleTitle: Influence of Water on Propagation for Future G-Band 6G Communication Systems Using THz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: THz spectrum is unexplored spectrum and has potential to being revolution especially in communication systems. However, its extreme high frequency properties raise questions about propagation mechanisms within current environments, presenting ongoing challenges. Therefore, this paper investigates the impact of transmission loss caused by water within the G-band spectrum which is proposed for the 6G communication system. Through measurement conducted with THz spectroscopy and analysis, it was shown that transmittance levels increase in proportion to the wetness level in the sponge.

articleTitle: The Practical Real-time Radar Processing for Obstacle Detection on The Railway Track
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper considers the MIMO radar processing to detect and track the obstacles on the railway track, where a high rate of real-time processing is necessary. Since there exist many obstacles located outside the detection area in this environment, the typical constant false-alarm rate detector usually detects all of such undesired obstacles. This requires a higher computation workload in the next steps of processing (Angle Fast Fourier transform, clustering, and tracking) and hinders the high rate of real-time radar processing. Therefore, this work proposes a detection approach that can suppress the power of rangevelocity spectrum bins caused by the reflection waves generated by the obstacles existing outside the detection area to reduce the consequent computation workload after this detection block. The measurement result verified such merit.

articleTitle: Eight-port MIMO Slot Antennas for Wi-Fi 7 Access Point Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper presents an 8 × 8 MIMO access point antenna designed for use in the Wi-Fi 7 frequency bands. The 8 × 8 MIMO antennas use microstrip lines to excite inverted open L-shaped slots and closed step-width slots for the frequency bands. The antenna material used in this experiment is glass fiber board (FR4), with a dielectric constant of 4.4, loss tangent of 0.0245, and thickness of 1.6 mm. The overall dimensions of the design are 100 × 100 × 34.45 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and 50-ohm SMA connectors connected to microstrip lines are used to excite the antenna, and with a distance of 31.25 mm between the MIMO antennas and the reflector. From the results, the design can cover all bands of Wi-Fi 6E/7. Therefore, this antenna is suitable for use in Wi-Fi 6E/7 MIMO antennas on access point applications.

articleTitle: GNSS L1/L2/L5-Band Patch Antenna with Proximity Quad Quadrature Coupled Feed
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a circular patch antenna, which is excited by four proximity L probes each with quadrature phase difference. The feeding network, placed below the antenna, delivering power to the L probe through vias, consists of four output ports. Each output port maintains a 90-degree phase difference with equal power amplitude with respect to the next output port across frequencies. The feed network consists of a broadside coupler and two Marchand baluns to fulfill the design requirement for ensuring good circular polarization. It is designed in stripline configuration to reduce the signal loss and facilitate strong coupling. The mechanical structure adopts an aluminum frame as the main support and is fixed by a M6 screw. This lightens the weight while maintaining the stability and strength. The simulated results of the integrated antenna show that the realized gains in the L1 (1575.42 MHz), L2 (1227.6 MHz), and L5 (1176.45 MHz) bands are 4.0 dBic, 4.2 dBic, and 3.3 dBic, respectively. The VSWR is less than 2 in all three bands, and the axial ratio (AR) is remarkably less than 2 over the entire band. Its wideband and stable circular polarization properties make it highly suitable for GNSS applications.

articleTitle: Design of a wideband microstrip antenna fed by an L-probe with double-layered radiation elements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents design of a wideband microstrip antenna (MSA) fed by an L-probe with double-layered radiation elements. The proposed antenna consists of double-layered square radiating patches and a feeding L-shaped probe (L-probe) above the ground plane. Air layers are assumed between the top patches and the ground plane. The radiating patches are excited by the L-probe with electromagnetic coupling. The design frequency of the proposed antenna is around 0.6 GHz. The structural dimensions such as the size and the height of the two patches and L-probe are tuned by using the electromagnetic simulator. The total height of the proposed antenna is set to 50 mm. The simulated results reveal that triple resonance characteristics with a fractional bandwidth of 43.0% of less than −7.4 dB reflection (VSRW = 2.5) are observed. In comparison with the conventional MSA with a single-layer radiating patch and almost the same height, the fractional bandwidth and the broadside gain in the above bandwidth are improved by approximately 5.6% and by at most 0.6 dBi, respectively. It is also confirmed by the simulation that the cross polarization of the H-plane pattern is reduced by about 3 dB at the lower frequency in the bandwidth.

articleTitle: On-Body Performance Analysis of Wearable Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed on-body performance analysis of wideband wearable antenna for 5G applications. The proposed design (antipodal vivaldi antenna structure implemented on a polyimide and polyester combined substrate) showed excellent performance in free space with a bandwidth of 910 MHz (covering 5G-NR Bands like n48, n77, and n78). Afterward, since the antenna is wearable, it is required to perform efficiently near the human body. Consequently, a detailed on-body analysis was conducted, and the antenna radiates efficiently. SAR has been assessed to make sure of the safety of the wearer; throughout the entire bandwidth, the SAR value remains within the safety regulation of ICNIPR, threshold 2W/kg per 10g of tissue.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the IEMI Effects on Drone IMUs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Due to the commercialization of drones, specific research on the evaluation or response of radio wave effects is required, and the demand for these technologies is increasing from both industry and academia. This paper aims to evaluate the electromagnetic effects of the drone component Pixhawk.

articleTitle: Angular Selective in Periodic Structures: Performance, Methods, and Prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Periodic structures such as frequency selective surfaces, absorbers, and polarization conversion surfaces have received extensive attention due to their distinct amplitude and phase responses in the frequency domain. These studies have led to excellent performance characteristics and effective design methods. However, the dimension of angle as a control factor for plane electromagnetic waves has not been fully explored. This paper discusses angular selective engineering in periodic structures, providing a comprehensive overview of both performance and implementation methods. Finally, it concludes with a discussion on the future research directions in angular selective within periodic structures.

articleTitle: Compact superdirective array with beamforming capability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a compact, wide-band and efficient superdirective antenna array with beam-forming capability in the azimuthal plane for a 5G wireless home gateway. The antenna architecture is designed to operate in the 5G NR n28 frequency band between [758-803 MHz] with a compact form factor with respect to the operating wavelength (λ = 384 mm) of 0.38λ×0.38λ×0.39λ. The optimized antenna enables the coverage of the four main directions of the horizontal plane with a directivity greater than 8 dBi, a total efficiency greater than 80% and a wide impedance bandwidth of 16.6%.

articleTitle: RCS Estimation of Chaff Cloud Based on PO
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Traditionally, long and thin rectangular metal fragments are employed for the chaff cloud. This cloud area is very large, so that numerical matrix methods such as FDTD is almost impossible for radar cross section (RCS) calculation. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the scattered field from individual pieces of metal and then superimpose them to estimate the RCS in the chaff distribution space. The scattered field from a flat metal plate can be easily calculated using physical optics (PO). Their arrangement is twisted relative to each other, so an appropriate coordinate transformation is required. This arrangement can be generated using standard statistical distributions.

articleTitle: Measurement and Modeling of Basic Transmission Loss in Factory Environments at 300 GHz frequency under LOS conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we conducted measurements and modelling of basic transmission loss for indoor factory environments at a frequency of 300 GHz. The measurements were carried out along line-of-sight (LoS) paths in various factory environments, including a ship repair factory, a ceramic and metal injection factory, and a dental implants factory. Prior to measuring the basic transmission loss, we verified the measurement system. Free-space loss was measured in anechoic chamber and compared with theoretical free-space loss for validation. Power loss coefficients for basic transmission loss were then modeled form the extensive dataset gathered. The results show that the power loss coefficients are close to 20, even considering reflection effects from metal machinery.

articleTitle: Analysis and Measurement of a Novel Rectenna Array Crossing a Loop and Dipole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study introduces a novel rectenna array that combines a dipole antenna with a loop antenna, using a rectifying diode as the dipole and two LEDs as the loop. The simulated electromagnetic field distribution clarifies the differences between this new design and the conventional crossed dipole antenna. It also offers insights into extending wireless power transmission distance through the arraying of the rectenna, based on magnetic field distribution analysis. An experiment was conducted to illuminate the LEDs using a smartphone’s Wi-Fi tethering as the wave source, with results closely aligning with the analytical predictions. We also measured the S-parameters using a vector network analyzer (VNA) to evaluate the wireless power transmission efficiency for each rectenna element, confirming that the trends matched the analytical results.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Human-Body Ranging Using Wi-Fi CSI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a human-body ranging method using Multiple-Input Single-Output (MISO) Wi-Fi radar, and reports its experimental evaluation of ranging accuracy. The proposed method estimates the path length from the transmitter to receiver via human-body based on Time-Of-Flight (TOF) calculated by Wi-Fi’s Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) channel. The experimental result shows that the distance estimation error was 1.34 m in the proposed method, and improved by 2.05 m compared with the authors’ previously proposed technique.

articleTitle: A Metasurface-based Triple Band Transmittive type Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This manuscript presents a metasurface as a linear to circular polarization (LP-to-CP) converter designed on a single 1 mm thick dielectric substrate with triple operating bands. The unit cell comprises diagonally arranged metallic loops in both the layers of the substrate surrounded by a larger square ring while each of the diagonal elements consists of three distinct square loops. The CP conversion has been realized at three distinct frequency bands i.e., 7.05-9.16 GHz, 16.40-20.76 GHz, and 23.46-24.93 GHz offering respective 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidths of 26.25%, 23.5%, and 2.2% in comparison to the center frequencies. The anti-clockwise rotation of the electric surface current implies the left-handed CP nature in all the frequencies of interest.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Reconfigurable Beam Scanning Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Based on electronic modulation technology and polarization conversion principle, a wideband and high-efficiency 1bit reconfigurable beam scanning transmitarray antenna is proposed in this article. The upper patch of the proposed unit cell is used to receive x-polarized electromagnetic (EM) waves and conduct it to the lower patch that radiates y-polarized EM waves by two metal vias. A relative transmission bandwidth of 39.2% (23.8 GHz to 35.4 GHz) with a transmission amplitude greater than -1 dB is realized. The fan-shaped microstrip line eliminates the coupling effect of the bias line on the high-frequency performance of the unit cell. Finally, wideband 1bit transmission phase manipulation is realized by selecting the conduction path of the induced current in the ring connector through the PIN diode "on" and "off" states. To verify this work, a transmitarray antenna composed of 30 × 30 units and working at 28 GHz has been designed. The simulated results demonstrated that the transmitarray antenna can achieve beam scanning from 0° to 30° in the two-dimensional plane with a gain reduction of no more than 0.3 dB.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of 3-D Magnetic Flux Leakage for External and Internal Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of 3-D magnetic flux leakage (MFL) resulting from defects, utilizing precise wire rope modeling with finite element model (FEM) simulation. Conventional 3-D MFL techniques often rely on simple dipole models and idealized cylindrical wire rope models, primarily focusing on external defects. In contrast, this study incorporates the consideration of stranded wire rope angles to enable accurate interpretation of the MFL signal in an oblique manner with considering both external and internal defects.

articleTitle: A Beamwidth-Controllable Millimeter-Wave Antenna Array With Spatial Variable Orthogonal Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A reconfigurable dual-polarized antenna array system featuring wide-range continuous beamwidth control (WCBC) is developed based on polarization-mixing method. By simultaneously exciting dual polarizations, the total power pattern can be controlled with a wide range from 21°to 100°. Moreover, the polarization mixing method results in a novel spatial variable (SV) polarization, which means the polarization varies with spatial angle. To maintain the polarization diversity, a pair of sub modes with same pattern are designed to generate a pair of SV polarizations that are orthogonal to each other. In this manner, the proposed system can achieve wide-range beamwidth control and a new form of dual-polarization. Moreover, the system retains its beam scanning capabilities when the two polarizations are used separately. Notably, all elements are fully excited, eliminate the necessity for amplitude modulation, ensuring the high overall efficiency of the system.

articleTitle: Dual-Wideband Transmissive Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design for a novel single-layer, dual-wideband linear-to-circular polarization converter. The unit cell features two identical, diagonally oriented C-shaped metallic strips, integrated with four outward-extending diagonal parasitic strips that enhance polarization conversion. Positioned on an ultra-thin single substrate, the converter achieves a 90° phase shift for polarization conversion across two frequency bands centered at 11.5 and 30.7 GHz. It also operates effectively over two distinct frequency ranges: 6.45 to 16.72 GHz (a fractional bandwidth of 89.3%) and 25.06 to 36.35 GHz (36.7%). The converter delivers consistent polarization performance over a wide range of incidence angles and high transmittance at both operating frequency bands.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Environment Impacts on AOA-Based Indoor Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: There have been many studies on indoor localization using a super-resolution angle-of-arrival (AOA) estimation method, such as the Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm. Addressing the challenges presented by multipath propagation in practical environments, several studies have explored spatial smoothing techniques to improve AOA accuracy in a coherent environment, but algorithm tuning is still an important issue. In this study, an extensive measurement campaign confirmed the efficacy of spatial smoothing in enhancing AOA estimation. The results revealed that the environment significantly impacts localization errors, providing valuable insights into improving indoor localization accuracy, especially in practical indoor environments.

articleTitle: Isolation Improvement of LO-IF Port and RF-IF Port on Microstrip IQ Mixer by using Open Stub Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: One figure of merit of the IQ mixer is the isolation between all ports. This paper presents an open stub technique to improve signal isolation between the LO-IF port and RF-IF port on a microstrip IQ mixer with the center frequency of the LO signal at 5.5 GHz and a requirement bandwidth of 150 MHz for the RF signal. This technique utilizes the characteristic of an open stub transmission line with the length of a quarter wave signal that will act as a bandstop filter for LO and RF and have low attenuation for IF signal at 75 MHz. The experimental result shows that S21 of one open stub configuration at LO frequency can reach -32.2 dB, S21 at RF frequency with bandwidth 150 MHz is below -22 dB, and 3 dB bandwidth attenuation in a range of from 4 GHz to 7.4 GHz. Moreover, by cascading two open stubs the S21 value can further improved to -49.742 dB at LO frequency and below -46 dB for RF frequency. This technique can reach a high isolation and wide bandwidth.

articleTitle: mm-Wave/sub-THz Hemispherical Far-Field Measurement System supporting Various Testing Scenarios: Research Survey and Possibility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a recent research work on the streamlined hemispherical far-field antenna measurement systems supporting various testing scenarios across the millimeter-wave/sub-terahertz (mm-Wave/sub-THz) spectrum. Three use cases of distinctly different antenna types and feed interfaces are investigated utilizing this measurement system with multi-functionality and cost-effectiveness. Particularly, simple fixturing methods of the sample holder and anti-vibration metallic weights of the rotary stage are used in the proposed far-field system to enhance the measurement accuracy and cost-effectiveness despite maintaining the multi-functionality. Three use cases are demonstrated utilizing each exemplified sample. Finally, the main features and further research possibilities for real-life demonstrations of typical mmWave/sub-THz antenna module applications are discussed.

articleTitle: Multibeam Radiation Patterns of Positive and Negative Index Lens Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A negative refractive index (NRI) lens antenna is known to produce a thinner lens shape compared to a conventional lens antenna. Utilizing an NRI lens antenna is expected to yield a good multibeam characteristic. To achieve these multibeam results, the optimal feed position should be determined using a focal region ray tracing method. For different refractive index values √2.17 and -√2.17, the focal region rays of the hyperbolic-planar lens for both positive and negative refractive indices are obtained. The locus of the best feed positions is identified. The multibeam radiation pattern is then determined using an electromagnetic simulator for both positive and negative lenses. Based on the multibeam results, a negative refractive index lens, which is thinner than the conventional lens, is capable of performing excellent wide-angle beam scanning.

articleTitle: Basic Study on Near-field Range Migration for Millimeter-wave 2D-MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The main objective of our research is to construct a security system using millimeter-wave 2D-MIMO radar to check the possession of dangerous objects such as knives and guns. In our previous study, to realize 3D imaging by the radar, we used the Beamformer method. The method is based on the three-dimensional Fourier transform (3D-DFT), hence it is time-consuming for analyzing large areas and/or detailed imaging. Another factor that increases the computational time is that the larger the number of virtual elements in the MIMO radar. In security applications of the MIMO radar, targets locate in the near-field region, hence far-field approximation which can speed up calculations is not applicable. Therefore, in this paper we apply the range migration algorithm to the imaging processing by using the T-shaped MIMO radar, and evaluate computational efficiency by the algorithm.

articleTitle: Measurment Result of Broadband Reflectarray Antenna by Controlling Phase Center of Primary Radiator for Space Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Reflectarray antenna consists of a horn antenna as the primary radiator and a reflector made of flat surfaces. It is cheaper and easier to make than a parabolic antenna. On the other hand, it has the disadvantage of narrow bandwidth at frequencies other than the design frequency due to phase errors in the aperture plane. Therefore, we verified a measurement that cancels out the residual aberration by controlling the phase center position of the primary radiator with a far-field measurement method. Wideband reflectarray antenna using this method is described, and the validity of this theory is verified from the measurement results.

articleTitle: Estimation Method of Bistatic Scattering Field for Reflectarray with Various Angle of Incidence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Reflectarray has gained attractive attention to reduce coverage hole in 5G. Reflectarray is evaluated by the bistatic radar cross section (RCS). However, the measurement of bistatic RCS with various incidence angles is time consuming. This paper presents the estimation methods for bistatic RCS with various angles of incidence. Our proposed method is based on monostatic-bistatic equivalent theorem. The monostatic RCS is firstly measured to calculate scattering coefficients as equivalent current source of the reflectarray. By using scattering coefficient with simple calculation, the bistatic RCS of the reflectarray with various incident angle can be predicted, even though monostatic RCS measurement with only one time. The validation of the estimation method is demonstrated by the measurement results of the reflectarray.

articleTitle: A Compact UWB ±45 ° Dual-polarized Rectenna based on DC Combining
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact UWB ±45 ° dual-polarized rectenna suitable for Internet of Things (IoT) applications is proposed in this paper. The novel approach of introducing a special feeding structure and distinctive curved stubs is primarily aims to improve the impedance matching with isolation performance and to obtain miniaturization features of dual-polarized dipole antenna at the same time. Simulation results indicate that the introduced rectenna is highly efficient in converting ambient RF energy into DC power, functioning effectively over a broadband range of 1.8-3.6 GHz. To put it differently, the suggested energy harvester shows significant potential for application, especially for the case with various polarization feature of incoming waves, low level of input power and a high demand for DC output power.

articleTitle: Toward Reproducing actual 5G MIMO OTA Field in the Lab: Capturing and Simulating 5G Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper aims to discuss methods for reproducing 5G MIMO OTA (Over-The-Air) tests from real field conditions in Lab. By using a 5G UE (User Equipment) and Anritsu AirMonitor equipment, 5G signals are captured in real field environments. These captured signals are then utilized to create channel models and test scripts. The proposed method involves applying these outputs to the Anritsu base station emulator MT8000A and performing radiation tests using an RTS (Radiated Two-Stage) chamber.

articleTitle: Pattern synthesis of leaky wave antenna including feeding system
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Leaky wave antenna radiating cosecant-squared patterns proposed by adjusting the first element position is affected by the feeding structure such as parallel plate waveguide. This paper introduces the position adjustment of the second and the third strip elements in addition to the first one to control the cosec<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> pattern precisely. The proposed design method is demonstrated for 28GHz antenna.

articleTitle: GPU Accelerated Shooting Bouncing Rays–An Enabler for Future Radar in the Context of Autonomous Driving and Aerospace & Defense
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a new technology that could accelerate the development of radar in Autonomous Driving and Aerospace & Defense (A&D). By leveraging Ansys Shooting and Bouncing Rays (SBR) solver and GPU enabled High Performance Computing (HPC), we can accurately predict performance of radar systems in very large and complex scenarios in real-time. This technology allows time and cost reductions for radar development and overcomes the challenges of obtaining real-life data where trial launches and measurements are not always possible.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-Based Complementary Ring Resonator for Sensing of Anaemia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A metamaterial-based microwave resonator is presented in this paper for the detection of anaemia. The 20×30 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> design consists of a transmission line integrated with the circulatory patch with four complementary rings. The transmission coefficient of the sensor varies when the permittivity of blood is increased due to anaemia. Response of the design under blood’s normal dielectric characteristics was set as a reference and a mathematical model was developed using regression analysis. The R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.9838 was obtained based on resonance shift. The designed resonator due to high quality factor can detect the change in blood’s permittivity and loss tangent at 15 MHz per unit increase.

articleTitle: A Rate-enhanced Square-wave LoRa Backscatter Communication Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The characteristics of LoRa signals give them the ability to transmit over long distances, therefore LoRa has been used in combination with backscatter to increase the communication distance. However, existing LoRa backscatter schemes suffer from rate limitation. In this paper, we propose to improve the data rate by using a combination of digitally synthesized LoRa square wave and high-order quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) at the tag. The design of the scheme using 16QAM is explained in detail in the paper and the feasibility of the scheme is verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Generation of Spatio-Temporal Propagation Path near Human Body in 300 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to simulate spatio-temporal propagation paths between a user terminal and a relay device such as a wearable terminal in 300 GHz bands, treating a direct wave and human body scattered waves as deterministic paths, and other scattered waves as stochastic paths. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the proposed method was verified by measuring arrival angle profiles using a measurement system with a rotating reflector antenna as the receiving antenna, and it was shown that the proposed method can accurately reflect the influence of the human body on the propagation path.

articleTitle: Illuminated Spot Size Reduction of Near Field Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
