abstract: Due to the expected demand for wireless power transmission, radio waves must be transmitted efficiently in near-field region. The illuminated spot size is restricted by the regulation for the safety, and near field pattern shaping is required. This paper presents near field pattern synthesis to minimize the spot size for planar array used for 24GHz short range power transmission.

articleTitle: An Experiential Study of CDE(Cable Discharge Event) Phenomenon
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A cable discharge event (CDE) is a phenomenon that occurs when a cable and an electronic device are connected, the electric charge in the cable moves to the electronic device with a low resistance path for a short period of time due to the potential difference, causing a malfunction in the electronic device. CDE are occurred when electronic devices and cables are connected. Therefore, every electronic device experiences at least one time of CDE when combined to a system. In this paper, we show the CDE experience that has been damaged to electronic devices caused by CDE. And we also show a method to reduce the possibility of damage to electronic devices due to CDE.

articleTitle: Investigation of Space-Time Approach for Background Reduction in Millimeter-Wave FMCW MIMO Radar Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study investigates the efficacy of a space-time algorithm in mitigating background interference in frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar imagery. Addressing this challenge is crucial to minimize target omission and to reduce the false detection rate. The approach consists of background identification in the f-k domain and suppression in the space-time domain. Realistic measurements were conducted in a scenario involving a single target in continuous back-and-forth motion. The results demonstrate an effective mitigation of the strong signal due to the colocation of the transmitting and receiving antennas as well as the clutter due to the stationary targets present within the experimental environment.

articleTitle: Scattering Modulation Method Based on Antenna Self-transceiver Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a scattering modulation method based on antenna self-transceiver characteristics is proposed, by analyzing the conversion mechanism of incoming space electromagnetic waves and the guided waves in the antenna system, combining the regulation of the guided waves in the system and achieve the precise regulation of the antenna mode scattering field.

articleTitle: A Wideband Tunable Filtering Phase Shifter with Continuous Phase-Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband tunable filtering phase shifter (TFPS) is presented in this work. The proposed phase shifter uses parallel coupled line stepped impedance resonator (SIR) structure to form the wideband filtering path. The open-ended stub is loaded at the port to introduce a transmission zero (TZ). The tunable part of this work is realized by a tunable phase shift unit (TPSU), which is composed of several varactor diodes at the end of the coupled line. Through analyzing phase characteristics of TPSU and its effect on the circuit, it can be deduced that the phase shifter could control phase shifts continuously. For validation, a wideband TFPS has been designed with an operating frequency range from 1.12 GHz to 2.63 GHz, the simulated results show that this design can control phase shift continuously of more than 180° within wideband fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 80%

articleTitle: Sensor Characteristics of Geosynchronous Synthetic Aperture Radar System for the Constant Sptatial Coverage over the Ground
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper examines the sensor characteristics and performance of GSO-SAR systems designed to permanently observe the area of interest. A geosynchronous orbit was designed to cover the area of interest. The system characteristic variables and SAR parameters were carefully chosen to avoid deviating too far from what the state-of-the-art technology can offer. A more reliable analysis of the GSO-SAR system was conducted by combining performance estimation and SAR simulation.

articleTitle: An in-situ Array Antenna Diagnosis Method Using Optically Modulated Scattering Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Array antennas have been applied in various domains. In order to measure the practical performance of array antennas, it is necessary to determine the operating states in situ. In this paper, an in-situ measurement of array antenna using the optically modulated scattering technique was proposed. A Ka-band array antenna was measured. The operating state of each element can be accurately determined from the near-field distributions. The proposed method has the potential to diagnose complex array antenna arrays due to its high-resolution advantage, which can be used in the in-situ diagnosis.

articleTitle: An Embedded Scheme-Based Dual-band Shared Aperture Base Station Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-band shared aperture base station array based on the embedded scheme, with mitigated cross-band scattering performance. Through inserting innovative helical filters into low-band (LB) radiators, the adverse impact on high-band (HB) antennas caused by close-placed LB antennas is largely restored, across a wideband of 1.36-2.72 GHz (66.7%). Despite matching difficulties brought by the helical filters, the developed LB antenna achieves successful matching in 0.8-0.96 GHz (17%). This is attributed to the specially designed LC series circuits integrated into the LB baluns. Moreover, the incorporation of helical filters extends current paths and enables a compact aperture size of the LB antennas. This leads to enhanced in-band isolation. Consistency between simulations and measurement results in the fabricated array validates the effectiveness of this design.

articleTitle: Design of Chip-Based D-Band Microstrip Coupled Line Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the chip-based D-band microstrip coupled line power divider. To balance the output signal, Metal6 is designed with boundary coupling and Metal5 is composed of stacked coupling to increase the area of boundary coupling, which ensures that the transmission loss can be reduced to maximize the signal transmission and maintain a stable output. The bandwidth of the proposed power divider is 157 - 170 GHz. After inputting signals into the input port, two balanced signals of equal phase and size can be output. The lowest transmission loss of 4.41 dB, the output power imbalance of 0.02 dB, and the chip size of 0.2312 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> are measured, which makes it suitable for the application in the 6th generation mobile communication devices.

articleTitle: Equivalent Electrical Conductivity Measurement Method of Conductive Surface Using Power Delay Profile in Reverberation Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method using the power delay profile of the reverberation cavity as a method for measuring the equivalent electrical conductivity of the conductive surface. The proposed method is verified through numerical analysis simulation. In the future, the accuracy analysis of the proposed method and verification through actual measurement will be performed.

articleTitle: Development of Proximity-Coupled Fed IBFD Filtering Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper deals with the development of an In-Band Full-Duplex (IBFD) filtering antenna (filtenna) which is fed by a proximity-coupled feeding method. The performance optimization of IBFD systems is focused by evaluating and comparing two IBFD antennas: one without a filter, and another one with a filter, both utilizing proximity-coupled feeding method. The integration of filters and the use of proximity-coupled feeding methods are essential for enhancing antenna performance, particularly in terms of self-interference cancellation and bandwidth response. The IBFD filtering antenna is designed on FR4 Epoxy substrates to operate at the frequency of 2.4 GHz. Simulation and measurement of key performance metrics are conducted to provide insights into the benefits and limitations of filters integration and proximity-coupled feeding method utilization in an IBFD antenna. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of filtering in suppressing undesirable frequencies and improving signal isolation, highlighting the importance of advanced antenna design techniques in optimizing the performance of IBFD system.

articleTitle: Tri-band Minkowski Island Split Ring Resonator Patch Antenna for WLAN and 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This research investigates the effects of the Minkowski Island split ring resonator (MI-SRR) on the patch antenna. Initially, a Minkowski Island patch antenna design, Antenna A, was created in the CST Microwave Studio. Incorporating different diameters of the MI-SRR on the substrate resulted in three distinct resonant frequencies, shown as in Antenna B and Antenna C. This tri-band antenna performs best at 2.40 GHz, 3.52 GHz, and 5.22 GHz of resonant frequencies, with return losses of -21.945 dB, -17.154 dB, and -16.536 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Power Delay Profiles in the Vicinity of Human Body at 300GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Delay profile characteristics at 300 GHz in the vicinity of the human body were evaluated in order to realize the virtualized terminal technology that increase the uplink speed of 6G mobile communication. In case Rx is set next to the right ear, delayed waves due to reflections at the cheek and chest were observed in addition to the direct wave. The delay spread was approximately 0.030 ns, with little difference observed between cases with and without wigs. In case Rx is placed on the wrist, the reflection waves at the wrist and abdomen were observed and the delay spread was about 0.033 ns.

articleTitle: Challenges and Recent Advances towards Real-Time UAV-mounted GPR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) systems on board Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are able to detect buried targets while avoiding the contact with the soil. Therefore, they are a promising solution for the detection of buried explosives, such as landmines. This contribution discusses some challenges that this technology must face to enable its usage in real operational scenarios. Furthermore, recent advances to overcome these limitations, mainly related to low acquisition speeds and high computational complexity, are also presented.

articleTitle: Generation of a Long-Nondiffractive-Range Leaky-Wave Bessel Beam through an Open-Stopband Mitigation Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Bessel beams maintain their focusing properties only up to a finite distance known as nondiffractive range. Efforts are needed in any frequency range to increase this distance as much as possible. In this work, an innovative leaky-wave wideband Bessel-beam launcher with a very extended nondiffractive range has been designed in the microwave range by exploiting an openstopband mitigation technique. In particular, at the working frequency of 30 GHz (λ = 1 cm), an impressive nondiffractive range of 10m has been reached with a planar, cost-effective, single-feeder structure having an aperture diameter of about half a meter. Full-wave results show that the launcher radiates Bessel beams at a distance that is 20 times its aperture diameter.

articleTitle: Acceleration Method of Antenna Calibration For Fully Digital Radar using OFDM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In modern radars, electronic beam steering using phased-array antennas is prevalent to achieve rapid beam steering response times. However, if the phase values differ from those that control the phase of each individual element, the performance of the antenna radiation pattern will degrade (antenna gain reduction, sidelobe level increase). Initially, during antenna manufacturing, calibration table is obtained to compensate for phase offsets due to manufacturing process errors, etc., using near-field measurements (off-line calibration). Real-time phase calibration (on-line calibration) is essential to compensate for phase errors caused by changes in RF device characteristics, such as temperature changes, during radar operation. A common transmitter phase calibration method involves constructing an individual calibration line for each array element and detecting the transmitter phase of the array element using the signal coupled to the calibration line as a result of the antenna array element transmission [1] . This paper presents a method and experimental results for accelerating the transmitter calibration of a fully digital phased-array antenna using OFDM.

articleTitle: Orientation Angle Estimation of Buildings and Streets in Urban Areas Using PolSAR Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR) has attracted attention in the field of earth observation. The scattering power decomposition, which is one of the PolSAR data analysis methods, can classify the earth surface targets based on the physical scattering mechanism. However, this technique has a problem of misclassification in urban areas where building walls and/or streets are not parallel to the observation orbit. In this paper, we propose a method to estimate orientation angle of them in urban areas by using a rotated dihedral model. In addition, a quantitative analysis on the estimation error of the azimuth angles is also provided.

articleTitle: Parallel Differential Line Fed Planar Aperture Antenna-in-package with X-shaped Patch in Multilayer Substrate at 300-GHz band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a parallel differential line feeding planar aperture antenna in multilayer substrate for use in 300-GHz band. The X-shaped patch enables feeding parallel differential line and excites polarization perpendicular to the signal lines. Double resonance is generated by the X-shaped patch and apertures in each layer. Moreover, the beamwidth can be controlled by the aperture in the top layer.

articleTitle: Input Impedance Reduction Techniques for the Resistive Dipoles on Printed Circuit Board
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study investigated methods to reduce the high input impedance of a resistive dipole antenna with the Wu-King profile. The resistive dipole antenna has a high reflection coefficient due to its high input impedance, which is largely dependent on the permittivity of the PCB substrate and the width of the antenna arms. We designed a resistive dipole with a resistance per unit length of R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> = 3337.5 Ω/m. We show that for the resistive dipole with a width of 3.2 mm on a PCB with a dielectric constant of ϵ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>= 4.4, the input impedance is improved by approximately 165 Ω compared to the case with ϵ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 1.0 and a width of 2.0 mm.

articleTitle: Frequency Reconfigurable Frequency Selective Surface based on PIN diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a frequency reconfigurable frequency selective surface (FSS) based on PIN diodes. By utilizing the forward and reverse bias characteristics of the PIN diode, combined with a simple periodic arrangement of square metal patches, the switching between two passbands has been successfully achieved. When the PIN diode is in the forward bias state, the -1dB passband is in the 8.3 - 11.6 GHz frequency range; when the PIN diode is in the reverse bias state, the -1dB passband is in the 6.1 - 6.8 GHz frequency range. This frequency selective structure can play an important role in the fields of communication, radar, antenna design, and wireless power transmission.

articleTitle: Near-field Localization for Coprime Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel two-phase near-field localization method for the symmetric coprime array is proposed which comprises two spare uniform linear arrays (ULAs). First, to extract the target angle information from the covariance matrix of the received signal, we utilize the one-dimensional (1D) multiple signal classification (MUSIC) method to obtain candidate target angles with respect to each decomposed subarrays. Then, the unique target angle is determined by exploiting the coprime property. Next, given the estimated target angle, the target rang is estimated by performing the 1D spectrum search with one decomposed sparse ULA. Finally, numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed near-field localization method.

articleTitle: Estimation of Shielding Effectiveness of Steel Fiber Reinforced Concrete Under Percolation Threshold
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper aims to simulate and predict the shielding effectiveness of reinforced concrete with steel fiber concentration below the percolation threshold. First, simulation results were obtained for a low steel fiber concentration of 0.01%. As the steel fiber content increases, the fibers connect, lowering the resonance frequency range. This characteristic was used to develop a method for predicting the shielding effectiveness for higher fiber concentration without significantly increasing the computational load. The predicted results were then compared with measurements for a fiber concentration of 0.1%.

articleTitle: A Basic Study of Ghost Vital Signs Removing for Non-contact Human Vital Signs Sensing based on mm-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In human vital signs sensing using radar, in addition to actual vital signs, ghost vital signs are detected by multiple reflection on furniture, walls, and pillars in indoor environment. In this paper, we propose a simple removing method of the ghost vital signs for the non-contact vital signs sensing based on mm-wave radar. We focus on the ghost features, 1) same cardio waveform and 2) longer range than the real. The proposed method thus measures ranges and waveforms of vibrated targets, and calculates correlation matrix between all the measured heartbeat waveforms. The vital sign, which is one of high correlation pairs and is in most short range, is removed as ghost. A simple experiment shows that the proposed method can find a ghost having high peak-to-peak intervals correlation in the heartbeat waveform with that of a real target and also has longer range, in an indoor environment.

articleTitle: Design of 3D Low-scattering Carrier with Controllable Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Radar cross section (RCS) measurements using a low-scattering metal support require the background response of the test site, and the low-scattering carrier is used to wrap the turntable at the top of the support, thus reducing the scattering of the turntable. Typically, the low-scattering carrier consists of parameterized surfaces and provides sufficient internal space to accommodate the turntable. Considering the low-scattering characteristics and spatial size limitations, this paper designs a parameter-controlled three-dimensional low-scattering model. The model’s back-scattering performance in the P-band was calculated using the method of moments, which showed lower RCS values compared to typical ogival body. The simulation results demonstrate that the design methodology of the low-scattering carrier presented in this paper has considerable application value.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Field for Dispersive Media Using Symplectic Integrator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The symplectic integrator (SI), widely used in quantum and classical physics, as a stable and reliable numerical method, was applied to electromagnetic field analysis of metals with frequency dispersion. The reflectivity of a dielectric slab of Au was computed and compared with the exact solution.

articleTitle: Low-Sidelobe Design of Intelligent Reflecting Surface Using Liquid Chrystal
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, low sidelobe design of Liquid Crystal-based Intelligent Reflecting Surface at 47 GHz band has been demonstrated. It is found that both the large phase change of over 360 degrees, the constant reflection magnitude change is important to obtain low sidelobe scattering pattern used for IRS applications such as 5G communications.

articleTitle: A Dual Antenna Pair Design for Wi-Fi 7 Laptop Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a small size dual antenna pair (DAP) for Wi-Fi 7 laptop operations in the 2.4 GHz (2400–2484 MHz), 5 GHz (5150–5875 MHz), and 6 GHz (5925–7125 MHz) frequency bands. To excite three resonant modes, ensuring complete coverage of the Wi-Fi 7 operational bands, each single antenna element of dimensions 14.8×4.0 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is composed of a modified folding inverted-F antenna (MF-IFA) and a meandering stub. To allow better isolation level between the two antennas, a T-shaped protruded ground structure is loaded between them. This DAP design offers several advantages, including small size and low profile, making it well-suited for modern laptops with thin frames or narrow bezels.

articleTitle: A Broadband of Elliptical Microstrip Antenna for C-Band CP-SAR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle and small spacecraft applications make extensive use of the CP-SAR C band. This paper describes a parasitic circular polarization antenna design with a broadband axial ratio. The antenna is designed to operate at the 5.3 GHz center frequency. The antenna radiator and parasitic elements are designed using an elliptical antenna microstrip. Circular polarization is accomplished by adjusting the ellipse’s axis, which is rotated 45 degrees relative to the feeding line. Broadband antennas are produced by attaching six parasitic elements to the left and right sides of the radiator. Based on the simulation results, the simulation impedance bandwidth and axial ratio bandwidth are 480 MHz and 156 MHz, respectively. According to the simulation results, the designed antenna has a high axial ratio and can be used with the CP-SAR sensor.

articleTitle: Detection of UAV in a Clutter Environment using Pulse Doppler Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Globally, the market size for drones and small unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has increased rapidly. Due to the development of unmanned aerial vehicle manufacturing technology and low development costs, the scope of use is increasing not only for military purposes but also for civilian purposes. These UAVs can be greatly utilized in various other industrial fields such as delivery services, broadcasting, safety inspection, and leisure business. However, on the other hand, it has many risk factors such as terrorism, accidental or intentional invasion of privacy, and security threats to public institutions. In this paper, as a measure against these threats, we introduced a chirp pulse radar system that can be used to detect small drones and verified the drone detection ability using this system.

articleTitle: A Parallel Plate Waveguide Measurement Technique for Characterizing Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a parallel plate waveguide (PPW) system to characterize frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) in microwave frequencies. The setup includes two metallic sheets placed parallel to each other with a feeding source at each end that provides a wideband impedance matching. The dimensions of the sheet have been varied gradually to minimize the edge radiation effect, whereas the thru-reflect-line (TRL) calibration technique has been carried out for accurate measurement. Three different FSS geometries, one bandstop, one bandpass, and one broadband absorber have been considered, and their scattering parameters have been determined. The responses have been compared with those of the unit cell simulated responses, and good agreement are observed in all cases, thereby validating the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed PPW system.

articleTitle: Effect of ground gradient on road-to-vehicle radio propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, radio propagation simulation based on ray tracing simulation are carried out to investigate the effect of ground gradient on radio propagation. The results show that in the Line-Of-Sight (LOS) environment, the effect of the gradient is small even if the position of the transmitting point is changed. In the Non-Line-Of-Sight (NLOS) environment, the effect is increased as the distance from the transmitting point is increased.

articleTitle: RFID-UAV Displacement Acquisition based on Tag Antenna Array and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a spherical unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) combined with UHF radio frequency identification (RFID) and machine learning algorithms for the UAV displacement acquisition of stationary UAV applications. Unlike vision and satellite positioning techniques, this paper proposes an economic RFID intelligent displacement acquisition method that can monitor the small and random deflections of UAV. The surface of the drone is uniformly affixed with 9 RFID passive tag antennas operated at 920 MHz in a circular tag antenna array, and an RFID reader is placed on the ground in order to analyze the array Received Signal Strength Indication (RSSI) within interrogation footprint. To analyze RSSI value due to UAV random displacement, the data is divided into four classes by the difference in direction: displacement to the north direction is class 1, displacement to the south direction is class 2, displacement to the east is class 3, and displacement to the west is class 4. Our dataset has about 4000 RSSI data, and we trained a model with the machine learning Random Forest algorithm, which can be used to predict the state of UAV with newly collected data. The results show that the model has a good accuracy rate of about 93%, much higher than other algorithms' accuracy of only about 80%.

articleTitle: Ka-band Up/downconverter for High-altitude Platform Station (HAPS) for Emergency Aid
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the system planning for a Ka-band up-down converter to be used in high-altitude platform station (HAPS). The cellular signals from end-users received by the HAPS will be up-converted to Ka-band to establish a direct link to a ground station and down-converted back to cellular signals to resume transmission in the back haul. The HAPS can replace damage base stations and thereby strengthen the robustness of mobile communication system during emergency. The schematic of the up-downconverter will be briefed introduced.

articleTitle: Analysis of Target Motion on Range Estimation in Single-Pulse Narrow-Band FMCW Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: When the pulse interval is sufficiently long, the range estimation bias caused by the target motion is not neglectable. In this paper, considering the single-pulse narrow-band FMCW model, we investigate the influence of the target motion on range estimation. Under the uniform motion assumption, we analytically show that the ratio of the range bias to target velocity is only related to the carrier frequency and the frequency modulation slope, and an equivalent time is defined to explain its physical meaning. Simulation results prove the effectiveness of the analysis.

articleTitle: An Overview of Self-Powered Reconfigurable Metasurfaces (SPRM): A Brief Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This overview explores the tailless information-energy metasurface (IEMS), a novel approach for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). The IEMS integrates real-time electromagnetic modulation capabilities with energy collection and rectification circuits, eliminating the need for an external power supply. Compared to traditional reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), the IEMS offers a self-powered operation and a simpler structure. These advancements have the potential to revolutionize various applications in SWIPT and beyond.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: Direction of Arrival Estimation Using a Transmitarray and a Single Antenna Element
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper deals with a direction-of-arrival estimation (DOA) using an optimized transmitarray and a single receiving antenna. The transmitarray consists of 1-bit elements with 0° and 180° transmission phases. The transmission phase distribution was optimized using a genetic algorithm. The accuracy of the DOA estimation is almost the same as that of the DOA estimation system using a 3-element linear array antenna.

articleTitle: A Novel Low-Profile Ka-Band Circularly Polarized Double-Folded Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile Ka-band circularly polarized double-folded transmitarray antenna (CP-DFTA) is proposed. The proposed CP-DFTA consists of the polarization rotation reflection surface (PRRS) on the bottom, the integrated transmission-reflection (ITR) unit and the linearly polarized (LP) feed horn on the top, and the LP to CP converter above the ITR. The proposed ITR unit is based on the Fabry-Perot structure with only a double-layer dielectric substrate, when the simple C-shaped ring in the middle. Moreover, the PRRS is achieved by using only a metal strip rotated by 45°. This double-folded design converts the LP spherical wave from the horn antenna into a plane wave through double-folded reflection, PRRS twisting twice, ITR receiving, and through transmission phase modulation, which then passes through the LP to CP converter to ultimately radiate the left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP) wave. In this way, the antenna profile can be further reduced to about 1/4 of the focal length. Meanwhile, the simplicity of the proposed structure greatly reduces the design difficulty. The results show that the proposed CP-DFTA, with an overall size of 9.7λ × 9.7λ × 2.1λ (at 29GHz), achieves a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 20.7% (26-32 GHz) with a maximum gain of 24.8 dB at 30 GHz. Moreover, the 3-dB AR bandwidth is 13.1% (26.5-30.2 GHz) and the lowest axial ratio is 1.7 dB at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Iterative Weight Calculation for Beamforming with Broad Nulls in Microwave Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Microwave power transfer (MPT) facilitates long-distance power transfer through electromagnetic wave propagation. However, concerns about human safety and potential damage to electronic devices from electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure have limited wider adoption of MPT. In this study, we introduce a low-computational-cost iterative weight calculation for beamforming with broad nulls for MPT. Computer simulations reveal that the proposed method effectively reduces EMF exposure while also lowering computational costs compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: Time Domain Analysis of Scattering Waves by MoM Combined with Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Compressed sensing is applied to time-domain analysis of electromagnetic waves by using the method of moments. Compared to the original method, the computational time is reduced with the compressed matrix and the same accuracy is maintained.

articleTitle: Dispersion analysis of quasi twist-symmetric structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We explore the dispersion properties of quasi-twist-symmetric structures using the multimode transfer-matrix method. Unlike periodic structures, these aperiodic structures do not have a translation periodicity because they are formed by translation and rotation by an angle s2π of a given subunit cell, being s an irrational number. In this work, this structure is exemplified by a pin-loaded coaxial transmission line, and it cannot be directly analyzed using commercial software due to the lack of periodicity. The results indicate that the dispersion diagrams of this kind twist-symmetric structures lie between the dispersion diagrams of periodic structures with similar rotation angles.

articleTitle: Low Scan-loss Multi-beam Lens Antenna Fed by Horns with Separated Phase Centers in E/H-planes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a wide-angle beam-scanning multi-beam dielectric lens antenna fed by horns with separated phase centers in E/H-planes by different wall heights. The positions of the phase centers of the horn antenna in the E/H-planes are designed independently of the wall heights. In the proposed antenna, these phase centers are aligned at the focus position of the lens separated by astigmatism. Furthermore, the primary pattern for the lens is optimized by the horn aperture size. The proposed antenna with a separated phase center improves the directivity in wide-angle directions. Then, this antenna can realize a multi-beam lens antenna with wide-angle beam scanning.

articleTitle: Metaloop Antenna with Upgraded Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a triband circularly polarized (CP) metaloop antenna. Firstly, an enlargement factor, n, is defined. Secondly, it is confirmed that a metaloop antenna operates as a dual-band counter CP antenna, even when the enlargement factor exceeds four (n > 4). Thirdly, parasitic conducting patches are inserted into the open space within an enlarged metaloop, thereby creating tri-band CP operation.

articleTitle: A Shared Aperture Antenna Array Fed by Diplexer Integrated Power Dividers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a diplexer based on microstrip lines periodically loaded electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) is proposed. In the stopband, the EBG property is used for achieving high isolation, while in the passband, the electromagnetic wave travels along the microstrip line in the form of quasi-TEM mode. The proposed diplexer has low passband loss and large stopband bandwidth in X and Ka bands, which is used for dual-band shared-aperture microstrip patch antenna array. It can feed the antenna array with a single input port and a simple feeding network. The antenna gain reaches 16.65 and 22.07 dBi at 9.9 and 30 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: Body-of-Revolution Electromagnetic Particle-in-Cell Simulations on Unstructured Meshes for Modeling Lunar Magnetic Anomalies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The Lunar Magnetic Anomalies (LMAs) interact with the solar wind, leading to various particle behaviors. In certain regions of LMAs, the kinetic effects of particles become significant. This study investigates these phenomena using Body-of-Revolution Electromagnetic Particle-in-Cell (BORPIC++) simulations, which model 3D scenarios in an axisymmetric framework efficiently. BORPIC++ treats particles as charge rings, with updates based on the Lorentz force and modified Maxwell’s equation. Simulations tested particle interactions with external magnetic fields in three regions, showing successful modeling of particle dynamics and suggesting BORPIC++'s potential for LMA studies.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband 3-Dimensional Self-Complementary Antenna and Its Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel ultra-wideband three-dimensional (3D) self-complementary antenna solution aimed at enhancing the properties of a planar self-complementary antenna (SCA). The antenna under consideration is produced by the integration of a loop antenna with a slot antenna, drawing inspiration from the stitch pattern observed in a baseball. The proposed antenna can be constructed in both hexahedral and spherical forms. The hexahedral 3D SCA exhibits an exceptionally wideband characteristic of 47.3:1. Moreover, the ultra-wideband 3D SCA is produced in a hemispherical form on the ground plane specifically designed for installation in unmanned aircraft vehicles (UAVs). To validate the antenna’s performance, it is mounted on a scaled-down UAV model and its performance is assessed to confirm its suitability.

articleTitle: A THz Reconfigurable Reflectarray Element Design Based on CMOS Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a 1-bit reconfigurable reflectarray (RRA) element design based on the CMOS technique in terahertz (THz) frequency range. A switch is designed in 65nm CMOS process and the TRL calibration on the chip is applied to extract the equivalent impedance of the switch in THz frequency range. The RRA element design is guided by the microwave network theory in order to match the CMOS switch. The simulation results of the elements demonstrate the 1-bit performance of equal amplitude and 180° phase difference at 287 GHz.

articleTitle: A Series-fed Microstrip Patch Antenna Using Modified Polyimide for Sub-THz Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the sub-THz frequency band, a serious problem arises due to the increased transmission loss. To design an efficient series-fed microstrip patch antenna suitable for high frequencies, it is crucial to adopt an optimal substrate to minimize conductor loss and dielectric loss. In this paper, a modified polyimide-based 8-element series-fed microstrip patch antenna (SFPA) is designed and verified through simulation. First, the optimal substrate thickness was analyzed using 50 Ω microstrip lines to minimize transmission losses. In addition, radiation efficiency according to substrate thickness was analyzed through EM simulation using a single-patch antenna operating at 122.5 GHz. Finally, an 8-element SFPA was designed with the optimal substrate thickness obtained through simulation, and 15.3 dBi gain performance was confirmed as a result of the simulation.

articleTitle: Scattering of Non-classical Lights in N-port Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this conference paper, we analyze the scattering of non-classical lights in a N-port system. Specifically, the coincidence probability for (i) unentangled N-photons incidence and (ii) two-photon entangled pair incidence to a generic N-port system are mainly investigated. By introducing a permanent operator of a scattering matrix for a given N-port system, mathematical expressions for the coincidence probability are formulated.

articleTitle: Stable Discrete Mixed Fourier Transform (DMFT) in Split-Step Parabolic Equation (SSPE) for Long-range Electromagnetic Propagation Modeling Over Ocean Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A split-step parabolic equation (SSPE) with a stable discrete mixed Fourier transform (DMFT) is introduced for the modeling of long-range electromagnetic propagation over ocean surfaces. Our DMFT approach utilizes the difference equation with a mixed coefficient, and the initial coefficients of the general solutions are determined using the endpoints of normalized fields. Numerical computations based on realistic atmospheric environments are conducted to ensure that the two-way DMFT-SSPE remains stable and efficient even for small discretization steps and a large number of sample points.

articleTitle: A Dual Broadband Substrate Integrated Waveguide Dielectric Resonator Antenna with T-Slot for 5G mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A broadband Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) fed with higher order mode using a T-slot is proposed. The dielectric resonator has a dielectric constant of 10 with loss tangent of 0.002 and is etched on Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrate having a thickness of 0.254mm and relative permittivity of 2.2 with loss tangent of 0.0009. This antenna exhibits a dual band behavior with impedance bandwidth of 5.07GHz (25.35-30.42 GHz) and 1.11GHz (34.15-35.26 GHz) and broadside stable radiation pattern. The design provides peak gain of 8.5dB at 26.3GHz, 7.8dB at 27.4GHz, 6.8dB at 28.5GHz, 9.2dB at 34.8GHz and radiation efficiency of more than 98%. The effect of feeding on the bandwidth, S11, gain, radiation efficiency and radiation pattern are examined and analyzed. It is suitable for 5G mm Wave applications.

articleTitle: Planar and Conformal Microwave Metasurfaces Based on the Field Synthesis Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Planar and conformal metasurfaces for scattering and radiation applications are presented, based on the field synthesis method. Total tangential fields are constructed and optimized to make the metasurfaces passive, while achieving specific functionalities such as plane wave-to-surface wave conversion, invisibility cloaking, and leaky-wave radiation. Characterized by spatially modulated surface impedances, they are realized using arrays of subwavelength meta-atoms. Physical metasurface designs are validated with simulation and/or experiment.

articleTitle: Point-to-Point Reflector Design for Illuminating Designated Region at 28 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a new method for designing a passive reflector to effectively and uniformly illuminate a designated region, termed the point-to-point reflector design method. A simulation is conducted to evaluate its performance. The results demonstrate that the point-to-point reflector outperforms common-shaped reflectors in terms of uniform coverage at the frequency of 28 GHz. Subsequent error optimization further refines the performance of the designed reflector, ensuring a more stable solution.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction Considerations for 2×2 and 3×3 Sparse Microstrip Patch Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reviews how recent advancements in sparse antenna arrays optimization help reduce mutual coupling, even in simple setups like 2×2 and 3×3 microstrip patch antennas Uniform Rectangular Array (URA). It discusses and compares techniques and widely used optimisation methods to enhance array analogue beamforming performance and minimise interference through side-lobe reduction. The study shows that careful positioning and use of optimisation algorithms can help not only maintain the array gain, but also reduce inter-element coupling, making it useful for very basic array configurations.

articleTitle: Circularly-Polarized Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces for Arbitrary Beam Shaping
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We hereby propose a circularly-polarized reconfigurable intelligent surface that can synthesize complex far-field patterns, which would typically require independent amplitude and phase control of the local reflection coefficients. The proposed unit cell is structurally symmetric and includes varactor diodes, allowing circular-polarization operation and continuous local phase manipulation over nearly 300°, with relatively low loss. By leveraging a genetic algorithm in the synthesis of radiation patterns, we showcase the versatility of the proposed surface through the numerical demonstrations of (i) anomalous reflection and (ii) arbitrary beam splitting.

articleTitle: Out-of-band radiation for antenna array transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This investigation is over the issues of the transmitted signal linearity of a 4×4 antenna array for 28 GHz operation while in different beam steering direction. Not only simulating antenna array’s out-of-band radiation of beamforming, some position dependent phenomena are confirmed with the measured results of actual 4×4 antenna array. As including environmental temperature effect, it is worthy of notice that when the antenna array is beamforming at 0 degree with 20 dB signal attenuation, its linearity is comparably worse than that of the other beamforming angle. The possible root cause of such phenomena was evaluated and confirmed by measuring the adjacent channel power ratio of the nearby angle for a single column of the antenna array fed with Anokiwave IC only at a time.

articleTitle: Sampling Method for Planar Near-field to Far-field Transformation using Gaussian Process Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The near-field to far-field transformation method is a well-established measurement technique that achieves high-accuracy far-field antenna radiation patterns from near-field data. However, this method is often time-consuming. This paper proposes an efficient sampling method using Gaussian process regression to calculate far-field data. By employing 86% undersampled near-field data with a sampling interval exceeding the limits set by the sampling theorem, accurate far-field radiation patterns can be derived through a limited number of Gaussian process regression iterations.

articleTitle: Connection Ratio Improvement for 300-GHz-Band Wireless Links during Local Downpours via Link-Disconnection Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, a classification model was developed to predict instantaneous interruptions in 300-GHz-band fronthaul connections 1 min before they occur during a local downpour. We investigated a method to prevent instantaneous interruptions during local downpours by switching the route between remote antenna unit (RAU) and baseband unit (BBU) in advance. Using 1-min rainfall intensity data for the Tokyo area, we calculated the received power per minute for each wireless link. Then, a machine-learning-based classification model was developed to predict the connection status of the link 1 min ahead by using the received power data 1–15 min before the current time. Cross-validation results showed that the accuracy of the developed classification model was approximately 93%. By using the predicted connection status to switch the route between RAU and BBU, we successfully prevented more than 1000 instantaneous interruptions during a 30-min local downpour.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Printed Coded Metasurface for Split Beam Generation in Arbitrary Direction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band metal-dielectric printed coded metasurface operating at f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>=20 GHz and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</inf> = 30 GHz for pattern reconfiguration and splitting of incoming electromagnetic waves. The designed surface consists of three layers of swastika and cross slots printed on dielectric layers separated by air gaps to resonate at dual frequency bands. Such a dual-band surface can be utilized to generate or split an incoming wave into multiple beams, which is crucial for applications in MIMO systems. The simulated radiation patterns demonstrate dual-band beam splitting consistent with analytical calculations using the metasurface.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of Dissipative Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics without Markovian Approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We develop a numerical framework to analyze the dynamics of a dissipative cavity quantum electrodynamics without the Markovian approximation. For the correct quantization of electromagnetic fields in the presence of lossy dielectric objects in the free space, we employ the so-called BAMA formulation [1] which takes into account fluctuations to both radiation and medium losses. With the coarse-graining strategy, the BAMA fields (or modes) can be evaluated by using conventional computational electromagnetics numerical modes, e.g., FEM, FDTD, or MoM. We then incorporate the BAMA modes into the multimode Jaynes-Cummings model and solve the time-dependent Schrödinger equation to find probability amplitudes.

articleTitle: Characteristics Assessment of X-Band Wave Absorber Using Constitutive Material Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper assesses the characteristics of X-band wave absorber composed of square patch array using its constitutive material parameters. The characteristics of wave absorber, designed to operate at the X-band frequency range, is assessed through a single unit cell of square patch applying proper boundaries to profile an infinite square patch array. Three different widths of square patch unit cell are employed to generate the frequency responses of 9 GHz, 10 GHz, and 11 GHz. Through characteristics assessment, these correspond to the conductivity values of (0.006 – j4.21) × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>S/m, (0.13 – j2.81) × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> S/m, and (0.35 – j2.97) × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> S/m, respectively. It shows that the shift of frequency response is affected by the dimension of patch which can be assessed through its constitutive material parameters. In addition, an experimental verification is carried out by measuring the frequency response of an X-band wave absorber prototype.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Small Antenna for Wireless Power Transfer Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A method of non-interfering wireless testing was proposed for small power receiving antennas in miniature wireless power transfer-compatible IoT devices. The antenna patterns were measured with the proposed and traditional wired methods, demonstrating the importance of the former for efficient antenna design and optimization, and the drawbacks of the later when working with small antennas in practical configurations.

articleTitle: Estimation Formula of Line-of-Sight Probability Considering Road Length for an Urban Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses an estimation formula of line-of-sight (LOS) probability considering LOS road length for an urban environment. We developed an LOS estimation formula that adapts to changes of the LOS road length. As an urban environment model that probabilistically restricts sight-length, we proposed a restricted road-length model and clarify the effect of the LOS restriction on the LOS probability. On the basis of the results, the estimation formula of LOS probability for a uniform-grid-pattern city constructed in a previous study was modified to develop a new estimation formula suitable for an actual urban environment, taking into account the effect of the LOS restriction. As a result, we obtained an LOS probability estimation formula that is adaptable to changes of the LOS road length.

articleTitle: Design and Field Trial Measurement of 1-Bit Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) have been recognized as an important technology to overcome non-line-of-sight (NLOS) situations beyond 5G and 6G wireless communications. In this paper, we design a 1-bit RIS unit cell with low loss and wide phase shift bandwidth in the upper-mid band 8 GHz. Based on the designed unit cell, we fabricated 32 × 32 RIS. Measurements were taken to validate the performance of the proposed RIS in a non-light-of-sight environment.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Scattering Field Strength of Reflectarray Elements by Dielectric Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, it is demonstrated that scattering field strength of reflectarray elements can be enhanced by introducing a dielectric superstrate. Rigorous expressions of far field radiated from current source covered by the dielectric superstrate are derived and well-known resonance conditions are revisited for the reflectarray elements. Numerical simulation is performed and effect of dielectric superstrate on the scattering field strength of the reflectarray elements is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Toward Realization of RIS-assisted Wireless Information and Power Transfer System: Implementation and Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a series of studies on the implementation of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) in wireless communication and power transfer systems. The discussed studies put together comprehensive RIS-assisted systems covering RIS unit cell design, testbed setup, practical algorithms, and experimental validations. The results of these experiments highlight the significant enhancement that RIS can bring to wireless network performance.

articleTitle: Wideband RCS Reduction of Curved Surface Based on High-Frequency Approximation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A curve-loaded quarter cylinder model based on height fluctuation to realize multiple phase cancellation is proposed, which can be used to reduce the wideband radar cross section (RCS) of cylindrical objects. The continuous surface is defined by the multi-order Fourier function. MATLAB programming is used to calculate the RCS of the curve-loaded quarter cylinder model at a certain incident angle. Using particle swarm optimization (PSO) technology, taking Fourier function parameters of the surface as particles and RCS reduction as the optimization objective, the form of the surface is controlled and optimized to achieve broadband RCS reduction under normal incidence. The monostatic 10 dB RCS reduction can be achieved for the model in the range of 4 - 20 GHz (fractional bandwidth of more than 130%). The proposed design method and designed model have important applications in shaping technology to realize cylinder object’s electromagnetic stealth.

articleTitle: Real-Time Phased-Array Monitoring System for On-Site Calibration Using Beam-Steering Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel real-time phased array monitoring method is proposed for the on-site phased-array calibration during the mission operation. The proposed method can successively estimate the individual element fields and its variations during the beam-steering, with the aid of the Kalman filter. Numerical simulations have demonstrated that the proposed method can effectively estimate the element fields along with the beam steering.

articleTitle: A Study on Miniaturized Patch Antenna Array with Circular Polarization for Earth Sensing Platform via LEO Satellite
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, a satellite sensing platform that collects global sensor data using low earth orbit (LEO) satellites has been attracting attention. In this paper, we propose a L-probe-fed miniaturized patch antenna array with circular polarization that can operate at two frequency bands of 860 MHz and 920 MHz for satellite sensing platform via LEO satellite. Characteristics of the proposed antenna array are clarified by electromagnetic simulation based on the finite element method (FEM).

articleTitle: Link Characteristics between Base Stations and Drones in Mobile Communication Systems with Drone Relay Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Currently, mobile communication system using drones as relay stations has been investigated to further increase transmission speeds, increase system capacity, and expand service areas. However, its effects have not yet been fully clarified. In this paper, we clarify the link characteristics between base stations and drones in an urban macrocell environment from the relationship between drone altitude and base station antenna height.

articleTitle: A Study on a Low-Loss Connector for Converting a Dielectric Waveguide to a Rectangular Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The demand for high-speed and high-capacity communication and radar systems operating at frequencies above millimeter waves has increased. Dielectric waveguides have been studied as low-loss, flexible transmission lines, but loss occurs when converting them to coaxial connectors or rectangular waveguides. This paper presents a low-loss connector for converting between a dielectric waveguide and a rectangular waveguide at 28 GHz. The characteristics of the dielectric waveguide were measured at various lengths and compared with simulation results. The proposed connector achieved S21 of approximately -0.15 dB around 28 GHz, indicating its effectiveness in attaining low-loss conversion.

articleTitle: Physically Unclonable Functions Based on Scattering of Core-Shell Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, we study the sensitivity of Fano-type resonant scattering from a core-shell (plasmonic-dielectric) nanoparticle and its potential applications in optical encryption and hardware security. Specifically, we present the physical unclonable function (PUF) based on the scattering cross section (SCS) spectra of core-shell nanoparticles, of which the ultrahigh sensitivity near the Fano resonance makes their scattering properties highly sensitive to nanomanfacturing process variations. Such a property leads to a perfect entropy source for the generation of PUF-based cryptographic keys encoded in scattering responses. Our numerical and statistical results show that this optical PUF can exhibit excellent uniqueness and randomness for effective encryption.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Dual-Band Reflective Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-band reflective metasurface unit cell is presented based on the square split ring resonator (SSRR) with loaded capacitors at 8 and 10 GHz. By utilizing the loaded capacitor, the reflection phase of each resonator can be controlled. The initial loaded capacitor value is chosen to be 0.35 pF where the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> value achieves 0.956 at 8 GHz and 0.739 at 10 GHz, with the reflection phase being -13.478° at 8 GHz and -6.786° at 10 GHz. The reflection phase reaches -58.9° at 8 GHz and -161.065° at 10 GHz if the loaded capacitor values change from 0.2 pF to 2 pF.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Dual Circularly Polarized Large Element Spacing Phased Array Antenna with Grating Lobe Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave 4×4-element phased array antenna (PAA) with dual circular polarization (CP), employing λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> element spacing for limited field of view (FoV) scanning. The circular polarization is achieved through the integration of a 90° hybrid coupler into multi-layer printed circuit boards (PCBs). Moreover, a corrugated lens, affixed to the PCBs via a metal block, shapes the radiation pattern to produce a flat-top active element pattern (AEP), effectively suppressing grating lobes during beam scanning. The designed array achieves a boresight gain of over 19 dBic across a scanning range of ±15°, demonstrating a gain variation of 0.5 dB and maintaining a -10 dB grating lobe level within the 26–28 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: Integrated Sensing and Communications Signal SINR Prediction with Multi-Beam Statistical Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The development of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) brings new challenges to network optimization. This is not only due to the unpredictable relationship between ISAC network performance and network parameters but also the lack of well-suited ISAC channel models for ISAC network optimization. We propose a framework of multi-beam statistical channel modeling aided ISAC signal signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratios (SINR) prediction, utilizing channel angular power spectrum to accurately characterize both echo signal and communication signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio after antenna parameter adjustment. Utilizing real-world driving test data for multi-path channel estimation, this framework accurately characterizes the stochastic sensing channels and provides effective prediction strategies for antenna parameter adjustments. Simulation results demonstrate that our approach outperforms the conventional method with a single-beam path loss model.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing of Ceramics for Permittivity Optimization in Dielectric Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work focuses on the realization of ceramic dielectric resonators with porous and complex geometry using additive manufacturing to control their effective permittivity. Several cylindrical alumina and zirconia samples integrating different volume fractions of air inclusions were developed and characterized. By incorporating up to 95.5 vol% of inclusions, we reduced the effective permittivity from 9.4 to 1.3 for alumina and from 32.7 to 7.8 for zirconia. The effectiveness of these samples in antenna applications was also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Study of the new MACKEY III with one-layered structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Based on metamaterial technology, which realizes unique electrical characteristics through periodic microstructures, we proposed MACKEY, a compact and thin antenna that can operate on metal. Conventional MACKEYs have a two-layer substrate in which the radiating element and the power-feeding element are placed in different layers. In this study, we propose MACKEYIII, which has a simpler structure and lower cost than conventional MACKEYs by placing the radiating element and the power-feeding element on the same layer to make it a one-layer substrate.

articleTitle: Glass-printed Uniplanar Magnetic Dipole Array Antennas for Omni-directional Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a planar magnetic array antenna designed for Sub6 GHz applications, addressing the limitations of traditional electrical dipole antennas on glass substrates. The antenna, fabricated on a quartz substrate, forms a magnetic dipole through small loops arranged in a 120° array, achieving a substrate-parallel omnidirectional pattern without vias. The proposed antenna shows 10 dB matching bandwidth from 5.5 GHz to 6 GHz with 3.69 dB realized gain and omnidirectional radiation at 5.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Passive RFID Tag Antenna on Kapton Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The main goal in the RFID tag antenna design is to reduce the antenna size while maintaining the gain high as possible. In this paper, we propose a design of UHF RFID tag meander dipole antenna on Kapton, the antenna resonates at 921 MHz – the mid-frequency of the Malaysian band for UHF RFID. The antenna was matched to NXP UCODE G2iL chip. The antenna was designed and optimized using CST software. The overall antenna dimensions were 85.93 x 19.7 mm, and the maximum gain achieved was 1.92 dBi, and the antenna is linearly polarized. The maximum theoretical read range can be achieved in free space by a circularly polarized 4 watts EIRP reader was estimated to be 11.5 meters.

articleTitle: Parity-Time Symmetry in Wireless Transfer of Power and Information
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: After the concept of parity-time (PT) symmetry was first proposed in quantum physics about a decade ago, it is actively being applied to diverse fields of physics. This work introduces how the PT symmetry is applied to the wireless delivery of power and information. We first show that multiple coils obeying the PT symmetry can enlarge the operational area of wireless powering. In contrast to the conventional Multiple-Input-Single-Output (MISO) scheme, the proposed system does not require a linear power amplifier and a phase shifter for each coil, thus greatly saves the system cost. Secondly, we demonstrate that simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) in PT symmetry can achieve high power transfer efficiency and a high signal-to-noise (SNR) ratio at the same time, which was impossible for a conventional SWIPT method, the load modulation.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: Broadband Circularly Polarized Antenna Arrays with Anisotropic Artificial Gradient Dielectric Slabs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents broadband circularly polarized antenna arrays operating from 6 to 18 GHz utilizing anisotropic artificial gradient dielectric slabs. The proposed antenna consists of three anisotropic slabs with different impedances, stacked above a 45° slant linearly polarized bow-tie slot antenna. The gradient slabs feature distinct impedance distributions in the x- and y- directions based on a linear distribution to achieve broadband impedance matching and circular polarization characteristics. The proposed antenna exhibits a 10-dB matching bandwidth from 6 to 17.6 GHz and an average axial ratio of 3.39 dB across the operating frequency.

articleTitle: Switchable Circularly Polarized GPS Antenna Based on PIN Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the development of microstrip patch antenna with the capability to switch its polarization by utilizing PIN diodes. The proposed antenna is designed a a Rogers RT/duroid 5880 substrate to operate at the frequency of 1.575 GHz for Global Positioning System (GPS) application. To attain a circular polarization, a diagonal slot is incorporated at the center of patch. Whilst to gain a switchable polarization, BAR64-02V type PIN diodes are utilized upon the diagonal slot. Simulation and measurement are conducted to characterize and verify the capability of proposed antenna to produce and switch circular polarization.

articleTitle: An Integrated High-Performance RFID Timing System for Marathon Events
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper demonstrates an optimized RFID timing system for outdoor mass sporting events through integrated antenna, reader, and embedded innovations overcoming conventional product limitations. Key outcomes include a high-performance prototype and bolstering the industry RFID expertise for product commercialization.

articleTitle: Spaceborne SAR Antenna Development Status and Plans Suitable for Tip and Cue Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The concept of tip and cue monitoring is to find the location of a suspicious object using a wide-area observation sensor and then take a closer look using a high-resolution satellite sensor. Efficient surveillance can be achieved through a constellation that combines a large SAR satellite based on active phased array antenna and SAR satellites equipped with light weight reflectors. We present the development status and future development plans of spaceborne SAR antennas suitable for tip and cue monitoring.

articleTitle: Accuracy Improvement of Magnetic Field Measurement in WPT Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present an electromagnetic field visualization system that integrates magnetic field measurement with augmented reality (AR) technology. A key aspect of this system is accurately converting the voltage measured by a shielded loop probe into magnetic field strength using a conversion coefficient derived from Faraday's law. Traditionally, this conversion requires frequent calibration due to inhomogeneous magnetic fields and probe dimensions. In this study, we validate that by designing a probe with sufficiently small electrical dimensions—a radius of approximately 9.7 mm at 13.56 MHz—the magnetic field within the probe area can be considered homogeneous. This allows for the direct application of the theoretical conversion coefficient without the need for calibration. Through full-wave simulations and experimental measurements using a two-loop coil as the device under test (DUT), we demonstrate that the theoretical C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">VH</inf> remains consistent in regions where the magnetic field is homogeneous. Our results confirm the validity of the proposed equation and enhance the practicality of electromagnetic field visualization systems.

articleTitle: Plane Wave Characteristics of a Dielectric Lens Antenna with Serrated Structure for CATR Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Beyond 5G/6G, large aperture antennas are used to compensate for the high propagation loss in the millimeter wave band. The large anechoic chambers required to accommodate DFF (Direct Far Field) measurements can be prohibitively large and expensive. Establishing anechoic chambers and test ranges large enough to accommodate DFF measurements has proven difficult and costly. More recently, however, the characterization of large aperture millimeter-wave antennas and transceivers can be more economically performed utilizing Compact Antenna Test Range (CATR) systems. Unlike traditional large anechoic chamber-based systems that utilize Direct Far Field (DFF) techniques, CATR systems incorporate Indirect Far-Field (IFF) techniques with reflectors to achieve comparable measurements using less space. This translates into smaller and less expensive test systems. However, conventional reflectors used in millimeter-wave CATR chambers can be expensive to manufacture and set up. This paper presents a more economical dielectric lens that utilizes a serrated structure (SS) around the dielectric lens to achieve suitable plane-wave characteristics.

articleTitle: Effect of the transmitter antenna radiation pattern on propagation of millimeter wave band in urban street cell environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Effect of the transmitter antenna radiation pattern on the propagation delay and the angle of arrival characteristics in the millimeter-wave band is examined based on measured data using a 67-GHz channel sounder. The results show that the transmitter antenna radiation pattern has a significant effect on both the propagation delay and angle of arrival characteristics.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable mmWave Planar Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact, low-profile, and pattern-reconfigurable millimeter-wave V2X antenna array. Its hybrid design, coupled with beam-scanning capabilities, facilitates extensive spatial coverage within the n257 band. By employing PIN diode-controlled strips, the antenna array achieves vertical beam tilting of up to ±40° on a vehicle with minimal gain deviation of under 1 dB. Moreover, the subarray can scan the beam within an angle of ±32° while maintaining a gain exceeding 8 dBi. The overall circular antenna array, inclusive of director and reflector elements positioned adjacent to the antenna with an added substrate, boasts dimensions of 74.2mm×74.2mm×2.2mm, underscoring its compactness. Fabrication of the antenna array is carried out, and measurements encompassing beam scanning, S-parameters, and communication are conducted to confirm the simulated findings.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Metamaterial Absorber Using a Slotted Octagonal Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative electromagnetic metamaterial absorber (MMA) distinguished by its low-profile, polarization insensitivity (PI), and capability to function across multiple frequency ranges. The MMA unit cell comprises a slotted octagonal metallic patch fabricated on an FR4 dielectric substrate, with a grounded metallic layer at the back, and notably lacks resistive lumped components. Experimental findings illustrate that the proposed MMA achieves absorption levels surpassing 75% for normal incidence over diverse frequency bands, ranging from 2.22 to 2.38 GHz, 6.86 to 7.24 GHz, 11.68 to 12.71 GHz, 14.1 to 14.8 GHz, and 15.47 to 16 GHz.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of the MACKEY C-type by calculation and measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The aim of the study is to further miniaturise the MAKCEYII. In order to lower the resonance frequency, we focused on increasing the capacitance of the antenna. Two capacitance elements were mounted on the antenna substrate of the MACKEY II. The anntena’s capacitance has successfully reduced the resonant frequency by increasing the antenna's capacitance, result in reducing the anntena side. In this paper, the performance of the anntena is evaluated by comparing the analysed and measured values.

articleTitle: Analytic Integration Approach for Precise Calculation of MoM Matrix Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To solve electromagnetic scattering and radiation problems using the Rao-Wilton-Glisson(RWG) basis function, double surface integrals over triangular domains are computed. When the distance between the source point and the observation point is large, these surface integrals are computed using numerical integration methods that offer high computational accuracy and convenience. However, when the distance between the source point and the observation point is small, the 1/R and 1/R <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> components within the surface integral become singular, leading to reduced accuracy when computed using numerical integration alone. Therefore, alternative approaches are required to achieve high computational accuracy when the distance between the source point and the observation point is small. In this paper, we introduce a method for handling singular integrals and provide results from applying this method to example to demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Bistatic Microwave Imaging with Different Transmission Positions Using Multiband Sensors for Breast Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Microwave imaging is a promising technique for detecting breast tumors, offering an alternative to conventional medical imaging modalities. This study investigates the use of a bistatic microwave imaging system with multiband sensors and different transmission positions to improve the detection of breast cancer. A homogeneous breast phantom model was developed to simulate the dielectric properties of biological breast tissues, including the skin, fat, and tumor. The study evaluated the performance of the system under two antenna transmission conditions - horizontal (azimuth angle) and vertical (polar angle) positions. Simulation results show that the transmission coefficient (S21) can effectively detect tumors as small as 4 mm in size using both horizontal and vertical transmission positions.
